# The Input (LF): The Large-Field Ingredients of the Young Matched Pairs

{#P.1} This note proves the input (LF) of `WILSON_IT1_CAUCHY_ESTIMATE_2026_10_27.md` (its (LF) line, §6.2, and §8.6). Bałaban is cited by printed page and equation, checked on the transcriptions in `Balaban\tex\<paper>\parts`.
{#P.1-1} The notation is the Cauchy note's: {#D.δ_j} δ_j := (g^B_j)^{−2} − (g^A_j)^{−2} is the two runs' coupling difference at the shared scale j, with g^B_j, here and throughout this note, run B's coupling at the shared scale j, its own scale j + 1, so that δ_j is the Cauchy note's (g^B_{j+1})^{−2} − (g^A_j)^{−2} (#C1.1-4), {#D.ϑ_j} ϑ_j := g_j(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j) is Bałaban's δ_j (CRE p.265 l.39), and δ′_j = g_jA₁p₁(g_j) is his (LFR I p.183 l.2).
{#P.1-2} Lines and paragraphs carry tags in braces, cited without the braces as #tag (a paragraph of a long item carries the item's tag followed by its number, as #A.11.25); LABELS_LF_AND_TABLE.md lists every tag with its current line.
{#P.2} A line continues on the following lines tagged with its tag and a number, as #4.9-1; a citation #tag covers the line with its continuations, and #tag-q cites one continuation. This note numbers only §§1–5, so a bare section number §6–§11 (as §8.4 or §9.8) is the Cauchy note's, unless the line names another note.

## 1. The Structure of a Young History {#S1}

{#1.1} Let X be an alive component of a young matched pair, and j₀ > k − ⌊k/2⌋ the pair's birth scale, that of its oldest alive component (the Cauchy note's #CP.2), so that X is born at a scale ≥ j₀ and Ω_i = T for i < j₀ (the Cauchy note's #C6.2.1-7).

- {#1.2} *The integration variables.* By CRE (2.20)–(2.21) (p.258 l.14–31), the operation 𝐓^{(j)} integrates V_j on Ω^c_{j+1} ∩ X with the constraint δ(V̄_jV^{−1}_{j+1}). On the part of X in Ω^c_{j₀}, which lies in every Ω^c_{j+1} with j ≥ j₀ − 1 since Ω₁ ⊃ Ω₂ ⊃ … ⊃ Ω_k (CRE p.254 l.47), the variables V_{j₀}, …, V_{k−1} on the bonds whose blocks lie in Ω^c_{j₀} are fixed by the constraints as iterated block averages of V_{j₀−1}; on a block that meets Ω_{j₀}, V_j is in part a variable of Ω_{j₀} ∖ Ω_{j+1}.
  {#1.2-1} So on the part of X in Ω^c_{j₀} the operations 𝐓^{(j)}, j ≥ j₀ − 1, integrate V_{j₀−1}, with the Haar measure and the constraints; their fluctuation variables A_j, on Z_{j+1} ∩ Ω_{j+1} ∩ X, lie in Ω_{j+1} ⊂ Ω_{j₀}. The factors are ζ(Ω^c_{j+1}) and χ of (2.21). (2.21) is printed for a 𝐓^{(j)} not changed by an 𝐑-operation; one changed by it keeps the general form, with other characteristic functions (p.258 l.22–23, l.34–36).
- {#1.3} *The regularity of the data.* The point lies in Ω_{j₀−1} ∖ Ω_{j₀}, so the determining set carries the layer Λ_{j₀−1} there, with data V_{j₀−1}. VAR's hypothesis (7) (p.278 l.35–45) is one bound ε₁ on the data plaquettes of all layers, the mixed plaquettes at a layer's boundary included. It holds on the support of the term with the parameter C max_j(ε_j + ϑ_j), from the seven groups of LFR I p.178, as follows, and so with ε₁ of #1.6-1.
  - {#1.4} The cubes of (1.3) at the scale j, □ ⊂ (Ω_j^{∼4} ∖ Ω_{j+1}^∼) ∩ Z (LFR I p.178 l.16–19), bound the plaquettes of U_{j,□}(V_j) by ε_j(L^{k−j}η)². With Ω_{j₀−1} = T they cover the large-field region of the scale j₀ outside the collar Ω_{j₀}^∼ ∖ Ω_{j₀} (Ω^∼ is the enlargement, CRE p.250 l.26). The data of U_{j,□} are V_j, so CMP 98 Proposition 2 (p.26, (54)), which needs only the local plaquette bound (52), gives |V_j(∂p′) − 1| < 2ε_j there. This is the remark of VAR p.278 l.46. The group (1.4) gives the same at the scale j + 1.
  - {#1.5} In the collars, (1.7) and (1.8) put V_j, and the lifted fluctuation field, within 2ϑ_j of the reference configuration V^{(j)}_{□′}. This is the scale-j average of a minimiser corrected by exp i𝐇^{(j)}_{□′} (LFR I p.185 l.29), so its plaquettes are bounded by the item above, and those of V_j by that bound plus Cϑ_j.
  - {#1.6} By CRE (2.4) and (2.6) and ϑ_j = g_j(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j) (CRE p.265 l.39), C max_j(ε_j + ϑ_j) ≤ Cḡp₀(ḡ), a bound independent of k, K, and ε.
  - {#1.6-1} The notes' data parameter is {#D.ε₁} ε₁ := max(C max_j(ε_j + ϑ_j), C(M)R_kε_k), its first entry that of #1.3, its second that of (1.3) and U_0 in §4(c) (#4.43-1), with C(M) of #4.43-1.2, R_k = R̄(K − k) (#4.50-1.1.1), and every ε_j, ϑ_j, R_k, and ε_k, here and in every bound by them, the larger of its two runs' values, so that ε₁ bounds both runs' data parameters. VAR (7) at the first entry gives (7) at ε₁ ≤ a₁ (#T3.19-1).
  - {#1.6-2} By #1.6 and #4.50-1.1.1-1, with g_k ≤ (1 + β₀)γ (#4.50-1.1.1-1) and g ↦ g(log g^{−2})^{p₀+r} increasing on (0, e^{−(p₀+r)}), which contains (1 + β₀)γ for γ small, ε₁ ≤ {#D.ε̄₁} ε̄₁ := max(Cḡp₀(ḡ), C(M)2^{2r+1}LA₀(1 + β₀)γ(log((1 + β₀)γ)^{−2})^{p₀+r}), independent of k, K, and ε, and ε̄₁ ≤ a₁ for ḡ and γ small depending on M.
  - {#1.6-3} Against ε_k: ε_j ≤ (1 + β₀)ε_k at j ≤ k (#4.54-0), and ε_j ≤ (1 + β₀)²(j − k)^{1/2}ε_k at k < j ≤ k_s, by g_j ≤ (1 + β₀)(j − k)^{1/2}g_k (CRE (2.6)) and (log g_j^{−2})^{p₀} ≤ (1 + β₀)(log g_k^{−2})^{p₀} (CRE (2.7), p.255 l.55). So the first entry of ε₁ is ≤ C(1 + β₀)²(1 + A₁/A₀)max(1, k_s − k + 1)^{1/2}ε_k, and, with C(M) ≥ (1 + β₀)(1 + A₁/A₀)C and R_k ≥ 1 (#4.43-1.2), ε₁/ε_k ≤ (1 + β₀)C(M)R_kmax(1, k_s − k + 1)^{1/2}.
- {#1.7} *The configurations.* The fine configuration of the term is a minimiser with these data: U_k(V) for the action (CRE p.258 l.44–47), and U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(·) for the 𝐑-operation (LFR II (1.50), p.370 l.4). VAR Theorem 1 (p.279 l.8–28) treats determining sets 𝔅_k = ∪_jΛ_j, layer by layer. Its hypothesis (7) holds with ε₁ (#1.6-1). So the regularity (9)–(10), |A| < B₃Mε₁(L^jη)^{−1} and its companions, holds on every cube of VAR's class at the spacing L^jη of its layer (p.279 l.17–27), and every layer of X lies at a scale ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k/2 − 1.

{#1.8} The coarse block averages of V_{j₀−1} are not regular at the coarse scales, and the fine configuration depends on them only through the layers. This is why the depth of the young pairs is first order in the ratio of the fine spacing to the layer's spacing, L^{−(j₀−1)}: the same order as for the all-small-field pair at the scale j₀ − 1.

## 2. The Run-Dependent Ingredients, Sorted {#S2}

{#2.1} The ingredients of a young term at the scales i ≥ j₀ are listed in the Cauchy note's §6.2. The selectors are the seven groups of LFR I p.178 l.15–49 and the test (2.17).

{#2.2} (a) *The ingredients of (α).* The small-field action, the covariance, and the function (1.6) are derived in the Cauchy note's §6.2.

{#2.3} (b) *The coupling shells: (1.5) and (1.9).*
- {#2.4} (1.5), χ(|V_j(y,x) − 1| < ε_j), acts on the variable V_j(y,x) of the lattice T_{L^{−j}}, which both runs share. The threshold ε_j = g_jp₀(g_j) depends on the run only through the coupling.
- {#2.5} (1.9), χ(sup|A_j(b)| < g_j^{−1}ϑ_j), acts on the fluctuation variable. Its threshold also depends on the run only through the coupling.
- {#2.6} Bałaban's bounds are stated at one run's thresholds, so the split keeps each piece on one run's own support. With Π_X the product of run X's indicators and ρ_X the rest of its integrand,
  {#2.7} Π_Aρ_A − Π_Bρ_B = Π_AΠ_B(ρ_A − ρ_B) + Π_A(1 − Π_B)ρ_A − Π_B(1 − Π_A)ρ_B.
  {#2.8} The first piece lies on the common support and belongs to (α) (#2.2) and to (LF-A) (#2.18). In the second, 1 − Π_B ≤ Σ_b(1 − χ_{B,b}), and on the support of Π_A the factor 1 − χ_{B,b} is the indicator of the shell between the two thresholds at b. The third piece is the same with A and B exchanged.
- {#2.9} So each shell term is run A's own term (or run B's) with one shell indicator inserted. Bałaban's bound (1.79) of 𝐓′1 is proved by estimating the group-valued integrals, with their normalised weights (1.6), by 1, and the A_j-integrals by the positivity of their quadratic forms (LFR II p.383 l.30–34). The shell indicator is ≤ 1 and is kept inside the corresponding integral, so the shell term is at most Bałaban's bound times the mass of the shell under that normalised weight.
- {#2.10} That mass is ≤ C|t′ − t|t′^{d_G−1} times the maximal density on the shell, in the variable X = g_j^{−1}log V_j(y,x) for (1.5) and A_j(b) for (1.9). The thresholds are t = ε_j/g_j = p₀(g_j) and t = g_j^{−1}ϑ_j = (A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j), and |t′ − t| ≤ Ct|g_j − g′_j|/g_j ≤ Ctg_j²|x_j − x′_j|, with {#D.x_j} x_j := g_j^{−2} and the primes for the other run: |dt/dg| = 2p₀t/(g log g^{−2}) ≤ Ct/g for both thresholds, and |dg/dx| = ½g³ for x = g^{−2}, on the segment between x_j and x′_j, where ½x_j ≤ x ≤ (3/2)x_j by |δ_j| ≤ ½x_j (the Cauchy note's #C5.7-4–#C5.7-8).
  - {#2.11} For (1.5), the density of the normalised weight (1.6) in X is ≤ C, uniformly in g_j small, since z ≥ cg_j^{d_G}. On the shell it is ≤ Ce^{−cp₀(g_j)²}, since 1 − Re tr V ≥ c|log V|² near 1.
  - {#2.12} For (1.9), the A_j-Gaussian has the precision Q = C*Δ^{(j)}C − C*Δ^{(j)}CC^{(j)}C*Δ^{(j)}C of CRE (2.21), and Q ≤ C*Δ^{(j)}C since C^{(j)} ≥ 0. The marginal variance of A_j(b) is ((Q^{−1})_{bb}) ≥ (Q_{bb})^{−1} ≥ ‖C*Δ^{(j)}C‖^{−1}, so the marginal density is ≤ (‖C*Δ^{(j)}C‖/2π)^{d_G/2}, a lattice constant. No Gaussian tail is used.
  - {#2.13} So the per-variable relative shell factor is ≤ Cp₀(g_j)^{d_G}g_j²|x_j − x′_j|. The variables are counted per point of the history as the variables of (1.6) are in (α) (Cauchy note §6.2).
- {#2.14} The complement χ^{(j−1)c}(R_j) of LFR II p.380 l.43–46 has the shell of (1.9), since the difference of 1 − χ is minus that of χ. Bałaban bounds its integral by the same positivity of the quadratic form (p.380 l.42, l.47), so the same bound holds.
- {#2.15} Of the radial cutoffs of the 𝐑-operation, the numerators' factor χ̄(Λ)(V′_k) has its shell bounded at #4.161. The denominator's χ({|B′| < M₀g_k^{−1}ε_k}) of LFR II (1.2) is the soft test χ̄(Λ) of LFR I (1.101) (#3.22), and its shell is bounded per bond by the Lipschitz bound of χ̄ (the Cauchy note's #C8.6.7–#C8.6.7-4). The numerators' χ′ (|B| < g_k^{−1}δ′_k) of (1.70) is LFR I's sharp (1.82), and its shell is bounded by the density device of #2.10–#2.12 (#C8.6.9-2–#C8.6.9-6).
- {#2.16} The bound is relative to Bałaban's bound of the term, not to the term itself. So for these shell terms the majorant in the Cauchy note's (LF) (its #CP.2) is Bałaban's bound (1.79) of sup𝐓′1, which is the bound that its #C11c.1–#C11c.7-4 use.

{#2.17} (c) *The plaquette shells: (1.3), (1.4), (1.7), (1.8), and (2.17).* These test U_{j,□}(V_j), U_{j+1,□′}(V_{j+1}), or the reference configurations V^{(j)}_{□′} built from them. All are minimisers computed on the run's fine lattice. At equal data the two runs' tested quantities differ by δ^f_jt with {#D.δ^f_j.2} δ^f_j := C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀}, by the minimiser distance of the Cauchy note's §9.7 applied to the local problem of the cube (VAR Theorem 1 for 𝐁_j(□^{∼4}), as in the Cauchy note's §9.8). Their thresholds, ε_j = g_jp₀(g_j) and 2ϑ_j = 2g_j(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j), differ through the coupling by ≤ Ctg_j²|δ_j|, as in #2.10. This is (LF-P), §3.

{#2.18} (d) *The large-field integrands.* These are (LF-A), §4.

## 3. The Plaquette Shells {#S3}

{#3.1} (a) *The redundant tests.*
- {#3.2} CRE (3.6)–(3.8) (p.265 l.46–47, p.266 l.26–33): for a cube □ ⊂ Ω^∼_{k+1} of the scale-k test (2.17), on the support of the next scale's small-field test (3.2) and of the Q-test (3.3), |U_{k,□}(∂p) − 1| < (2(1 + β₀)L^{−2} + 4/10)ε_kη² < ε_kη², "Thus χ_k(□) = 1 for □ ⊂ Ω^∼_{k+1}". (3.9) gives the same for the axial-gauge functions χ_{Ax}.
- {#3.3} CRE p.268 l.26–30 with (3.19) and p.269 l.2–4: for □′ ⊂ R^c_{k+1}, the complement taken in Ω^{∼−1}_{k+1}, the Q-test of (3.3) is equal to 1 on the support of the fluctuation cutoff (3.16).
- {#3.4} So in each run's term the tests of the scale j that are not equal to 1 on the support of the term's other characteristic functions lie as follows.
  {#3.4-1} The plaquette and axial tests lie on cubes not contained in Ω^∼_{j+1}, in the large-field region Ω^c_{j+1} of the next scale. The reference tests lie on cubes of the collar Ω^{∼2}_{j+1} ∖ Ω_{j+1} (LFR I (1.7)) and of S_{j+1} = (Ω_{j+1} ∖ Ω^{∼−1}_{j+1}) ∪ R_{j+1} (CRE (3.20)–(3.21), p.269 l.7–21), and, in LFR I, of (Ω_{j+1} ∖ Λ^∼_{j+1}) ∩ Z (LFR I (1.8)). All of these lie in the large-field region of the term or its collar. The tests of the stopping scale act on every cube of Ω_k. Where a test is equal to 1 in both runs there is no shell.
- {#3.5} The consequences are three.
  - {#3.6} The all-small-field term ℓ₀ carries the stopping-scale test χ_k(T) of (2.18) and the fluctuation cutoffs (3.16), whose shells the Cauchy note's #C8.2.1-15 bounds, and no other test.
  - {#3.7} In a young history Ω_{i+1} = T for i + 1 < j₀, so every test that is not equal to 1 on the support of the other characteristic functions is at a scale ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k/2 − 1 on a cube of the history, or on a stopping-scale cube of Ω_k. So δ^f_j ≤ CL^{−(1−2ε₀)(k/2−1)}, and the history cubes are counted by the history volume, with no volume factor.
  - {#3.8} The tests at the fine scales occur only in the old histories, whose terms the Cauchy note's #C6.2.2-1 measures against each run's own Z_{ℓ₀}, with no comparison of tests.

{#3.9} (b) *The stopping-scale test of the all-small-field term.*
- {#3.10} *The shell.* ρ^X_{ℓ₀}(V) = χ^X_k(T)(V)exp A^X_k(V) on G^{bonds(T^{(k)})}, X = A, B, with χ^X_k(T) the product (2.17) over the stopping-scale cubes, at most N_s⁴ of them, built on run X's fine lattice.
  {#3.10-1} Write {#D.f^X_□} f^X_□ := sup_{p⊂□^∼}|U^X_{k,□}(V, ∂p) − 1|/(η^X)² and {#D.t^X} t^X := ε^X_k. On either run's support, |f^A_□ − f^B_□| ≤ δ^ft^A with {#D.δ^f} δ^f := C(ε/a)^{1−2ε₀} (#2.17), and |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_a²|δ_k| (#2.10).
  {#3.10-2} With {#D.δ^s} δ^s := 2δ^f + 4Cg_a²|δ_k|, which is δ^s_k of #3.32 and exceeds the width δ^f + Cg_a²|δ_k| that this split needs, the split #2.7 puts the shell on one run's own support: run A's term with the indicator of {t(1 − δ^s) ≤ f^A_□ < t}, {#D.t.2} t := t^A, inserted for one cube □, and the same with A and B exchanged.
- {#3.12} *The bound.* The soft tests bound this shell (#3.41–#3.42).

{#3.13} (c) *The young pairs.*
- {#3.14} *The form needed.* A bound of each shell term's mass by C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} times Bałaban's bound of the term, plus a coupling part ≤ |δ_j|, has per cube of the history the form (LF) asks for: s^{LF}_j ≤ C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} ≤ C_hθ̃^j, since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−2ε₀)}, with the coupling part inside s′_K. The soft tests give it (#3.37–#3.40-1).

{#3.16} (d) *The soft tests.*
- {#3.17} *The device.* F_K = N_K/(κ_KZ_K) (the Cauchy note's §1), with N_K and Z_K the lattice integrals, which do not depend on the decompositions of unity used to expand them. At every K and in both runs, each plaquette and reference test χ({f_□ < t}) is replaced by the soft test χ̄(f_□/t), {#D.χ̄(x)} χ̄(x) := min(1, max(0, (1 + κ_s − x)/κ_s)), and its complement by 1 − χ̄(f_□/t).
  - {#3.18} These are the tests of CRE (1.1), (1.4), (1.8), (2.17), (3.2), and (3.3); of LFR I (1.3)–(1.4), (1.7)–(1.8), (1.22)–(1.24), (1.27), (1.75), and (1.88); and their restatements in LFR II (1.70) and p.380 l.31–41 (l.43–46 is the sharp χ^{(j−1)c}(R_j) of #2.14).
  - {#3.19} *The cascade tests.* The tests χ_k^{(n)} of LFR I (1.22)–(1.24) are soft at nested thresholds. There n = j − h counts the integrations, n = 0, …, N with {#D.N} N := k − h, and U^{(N)}_{k,Z} = U″_{k,Z} (p.181 l.4, p.182 l.35).
    {#3.19.1} At a cube □, {#D.f^(n)_□} f^{(n)}_□ := sup|U^{(n)}_{k,Z}(∂p) − 1|/T_n(p) over the tested plaquettes p assigned to □ (#3.19.1-1), on the layers of (1.16) (#3.26-1), with T_n(p) the threshold of (1.24) at p. For j ≤ k₀, p.181 l.40–42 names but does not print the generalisations of (1.22) and (1.23), so the note defines χ_k^{(n)} there by (1.24)'s thresholds with no power of L₀ and c = 1 (j < k).
    {#3.19.1-0} These have (1.22)'s and (1.23)'s coefficients, 1 − β(1 − 2^{−(j−i+1)}) at the layers i < j and 1 − β/2 at the layer j, each times ε_i(L^{k−i}η)². (1.24)'s powers of L₀ are those of the overlapping regions (p.181 l.42–44), and for j ≤ k₀ the regions are disjoint (l.41). The note's account of (1.46)–(1.52) (#3.68–#3.68-1) carries the power of L₀ as a factor that is 1 at the layers i ≤ k₀ + 1, so it covers these thresholds.
      {#3.19.1-1} Each p is assigned to an LM₂R_i-cube containing it, i the scale of T_n(p), as in (1.88), the first in a fixed order of the cubes where p lies in several; any assignment gives the same sharp test. χ_k^{(n)} is replaced by ∏_□χ̄_c(f^{(n)}_□/(1 + κ_c)^{N−n}), with χ̄_c the function χ̄ with {#D.κ_c} κ_c := κ_s/(N + 1) in place of κ_s.
    - {#3.19-1} So the test n has the plateau f^{(n)}_□ ≤ (1 + κ_c)^{N−n} and the support f^{(n)}_□ < (1 + κ_c)^{N−n+1}, and every cascade threshold lies between T_n and (1 + κ_c)^{N+1}T_n ≤ e^{κ_s}T_n ≤ (1 + 2κ_s)T_n. The test n = N, at j = k, has the plateau T_N and the width κ_c, and it keeps this form wherever it occurs again.
  - {#3.20} A test keeps its soft form wherever it occurs again: as the stopping test of the next step, in a product of tests, and after a change of variables, as in LFR I (1.59). Where tests on overlapping cube sets are combined, as χ_k(X_i^{∼−6}) with χ_k(Ω_k^{∼4}) (LFR II p.378 l.15–16), the soft product keeps both factors, χ̄² on the overlap, with values in [0, 1] and the support of χ̄; no identity χ̄² = χ̄ is used, and each factor counts as one test in #3.34.
  - {#3.21} The radial cutoffs other than χ(Λ_i) of #3.22, and the fluctuation and gauge-fixing cutoffs, stay sharp: CRE (1.5), (1.18), and (3.16); LFR I (1.5), (1.9), (1.55), and (1.82), with (1.5) the restatement of CRE (1.5); and χ′ of LFR II (1.70), which is LFR I's (1.82) (LFR II p.381 l.33).
  - {#3.22} The radial cutoff χ(Λ_i) of the 𝐑-operation, LFR I (1.101), is soft, as defined at (1.100)–(1.102) (#3.80), and it is the same soft function in LFR II (1.1), (1.2), and (1.70) (p.356 l.19–37, p.378 l.13–14). Its shells are bounded per bond by the Lipschitz bound of χ̄: the shell of χ̄(Λ)(V′_k) in §4(d), and the denominator's in the Cauchy note's §8.6.
  - {#3.23} Every decomposition stays exact, since Σ_P∏_{□∉P}χ̄_□∏_{□∈P}(1 − χ̄_□) = ∏_□(χ̄_□ + 1 − χ̄_□) = 1 for any functions with values in [0, 1]. So N_K and Z_K are unchanged, and F_K is defined at every K by this one construction, both as run A of one pair and as run B of the next.
  - {#3.24} {#D.κ_s.2} κ_s := β/30 = 1/240, with β = 1/8 (§4(d), *The choice β = 1/8, checked.*), within Bałaban's β ≤ 1/4 of LFR I p.191 l.34–35 and p.198 l.16 (the choice of β below (1.24) allows β ≤ ½, p.182 l.17–18). A passed test of width κ_s enters at the threshold (1 + κ_s)t, and a passed cascade test at a threshold ≤ (1 + 2κ_s)t. The checks #3.48–#3.99-1 are written with 1 + κ_s and hold with 1 + 2κ_s in its place.
    - {#3.24-1} The smallest relative margin of the passed-test comparisons is that of LFR I (1.31) (p.184 l.8–9), β/10 − β/(5L²) ≥ 7β/90 at L ≥ 3, and (1 + β/15)(1 − 7β/90) < 1. The other margins absorb the factor 1 + 2κ_s = 1 + 1/120, as checked at each line (#3.48–#3.99-1).

The letter κ without the index is Bałaban's decay constant, as in exp(−κd_j(X)).
- {#3.25} *The shell bound.* For a test at □ of the scale j, put {#D.x^X} x^X := f^X_□/t^X in run X.
  - {#3.26} The thresholds differ by |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_j²|δ_j| ≤ ½t^A, with j the scale of the threshold (§2(b)). For the tests of local minimisers, §2(c)'s and their restatements, the tested quantities differ by |f^A − f^B| ≤ δ^f_jt^A on either run's support, with δ^f_j = C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} of §2(c) (#2.17), its C taken for data regular at the thresholds (1 + 2κ_s)t of the support. The tests of multiscale minimisers, (1.27), the cascade tests (1.22)–(1.24), and (1.75), are bounded in the same form in #3.26-1–#3.31.
    {#3.26-1} *The cascade tests.* U^{(n)}_{k,Z} = U(𝐁^{(n)}_k(Z), ·) (LFR I (1.18)–(1.20)) is a VAR minimiser with the same data in both runs, so (P′) of §5(c) holds for it (#3.27-1): U^A = e^{iεA′*}MU^B with a_{j(x)}|A′*(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇A′*(x)| ≤ 2ρ̄(x), j(x) the layer of 𝐁^{(n)}_k(Z) at x. By (1.16), this layer is the scale of T_n(p) at the tested plaquettes: i on Z″_{i+1} ∖ Z″_i (and on Γ_h ∩ Z″_{h+1} at i = h), and j = h + n on Ω^c_{j+1} ∖ Z″_j. These layers are scales of the history (#3.7).
      {#3.26-2} At a plaquette p of the layer i, T_n(p) is (1 − β(1 − 2^{−m}))L₀^{2l}cε_i times the scale factor of the layer i, with m, l ≥ 0 (l = 0 for j ≤ k₀, #3.19.1) and c ≥ 1, so at least (1 − β)ε_i times it. U^A(∂p) and MU^B(∂p) differ by |Π_be^{iεAd(P_{<b})A′*_b} − 1|, P_{<b} the partial transports of MU^B around p, whose linear part is the curl of εA′* with these transports; VAR's ∇ = ∇^η_{U₀} is covariant at U₀ = MU^B (VAR p.281 l.7, #5.18), and the transports differ from its own by the closing plaquette of MU^B, ≤ B₃ε₁ in the normalisation of the layer (VAR (8)).
        {#3.26-2-1} So the difference is at most a_i²|∇A′*| + C(a_i|A′*|)² + C(a_i|A′*|)B₃ε₁ ≤ 3ρ̄(x) for γ small, so relative to T_n(p) by ≤ 3ρ̄_i/((1 − β)ε_i) ≤ 4ρ̄_i/ε_i, ρ̄_i the bound ρ̄ of (P′) on the layer i. The passage from MU^B to run B's own plaquettes is §2(c)'s, which reads only the regularity of U^B.
      {#3.26-3} Since ε_i = g_ip₀(g_i) ≥ δ′_i = g_iA₁p₁(g_i), 4ρ̄_i/ε_i ≤ (4/c_v)·c_vρ̄_i/δ′_i ≤ (4/c_v)C_{1.27}(ε/a_i)^{1−2ε₀} by #3.29–#3.30-1. So the cascade tests have the form δ^f_i, with the constant C of δ^f_i taken at least 4C_{1.27}/c_v plus §2(c)'s.
    {#3.26-4} *The test (1.75).* χ_{k,Λ} tests f^X := inf_{V_k⌈Λ}sup_{p∈Ω_k^c}|U^X_{k,Z}(∂p) − 1|/(η^X)² at the threshold 2ε^X_k (LFR I p.193 l.4, η^X the fine spacing of run X); in #3.26-4–#3.26-5, t denotes run A's threshold 2ε^A_k, and the runs' thresholds are compared in #3.26. Its plaquettes lie at distance ≥ 2MR_k from Z^c (BP_LFR2_CHI_K_LAMBDA #3.84), where 𝐁_k(Z) consists of k-blocks (BP_LFR2_CHI_K_LAMBDA #3.84-1), so the layer of U_{k,Z} there is the scale k of t. Let f^A < (1 + 2κ_s)t, and let V_k⌈Λ, the same variables in both runs, have sup_p|U^A_{k,Z}(∂p) − 1|/(η^A)² < f^A + σt, with σ > 0 and f^A + σt < (1 + 2κ_s)t.

So #3.26-2–#3.26-2-1 applies at the layer k, sup_p|U^B_{k,Z}(∂p) − 1|/(η^B)² ≤ f^A + σt + δ^f_kt, and f^B ≤ f^A + δ^f_kt as σ → 0. With A and B exchanged, f^A ≤ f^B + δ^f_kt^B ≤ f^B + (3/2)δ^f_kt (#3.26), the 3/2 absorbed in the C of δ^f_k, so |f^A − f^B| ≤ δ^f_kt wherever min(f^A, f^B) < (1 + 2κ_s)t.

(1.59) is (1.27) after #3.69's change of variables, which leaves χ′^{(j)} unchanged (CRE p.252 l.2–3, l.9–10), so it too is compared at the common B_j; since |e^{ig^A_jB_j(b)} − e^{ig^B_jB_j(b)}| ≤ |g^A_j − g^B_j||B_j(b)|, its soft forms differ by ≤ |g^A_j − g^B_j||B_j(b)|/(2δ′_j) plus the threshold's part (#3.26).

The step's later operations leave them unchanged (p.181 l.17–19), and the later CRE steps k′ ≥ k test only V_{k′}, V_{k′+1}, and A_{k′} (CRE (2.17), (3.2), (3.3), (3.16)).     - {#3.30} The absorption. The shell bound is used on the histories of the young pairs, born at a scale n > k_s/8. A cascade test is χ̄_c(x/(1 + κ_c)^{N−n}), which is (1/κ_c)-Lipschitz in x, so for it the bound is δ^s_j/κ_c = (N + 1)δ^s_j/κ_s. The same holds for the complements.

A sharp test of a complex argument is not defined, so on Bałaban's complex domains the tests act on the real integration variables, and the soft tests do as well.

- {#3.43} *The statement (RS).* Bałaban's construction and bounds hold with the soft tests, with constants independent of k, K, ε, and the volume. This means four things.
  - {#3.44} (a) Every removal of a redundant test holds on the plateau f < t, given the other soft tests at the thresholds (1 + κ_s)t. A cascade test χ_k^{(n)} is removed on its plateau (1 + κ_c)^{N−n}T_n, given χ_k^{(n+1)} at its support threshold (1 + κ_c)^{N−n}T_{n+1}.
  - {#3.45} (b) Every bound that uses a passed test holds at the threshold (1 + κ_s)t, or (1 + 2κ_s)t for a cascade test, and every bound that uses a failed test at the threshold t.
  - {#3.46} (c) The changes of variables that carry a test into a test of the new variables (CRE (1.22), p.269 l.45–50; LFR I (1.59)) stay exact.
  - {#3.47} (d) VAR's (7) holds with ε₁ enlarged by the factor 1 + 2κ_s (§1), the passed cascade thresholds reaching (1 + 2κ_s)T_n. Nonnegativity is not affected, since the soft tests have values in [0, 1], the loop bound B_W holds with the factor 1 + 2κ_s of #3.99, and the convergence of the expansions holds by (b).
  - {#3.48} Bałaban takes A₀ "a sufficiently large constant" (CRE p.246 l.14–15) and A₁/A₀ small ((3.7), p.266 l.24). A failed test enters as a lower bound, which the threshold t gives as before. A passed test enters as an upper bound through margins, and the margins are compared in #3.49–#3.99-1.

## 4. The Large-Field Integrands {#S4}

{#4.1} By §1, U″_k is a VAR minimiser with layer data regular at their own scales, all at scales ≥ k/2 − 1.

{#4.2} (a) *The configurations and their data.*
- {#4.3} U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(V″⌈_{Λ^c}, exp ig_kBM^·(U^{(AL)}_0)⌈_{Λ∩Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}}, V″⌈_{(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c}) (LFR II (1.50), p.370 l.3–5) is the minimiser of the Wilson action with the multiscale determining set 𝐁″_k. Its data are the shared block variables V″ and B, except on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}, where they contain the block averages of U^{(AL)}_0.
- {#4.4} U_0 is the minimiser of A(U) over U regular on Z with M_{𝐁_k}(U) = M_{𝐁_k(Z)}(Q^{s*}_kV_k) on Z ∖ Λ and no constraint on Λ (LFR II (1.3), p.357 l.11–17, with "the results of Sect. G [15]", VAR).
- {#4.5} So the two runs' U″_k differ in three ways: (A-i) the fine lattice of the problem of U″_k at equal data; (A-ii) the data on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}, through U_0, whose own problem is solved on the run's fine lattice; and (A-iii) the coupling in exp ig_kB, which differs relatively by ≤ g_k²|δ_k| (#4.168) and belongs with the coupling terms of (α).
  {#4.5-1} *The configuration of (1.70).* LFR II (1.70) (p.377) evaluates the weighted action at U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″), Bałaban's name (p.368 l.6–7) for U″_{k,Z″_{h+2}}, the configuration U″_k localised "again in the domain Z″_{h+2} instead of Z" (p.367 l.54) as (1.16) localises it in Z (p.360 l.2–7).
    {#4.5-1-00} The localisation is CRE's operation (p.257 l.7–21): a set 𝐁 and U_𝐁 are localised to a domain Ω with ∂Ω ⊂ Ω_j ∖ Ω_{j+1}, Ω a union of M₁-cubes of T_ξ, and the distance between ∂Ω and "this boundary of Ω_j, Ω_{j+1}, which is contained in Ω" at least 2M₁, as U(𝐁 ∪ 𝐁_j(Ω), ·) = U_{𝐁,Ω}(·) with 𝐁 ∪ 𝐁_j(Ω) = (𝐁 ∩ Ω^{∼−2}) ∪ (𝐁_j(Ω) ∩ (Ω ∖ Ω^{∼−2})) ((2.14)–(2.15)). LFR II writes its joins in this notation, 𝐁₁ = 𝐁″_k(Z) ∪ 𝐁_h(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}), "given by (2.14) [III]" (p.361 l.36–37).
    {#4.5-1-0} So U″_{h+2} = U(𝐁_{1.70}, ·), {#D.𝐁_1.70} 𝐁_{1.70} := 𝐁″_k ∪ 𝐁_{h+1}(Z″_{h+2}). The index is forced: ∂Z″_{h+2} lies in 𝐁″_k's layer h + 1 (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.12-2), so ∂Ω ⊂ Ω_j ∖ Ω_{j+1} holds only at j = h + 1, and (2.14)'s other hypotheses hold there (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.12-2–#4.12-3).
    {#4.5-1-3} *The weight's support.* supp w ⊂ Z″_{h+1} (#4.41-1), which lies at ≥ dist(Ω″_{h+2}, (Ω″_{h+1})^c) ≥ LMR_{h+2}a_{h+1} (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.18-1) from Ω″_{h+2} ∩ Z and at ≥ 5LMR_{h+1}a_h from Z^c (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.12-1), so at > 2M₁a_{h+1} from Ω^c, Ω = Z″_{h+2}. So supp w ⊂ Ω^{∼−2}, where 𝐁_{1.70} is 𝐁″_k: the collar S (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.11) and the strip T_{1.70} of #4.5-2 lie off supp w, and at the points of supp w the layers, the data, and the profile π of #4.30 are those of 𝐁″_k.
    {#4.5-1-4} *The collar's data.* In (1.16) U″_{k,Z} without argument is U″_{k,Z} at the collar data M^·(Q_k^{s*}V_k), the averages of the lift of the variable of the collar's top scale k, at which the argument (1/i)log[M^·(U″_k)(M^·(Q_k^{s*}V_k))^{−1}]⌈_{Z∖Z^{∼−1}} of 𝐇″_{k,Z} vanishes (p.360 l.6–7).
      {#4.5-1-4-0} The localisation in Z″_{h+2} is the same operation (p.368 l.2: "We will not repeat again all the considerations connected with this operation"), with the collar's top scale h + 1, and U″_{h+2} depends only on the fields on Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} ∩ Z″_{h+2} and on (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c (p.368 l.4–6). So its collar data are M^·(Q^{s*}_{h+1}W), W the layer-(h + 1) variables on S, as CRE (2.16) takes U_{k,□} at M^·(Q_k^{s*}V_k).
      {#4.5-1-4-1} By CRE (1.3) the fine plaquettes of Q^{s*}W are 1 or plaquettes of W, and every contour of RG I (0.4) has holonomy 1 for Q^{s*}W: the lift is flat inside a block of the scale h + 1, and a contour between two such blocks crosses once along [x, x′] and once along c, each with W's variable.
      {#4.5-1-4-2} So the average of the lift to one lattice is the lift to the next coarser one, the collar data of every layer have plaquettes 1 or of W and satisfy (7) with W's ε₁ (#1.3), and the two runs' collar data agree at every common scale. On a layer 0 the minimiser is its datum (VAR (3) at j = 0; CRE (1.12): "U = V_0 on Ω_1^c"), so on the collar's layer 0, at each run's fine spacing, U″_{h+2} = Q^{s*}_{h+1}W.
    {#4.5-1-5} At the data of (1.70) the data on Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} ∩ Z″_{h+2} are exp ig_kB, with no U_0 (LFR II p.368 l.4–5 at A_0 = 0), so of #4.5's differences only (A-i), at equal data, and (A-iii) enter. (A-i) is the chain of (b) for 𝐁_{1.70}, with the strip of #4.5-2.
  {#4.5-2} *The runs' collars.* 𝐁_{h+1}(Ω) is built down to each run's fine lattice (CRE p.256 l.56–62), its domains maximal and read in cube layers (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.11). In ℓ∞-distance from Ω^c, run A's domains are Ω^A_1 at M₁a_1 and Ω^A_m at 2M₁a_m (m ≥ 2), and run B's, on T_{ε/L}, Ω^B_1 at M₁a_0, Ω^B_2 at 2M₁a_1, and Ω^B_{m+1} = Ω^A_m (m ≥ 2, L ≥ 2), by the maximal domains of CRE p.256 l.59–61, as at ∂□₀ (#4.445.1), with the box property of #4.5-2-0. So off the strip {#D.T_1.70} T_{1.70} := Ω ∖ Ω^B_2 run B's layer m + 1 is run A's layer m, and run B's constraints are run A's composed with M.
    {#4.5-2-0} *The box property.* All components of the domains Z″_j, h ≤ j ≤ k, are rectangular parallelepipeds (LFR I p.179 l.50–51). So CRE's lattice ℓ¹ distance from a point of Ω = Z″_{h+2} to Ω^c is its distance to the nearest face of its component, as for □₀ in #4.445.1, and the ℓ∞ depths of #4.5-2 are these distances; Ω lies on the grid of the M₁a_m-cubes, m ≤ h + 1 (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.12-3), so the domains are again boxes on aligned grids.
    {#4.5-2-1} On T_{1.70} run B is at least as fine as run A at every point: its layers 0 and 1, at ε/L and a_0, cover T_{1.70}, where run A has its layer 0, at a_0, to the distance M₁a_1 and its layer 1, at a_1, beyond. So {#D.Ũ} Ũ := MU^B, run B's configuration blocked to run A's lattice, here MU″^B, equals the a_0-lift Q^{s*}_{h+1}W on T_{1.70}, by run B's pin and the averaging of lifts on its layer 0 and by its constraint on its layer 1 (#4.5-1-4–#4.5-1-4-1).
      {#4.5-2-1-1} This is run A's pinned datum on run A's layer 0, Ũ satisfies run A's constraints on T_{1.70}, and of the two strip sources of #4.445.2 the data ratio vanishes and only the current enters.

With one weight w in both runs, A(w, U″^B) − A(w, U″^A) = −b_w(U″^B) − [A_ε(w, U″^A) − A_ε(w, Ũ)], {#D.b_w} b_w(W) := A_ε(w, MW) − A_{ε/L}(w, W) the weighted blocking artefact, and with U″^A = exp(iεA′*)Ũ (VAR (112), #4.38) the bracket is ⟨J_w, A′*⟩, J_w the weighted current of Ũ, plus a remainder of second order in A′*.

- {#4.52} *The gauge of the data.* By (1.50) (p.370 l.2–5) and (1.25) (p.362 l.22–29), the data of U″_k on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} are exp(ig_kB)M^·(U^{(AL)}_0), with B the integration variable, at whose equal values the note compares the two runs' integrands, and M^·(U^{(AL)}_0) = (M^·U_0)^{ū₀}: the averages of 𝐁₁ = 𝐁″_k(Z) ∪ 𝐁_h(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}) (p.361 l.36–38), at the shared scales m, h ≤ m ≤ k, transformed by ū₀, which is constant on the blocks and equal at their centres to the u₀ of LFR I (1.86).

{#4.56} (d) *The forms and the functions of the configurations at the step of the 𝐑-operation.* The notation is that of #4.6–#4.42-2: a_j = εL^j, j(x) the layer of x, a_n the history's finest spacing. - {#4.57} *The objects.* H″_{1,k,Z} is the linear term of 𝐇″_{k,Z}(g_kB) in (1.19)–(1.20) (LFR II p.360 l.44–50, p.361 l.3–8): the data derivative at B = 0 of the minimiser U″_{k,Z} of the multiscale determining set 𝐁″_k(Z), at the background U^0_{k,Z}.

H_{1,k} of (1.2) is the data derivative of U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ) in V′ = exp ig_kB′ on Λ^{(k)}, at the background U_0; the form of (1.2) carries the weight ζ₀ (p.356 l.31–p.357 l.8).
  {#4.57-2} On the supports of the cutoffs, |g_kB| < δ′_k by χ′ (p.360 l.41–43), with δ′_k = g_kA₁p₁(g_k) (LFR I p.183 l.2), and |B′| < M₀g_k^{−1}ε_k (p.356 l.37), with M₀ as in #3.96. So the fields are ≤ {#D.b_k} b_k := max(A₁p₁(g_k), M₀p₀(g_k)) per point of 𝐁₀ or of Λ^{(k)}.
  {#4.57-3} These are Bałaban's dimensionless data: B on a layer j′ is the variable of the constraint L^{j′}ηQ_{j′}A = B of PBG (3.109)–(3.110), so its lift carries the factor (L^{j′}η)^{−1} = a_{j′}^{−1} relative to (3.133) (PBG p.422 l.32–33). Bałaban's bounds of these forms are sums over 𝐁₀, with |𝐁₀| ≤ (100MR_k)^dN² (p.361 l.11–13 and l.19–20), and (d) compares the two runs per point of 𝐁₀ or of Λ^{(k)}.
- {#4.58} *The lifts and the chain rule.* VAR's constraint (3) (p.278 l.11–13) is the plain average, Ū^j = V on Λ_j, while PBG's lift belongs to the double bar. In each run the data derivative of a VAR minimiser with a multiscale determining set, in VAR's gauge (153), is H₁(1 + Ξ), with PBG's H₁ = G₁Q*(QG₁Q*)^{−1} of (3.129) for that set, Q the linearised multiscale double bar Q_db of #4.64, on S_j in the form of #4.62-0.2, and Ξ the interface twist of #4.61–#4.68, each run with its own Ξ at its own data. So the lifts of (1.2) and (1.21) are H₁B̃, with the twisted data {#D.B̃} B̃ := (1 + Ξ)B, and |B̃| ≤ (1 + 2dL)|B| per point (#4.62-1.1).
  {#4.58-0.1} PBG Theorem 3.12 gives it (3.132)–(3.133) between any two layers (p.422 l.17–30, p.423 l.30–36): for x ∈ Δ(y), y ∈ Λ_j, y′ ∈ Λ_{j′}, |∇H₁(x, y′)| ≤ O(1)a_j^{−1}a_{j′}^{−d}e^{−½δ₁d(y,y′)}, and ‖ζ′∇H₁(·, y′)‖_β ≤ O(1)(‖ζ′‖^ξ_β + |ζ′|)a_j^{−1−β}a_{j′}^{−d}e^{−½δ₁d(y,y′)} for ζ′ ∈ C₀^∞(Δ̃(y)). So the Hölder bound is at the scale of the receiving layer; in run B, PBG's L^jη is L^{j+1}(ε/L) = a_j at the shared scale j.
  {#4.58-0.2} The proof of (10.2) uses only the positivity of G₁^{−1} and the surjectivity of Q, so H₁B minimises ⟨A, (Δ₁ + DRD*)A⟩ under QA = B for the multiscale problem too. A layer of run B's set at the shared scale j ≥ 0 is at its own scale j + 1, where its averaging is M^{j+1} = M^j∘M, so its derivative is d(M^{j+1})(U^B) = d(M^j)(MU^B)∘dM(U^B) by the chain rule.
  {#4.58-1} So at aligned backgrounds Q^B = Q^AQ₁ layer by layer, for the double bar by (B4) of the Cauchy note's §10.1 with Q₁ = Q̄₁(U^B), and for the plain averaging by composition with Q₁ = Q₁^{pl} = dM(U^B). Hence (10.4)–(10.5) and the characterisation of E hold with the multiscale double bar Q and H₁.
  {#4.58-1.1} The characterisation identifies E with the Green operator on ker Q^A at run A's pair, {#D.G₁^Q} G₁^Q := G₁ − G₁Q*(QG₁Q*)^{−1}QG₁ = (I − H₁Q)G₁: for ψ ∈ ker Q^A the double-bar lift ℒ of §10.4 gives ℒψ ∈ ker Q^B and Q₁ℒψ = ψ, so ⟨ψ, G_A^{−1}E⟩ = β(ℒψ, 𝒜^B), and QG₁^Q = 0 and ⟨ψ, G₁^{−1}G₁^Qs⟩ = ⟨ψ, s⟩ for ψ ∈ ker Q give E₀ = G₁^Qs with {#D.⟨ψ,s⟩} ⟨ψ, s⟩ := β(ℒψ, 𝒜^B), {#D.E₀} E₀ := (I − H₁Q)E the part of E in ker Q^A, which is all of E at equal twisted data (#4.128).

    - {#4.63} Ξ² = 0. Ξ writes on the bonds of S_j, which lie within a_j of Ω_j^c, and reads the bonds of Λ_{j−1}. At the next interface Ξ reads bonds of Λ_j in the blocks B(z) of the outer endpoints z of S_{j+1}; these lie within (d + 1)a_{j+1} of Ω_{j+1}. So no bond of S_j is read by Ξ if every layer below the top, the only ones with an interface above them, is wider than (d + 1)L + 1 = 5L + 1 in its own units.
      {#4.63-1} It is: > RM ≥ 12L (#4.98) for a sequence satisfying PRT2 (2.2), (L^jη)^{−1}dist(Ω_j^c, Ω_{j+1}) > RM; and ≥ M or ≥ LM₁ for 𝐁″_k and the joins (#4.10-1), with M ≥ 2(d + 1)L²M₁ ≥ 10L² (W-δ #W8.19-1) and M₁ = KM′ ≥ M′ ≥ 6L (#T2.9, W-δ #W8.18), both > 5L + 1. Two interface corrections therefore cannot chain: Ξ² = 0 and (1 + Ξ)^{−1} = 1 − Ξ.

- {#4.131} *The π-part of β for multiscale data.* Notation as in the Cauchy note's #C10.4.98–#C10.4.101 and #C10.4.63–#C10.4.86, at d = 4, with {#D.ν.3} ν := 𝒬′*λ^B, the Cauchy note's ν_λ (#C10.3.7), {#D.ℓ.2} ℓ := a_j at an interface site of the layer j, τ̂_n for τ̂, and {#D.𝔰} 𝔰 := σ_ka_j^{−2}, as for the gauge-fixing sources above.

The gauge factor w of (B5) composes as the double bar does ((B4), CMP 98 (90)–(92)): run B's w is run A's w about MU^B, applied to the gauge parameter (1/i)log w₁ = Q′₁λ + q₁(λ, 𝒜) + … of the one-step factor w₁ and to the field Q₁𝒜.   - {#4.135} The bound of q. The one-step factor is w₁ = v₁(U₁^u)^{−1}·u(y)·v₁(U₁) (the Cauchy note's #C10.1.9-2) with v₁(U₁)(y) = (R_{0,y}U₁)‾ of CMP 98 (97) at j = 1 (p.032 l.31–32), the inverse of the u(y) of (87): the average over x ∈ B(y) of the logarithms of the contour variables (the Cauchy note's #C10.1.4-1-1), the group averages (0.10) of the holonomies h_Γ(x) of U₁U₀^{−1} along the contours Γ ∈ 𝐆(y, x), transported by the real background, each contour having at most dL fine bonds of length η = ε/L.
    {#4.135-0.1} Under u = e^{iλ}, h_Γ(x) becomes u(y)h_Γ(x)u_{x,Γ}^{−1}, with u_{x,Γ} the u(x) transported along Γ. The averages are linear in the logarithms up to third order: the block mean is linear, and for (0.10), Σ_Γ(1/i)log(e^{iA_Γ}e^{−iZ}) = 0, the second-order terms −½i[A_Γ, Z] sum to −½in[Ā, Ā] = 0 at Z = Ā + O(|A|²), Ā the mean of the A_Γ, so Z = Ā + O(|A|³). So the bilinear part of (1/i)log w₁ in (λ, A) consists only of the second-order Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff terms ½[X, Y] of the compositions: the two products u(y)h_Γ(x)u_{x,Γ}^{−1} and the product of the three factors of w₁.

At most four such terms occur, so |q₁(λ, A)(y)| ≤ c_qε sup_{B(y)}|λ| sup|A|, {#D.c_q} c_q := 4d, the second supremum over the bonds of the paths.
    {#4.135-2} Iterating the composition over the scales m < j, with |Q′| ≤ 1 and |Q₁A| ≤ sup|A| (averages), gives |q_A(λ, A)| ≤ Σ_{m<j}c_qL^mε sup|λ| sup|A| ≤ 2c_qa_j sup|λ| sup|A|, the suprema over the block of the scale j.

        {#4.144-1} Each term of Θ(ℱ, 𝒜) reads ℱ in one slot of q_A or q₁: in the field slot raw, through Q₁ℱ, or through P_Bℱ = ℱ − D_Bμ_ℱ, or in the parameter slot through μ_ℱ, δμ_ℱ, or Q′₁μ_ℱ, with the other slot a field of 𝒜, at most c_oσ_ka_j^{−1}, or a parameter of 𝒜, at most c_oσ_k, {#D.c_o} c_o := 1 + 2B_G(1 + c_𝔠)(c_{g2} + 2c_{g6}), by #4.136–#4.137 and τ̂_n ≤ 2. Polarising the five terms of #4.134, whose coefficients add up to 6, gives terms of Θ(ℱ, 𝒜) whose coefficients add up to 6.
      - {#4.145} The weights. In the composition of #4.135–#4.135-2, the step of the scale m reads the m-fold averages Q′^{(m)}λ and Q^{(m)}A at the sites and bonds of the scale m, and its output is carried to the scale j by the averages Q′ of the scales m + 1, …, j − 1. So each of the (a_j/a_m)⁴ blocks of the scale m in a cell of the scale j carries the weight (a_m/a_j)⁴.
        {#4.145-1} Within one block, q₁ pairs the parameter at the centre and at the points x of the block with the means over 𝐆(y, x) of the transported sums along contours of at most dL bonds of the scale m, and a bond has weight at most 1 in the mean of each of the L^d points x of its block, so its coefficient is at most a_m/L times the parameter, while the mean over the dL^d bonds of the block is a_mL^{−d} times it. The coefficient of a bond therefore exceeds the block mean by at most L^{d−1}.
        {#4.145-2} A Q^{(m)} average or a Q′^{(m)} average is an average over a block of the scale m with bounded weights, so its transpose spreads a coefficient over that block. With the measure a_j⁴ of the interface site and |D̄*ν| ≤ c_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4} per coarse cell (#4.139), the field-slot part of s_π therefore has, on every bond of the cell, the density at most c_qL^{d−1}c_νB̄_λε₁Σ_{m<j}a_m a_j^{−4}|λ| ≤ 2c_qL^{d−1}c_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−3}|λ|, |λ| the parameter in the other slot.
        {#4.145-3} The parameter-slot part is a transpose T*n of an operator T ∈ {μ_·, δμ_·, Q′₁μ_·} applied to a scalar density n with |n| ≤ 2c_qL^dc_oc_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}σ_k (the parameter is read at the run-A points of the cell, a sublattice of run B's points, whence L^d in place of L^{d−1}). On the layer j − 1 the same holds with the factor L of #4.139.
      - {#4.146} The gradient terms. The field-slot entries D_Bμ_ℱ, D_Aμ_ℱ, and D_Aδμ_ℱ are covariant differences of parameters. At the scale m, Q^{(m)}D_A = D_{(m)}Q′^{(m)} by the first order of (B5) iterated (Q₁D_Bλ = D_AQ′₁λ), and a transported contour sum of a covariant difference telescopes, contour by contour, to the difference of the transported end values.
        {#4.146-1} So these entries are parameter-slot reads at the two ends of each contour, of total weight at most two in each mean over 𝐆(y, x), without a derivative: the step of the scale m contributes at most 2c_q|λ| times the end values, with no geometric factor a_m/a_j, and the sum over m < j gives the factor j. Their part of s_π is T*n with |n| ≤ 4c_qjL^dc_oc_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}σ_k.

        {#4.147-1} So T* is a product of the same factors in the reverse order, with D and D*, Q′ and Q′* exchanged, and its sup bound is a product of the entries G′D* and DG′ of (3.42) and of the averages' bounds, |T*n| ≤ c_Ta_j sup|n|, with c_T a polynomial in B_G, c_𝔠, d, and the Cauchy note's C_tr (#C10.4.14-1).

  - {#4.150} For f^A two further terms are of relative size ε₁. The curvature terms of PBG (3.10), with |F| ≤ 2C₀^{ms}ε₁/a_j² at Ũ (#4.48.0-0), add at most 2(1 + d²)C₀^{ms}ε₁ times these bounds.

The quadratic form of (1.20) is (1.21) plus the small form (p.361 l.22–28), and the small form (with its part −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ)⟩), the linear term of (1.20), and V(ζ, ·) enter only through 𝐂_k (#4.156).
  {#4.151-1} So d is compared as a whole (#4.152–#4.155), and 𝐂_k with W_ext (#4.160–#4.160-2-1, #4.170–#4.200). Of the bounds of #4.201–#4.201-3 the main proof uses only that of (1.21), which (1.49) and (1.70) keep.
  - {#4.152} *The denominator.* By (1.1) (p.356 l.19–20), d = ∫δ_{G₀}(V′)χ exp[−g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ))] dV′|_Λ, where Bałaban's V_Λ carries on Λ the data of U_0 (LFR I (1.79), p.195). So V′ is the deviation from this data, V′ = 1 gives U_0, and the cutoff χ̄, the soft form of χ(|(1/i)log V′(b)| < M₀ε_k) (LFR I (1.101), p.201; §3(d)), is centred there.
    {#4.152-1} In the notation of (c), run X's integrand at V′ is exp[−g_k^{−2}A_X(ζ₀, U^X_{k,Z}(V′V′^X₀V_{Λ^c}))], with V_{Λ^c} the shared data off Λ (#4.43-1.1). At equal V′ the two runs' data on Λ^{(k)} differs by e^{i𝔛}, since V′V′^B₀ = V′e^{i𝔛}V′^A₀ and the norm is bi-invariant.
    {#4.152-2} On the support of χ̄, |V′ − 1| < (1 + κ_s)M₀ε_k. With C(M) ≥ 8(1 + κ_s)max(M₀, C_𝔛(M)), V′ and e^{it𝔛} each move the data by at most ε₁/8 per bond, so the data V′e^{it𝔛}V′^A₀V_{Λ^c}, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, is regular with 2ε₁, as in (c), "The comparison". At each V′ of the support the two runs' exponents therefore differ by at most the sum of two bounds.
    - {#4.153} The equal-data difference of g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(·)) at the data V′V′^A₀V_{Λ^c}. As for A(ζ₀, U_0) in (c), "The propagation", (b) bounds it by Σ_xC_w(ε₀)g_k^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁² over the points x of the layers of 𝐁_k(Z). The weight has a_{j(x)}|∇ζ₀| ≤ c_ζ, since |∇ζ₀| ≤ c_ζ/a_k (#4.109) and a_{j(x)} ≤ a_k.
    - {#4.154} The change of run B's g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(·)) from the data V′V′^A₀V_{Λ^c} to V′V′^B₀V_{Λ^c}. (c), "The propagation" and "The result", bounds it by C_A(M)g_k^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁² per bond of Λ^{(k)}. That bound uses only that the data path V′e^{it𝔛}V′^A₀V_{Λ^c} is regular with 2ε₁, which holds at every V′ of the support (#4.152), and #4.51-3's bound on ‖𝔛‖_∞, so it holds there and not only at V′ = 1.

    {#4.155} The Haar measure, δ_{G₀}, and χ̄ are the same in both runs at equal couplings, and the integrands are positive. So the Cauchy note's #C8.6.1-1 gives |log d^B − log d^A| ≤ φ_d, with φ_d the sum of the two bounds. By the results of (b) and (c), φ_d is ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the layers of 𝐁_k(Z) plus C_hθ̃^n per bond of Λ^{(k)}.
      {#4.155-1} On the complex class the argument of #C8.6.1 runs with absolute integration in place of positivity. It uses the lower bound of |d| by e^{−c(M)} times the integral of the modulus of its integrand, with {#D.e^−c(M)} e^{−c(M)} := exp(−O(1)log M|Λ|) and |Λ| ≤ O(M⁴) (Cauchy #C8.6.6-3, p.358 l.26), which holds on the class by #4.567-3. For a pointwise bound φ of the two runs' difference of the exponents it needs (e^φ − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ ½, and it gives |log d^B − log d^A| ≤ 2(e^φ − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ 4e^{c(M)}φ.
      {#4.155-2} The value D(1) at V′ = 1 of that difference does not depend on V′ and factors out of both integrals exactly, so φ is only the oscillation {#D.φ′_d} φ′_d := sup_{V′}|D(V′) − D(1)| over the support of χ̄. The data at V′ differs from that at V′ = 1 on Λ only, so by the kernel form of VAR Proposition 4 in (b) (rate ⅛δ₀) both runs' changes of U_{k,Z}, and their run difference, decay from Λ, and φ′_d ≤ C_d(M)C_hθ̃^n, with C_d(M) a constant of M that counts the points of the layers within the decay length of Λ.
      {#4.155-3} The second bound above is already on the bonds of Λ^{(k)}. So (e^{φ′_d} − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ ½ for n ≥ n_d(M), and then |log d^B − log d^A − D(1)| ≤ 4e^{c(M)}C_d(M)C_hθ̃^n, with |D(1)| ≤ φ_d. For n < n_d(M), each run's log d is bounded by Bałaban's bounds, and the factor θ̃^{−n_d} is absorbed in C_h. This uses the bounds #4.42 and #4.55 on the class, which #4.556–#4.569 derives under (T-c).
  - {#4.156} *The sum 𝐂_k.* LFR II collects the small terms of all the expansions of the Wilson actions, together with I(U_0) of (1.10), into 𝐂_k (p.369 l.2–7). 𝐂_k enters (1.49) as one term, and the expressions V(Y) of (1.68)–(1.69) through the re-summation of p.377 l.2–9. Among these small terms are the linear term of (1.20), the small form of (1.20) with its part −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ)⟩, V(ζ, ·), the last three terms of (1.24), the pieces of (1.26)–(1.29), and A(ζ₁, U_0) of (1.31) (p.361 l.10–28, p.362 l.29–40, p.363 l.11–45, p.364 l.1–16).
    {#4.156-1} Since (1.49) is an equality for (1.1), 𝐂_k is given exactly by (1.37) (p.365 l.43–50, with the second term of its right-hand side included in O(1) by p.366 l.12), the localisation of p.367 l.50–p.368 l.4 with (1.48) (p.368 l.32–36), and (1.10). In the notation of (c), with {#D.(g″)^−2} (g″)^{−2} := 1/(g″_k(·))², and with the weights split as ζ₀ + (1 − ζ₀),

    {#4.157} 𝐂_k = W_ext − A(w_Z, U_k) + g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_k) − A((g″)^{−2}ζ₀, U″_k) − g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(V′_kV′₀V_{Λ^c})) + A((g″)^{−2}ζ₁, U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″)) + ½Σ_{p∈T_η}η⁴ζ(x(p))|(DH″_{1,k,Z}B)(p)|² − log d + E_k(Λ),

    {#4.158} {#D.W_ext} W_ext := A(w_e, U_k) − A(w_e, U″_k), {#D.w_e} w_e := (g″)^{−2}(1 − ζ₀), {#D.w_Z} w_Z := ((g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2})(1 − ζ₀)1_Z.

    {#4.159} Here (g_k(·))^{−2} is g_k^{−2} on Z and (g″)^{−2} off Z (p.365 l.19), and the support of ζ₀ lies in Z (ζ_i ∈ C₀^∞(X_i), LFR I p.201 l.28, as p.365 l.33–40 uses it), so (g_k(·))^{−2}ζ₀ = g_k^{−2}ζ₀.
      {#4.159-1} Bałaban combines the weights ((g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2})(Z_k ∖ Z) and g_k^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) (p.364 l.36–45). Their sum is (g″)^{−2} off Z, where ζ₀ = 0, and g_k^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) on Z, that is, (g_k(·))^{−2}(1 − ζ₀). p.364 l.44 prints (g″)^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) = w_e for it, which differs from the sum by w_Z, nonzero wherever g″ ≠ g_k on Z ∩ supp(1 − ζ₀): at a point of the layer m of g″, (g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2} = β_m(1 − φ_m) + Σ_{m<l≤k}β_l (#4.171), bounded by O(1)(k − m) and not by 0 (p.364 l.35–36).
        {#4.159-1-1} Bałaban expands the combined action around U_k by (1.36) and states that its first term "is equal to" −A((g_k(·))^{−2}(1 − ζ₀), U_k) (p.365 l.29–33), the weight being the sum: the first term is the value at 𝐇 = 0, the action at U_k^{u_k^{−1}}, since U″_{k,Z^{∼−3}} = (exp iη𝐇U_k)^{u_k^{−1}}, and the action is gauge invariant. As (g_k(·))^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) = w_e − w_Z, A((g_k(·))^{−2}, U_k) = g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_k) + A(w_e, U_k) − A(w_Z, U_k).
      {#4.159-2} The term g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_0) on the left of (1.37) is the one that 1/d contributes by (1.10). With I(U_0), which 𝐂_k contains (p.369 l.7), it equals −log d + E_k(Λ) by (1.10), and (1.49) carries −E_k(Λ) separately.
    - {#4.160} The part 𝐂_k − W_ext. At equal couplings E_k(Λ) is the same in both runs. Each of the five actions is a sum over the plaquettes in the support of its weight, which lies in Z, and its weight is of the kind treated in (b): g_k^{−2}ζ₀ as for d above, (g″)^{−2}ζ₀ and (g″)^{−2}ζ₁ as the weight ζ₁/(g″)² of (1.70), and w_Z as in #4.160-0.2–#4.160-0.3. The configurations are VAR minimisers with multiscale data.
      {#4.160-0.1} The shared variable is V_k, as in #4.559–#4.559-2; then V′_k = V_k(V^X_Λ)^{−1} (p.378 l.12) depends on the run. U_k and U_{k,Z}(V′_kV′₀V_{Λ^c}) carry on Λ the data V′_kV′^X₀ (p.365 l.10–13), compared at equal V_k and regular as for d above, since χ̄ restricts V′_k in (1.1). U″_k carries the data exp(ig_kB)M^·(U^{(AL)}_0) of (1.50), and U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″) carries exp(ig_kB) and V″ only; both are regular as for the action of (1.70).
      {#4.160-0.2} The weight w_Z satisfies 0 ≤ w_Z ≤ (g″)^{−2}, which is all that (c) uses (#4.54-0.1). Its factor ((g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2})(1 − ζ₀) satisfies #4.41-1-1's bound |w| + a_{j(x)}|∇w| ≤ C_∇g_{j(x)}^{−2}, with 1 − ζ₀ in place of ζ₁, since a_{j(x)}|∇ζ₀| ≤ a_k|∇ζ₀| ≤ c_ζ (#4.109). In (b) the factor 1_Z enters only through the differences of the weight in J_∇ (#4.41-2) and in b_w (#4.41-3), each ≤ (1 + 2b₂ḡ²)g_{j(x)}^{−2} ≤ C_∇g_{j(x)}^{−2} and nonzero only at the plaquettes within ε of ∂Z.
      {#4.160-0.3} Z is a union of MR_k-cubes of the scale k (balaban_proofs/BP_LAYER_WIDTHS.md #4.18-2-1-2), so ∂Z meets a block of a layer j ≤ k in at most 2d of its faces, with at most 2(a_j/ε)³ sites of T_ε within ε of each. With d bonds at a site, a_j|A′*| ≤ ρ̄(x) (#4.41-0-1), and #4.41-2's plaquette deviation, these sites add ≤ 4d²(a_j/ε)³ε⁴·ε^{−3}·6C_∇g_j^{−2}·2C₀^{ms}ε₁ε²a_j^{−2}·ρ̄(x)a_j^{−1} = 48d²C₀^{ms}C_∇g_j^{−2}ε₁ρ̄(x) per block to the first-order term.
        {#4.160-0.3-1} In b_w they lie in at most 4d(a_j/ε)³ of the (a_j/ε)⁴ cells of the block, each with the fine action ≤ 3(C₀^{ms})²ε₁²(ε/a_j)⁴ (#4.41-3), and add ≤ 12d(C₀^{ms})²C_∇g_j^{−2}(ε/a_j)ε₁². These are at most d² and 2d times the first and third terms of #4.42, so #4.42 holds for A(w_Z, ·) with (1 + d²)C_w(ε₀) in place of C_w(ε₀), also in the term that #4.42-1 adds to C_h.
      {#4.160-1} So each action differs between the runs by ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the layers of its configuration in Z, by (b), plus ≤ C_hθ̃^n per data point of Λ, by (c). The form differs by ≤ ½r̄_nN_k ≤ ½C_hθ̃^n per point of 𝐁₀, by #4.201–#4.201-3, and log d by ≤ φ_d.
      {#4.160-2} Hence the two runs' values of 𝐂_k − W_ext differ by ≤ 13dC_hθ̃^n per point of the component's history (10 from the five actions, ½ from the form, 2 from φ_d, #4.155): a point of a coarser layer of Z, a point of 𝐁₀, a data point, and a bond of Λ^{(k)} are each counted at a point of the history that contains it, and the factor d covers the bonds at a point.
        {#4.160-2-1} This uses the Cauchy note's (10.6c) through the form and the form's interface pieces (#4.61–#4.150, #4.201). It holds at real configurations. On the class the actions and the form keep their bounds by #4.556–#4.569 under (T-c), and log d has #4.155-3's, which adds 4e^{c(M)}C_d(M)C_hθ̃^n once per component.
    - {#4.161} *The shell of χ̄(Λ)(V′_k).* The factor χ(Λ)(V′_k) of (1.1) outside the quotient, in its soft form χ̄ (§3(d), LFR I (1.101)), depends on the run through V^X_Λ. It is 1 on the components of the first class and stands on those of the second (p.378 l.13–15 and l.20–22).
      - {#4.162} At equal V_k the two runs' arguments {#D.f^X_b} f^X_b := |(1/i)log V′^X_k(b)| differ by at most the data difference {#D.s_n} s_n := C_Δ(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁ per bond of (c), by the triangle inequality of the bi-invariant distance, since V′^B_k = V′^A_k·V^A_Λ(V^B_Λ)^{−1}.
      - {#4.163} The thresholds are {#D.t^X.2} t^X := M₀ε^X_k, with M₀ the same in both runs (#3.96, p.378 l.10–14) and |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_k²|δ_k| ≤ ½t^A (#2.10).
      - {#4.164} Everywhere, χ̄(f/t) is Lipschitz in f with the constant 1/(κ_st), and |∂_tχ̄(f/t)| ≤ (1 + κ_s)/(κ_st), since the derivative vanishes where f ≥ (1 + κ_s)t. So per bond |χ̄(f^A_b/t^A) − χ̄(f^B_b/t^B)| ≤ δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c, with {#D.δ^χ_n} δ^χ_n := s_n/(κ_st^A) the data part and {#D.δ^χ_c} δ^χ_c := (1 + κ_s)|t^A − t^B|/(κ_s min(t^A, t^B)) ≤ 4Cg_k²|δ_k|/κ_s the coupling part, by min(t^A, t^B) ≥ ½t^A and 2(1 + κ_s) ≤ 4 (κ_s = 1/240, #T3.34-1).
      - {#4.165} The factor enters the split #3.33 with the other tests of Π_X. Since (Π_A − Π_B)₊ ≤ 1{Π_A > 0}|Π_A − Π_B|, with every factor in [0, 1], and 1{Π_A > 0} is the product of run A's sharp tests at the thresholds (1 + κ_s)t^A for the passed tests, t^A for the failed ones, and the cascade thresholds of #3.35, telescoping over the bonds gives (Π_A − Π_B)₊ρ_A ≤ |Λ^{(k)}|(δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c) times run A's own term with these sharp tests, which (RS) (#3.43–#3.47) covers, and the same with A and B exchanged.
        {#4.165-1} So the shell is bounded as the shells of #3.33–#3.35: by δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c per bond of Λ^{(k)}, times a run's own term with Bałaban's bounds. The coupling part is carried with |δ_k|, as in #3.40–#3.40-1.
      - {#4.166} δ^χ_n ≤ C_χ(M)θ̃^n. Here ε₁/ε_k ≤ C(M)R_km_s^{1/2} (#1.6-3, #D.m_s), R_k being at most 2^{r+1}L times a power of log(ḡ^{−2} + 8b′n + b′j(C) + C_W) and m_s ≤ 8(1 + β₀)²n (#4.55-0.1–#4.55-1), and (ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3} ≤ θ̃^nL^{−(1−ε₀)n/12} (#4.55-1-1 at s = ⅓). So δ^χ_n = s_n/(κ_sM₀ε_k) ≤ C_χ(M)θ̃^n with {#D.C_χ(M)} C_χ(M) := the supremum over the young histories of C_Δ(M)C(M)R_km_s^{1/2}L^{−(1−ε₀)n/12}/(κ_sM₀), finite since the slack L^{−(1−ε₀)n/12} absorbs R_km_s^{1/2}. It depends on M, j(C), ḡ, L, ε₀, r, b′, C_W, κ_s, and Bałaban's constants, and not on k, K, ε, or the volume.
    - {#4.168} The couplings. Their differences enter 𝐂_k − W_ext in three ways. Through the weights: at a point x of the layer m = j(x), (g″)^{−2} = (1 − φ_m)g_{m−1}^{−2} + φ_mg_m^{−2} (#4.159-1, #4.171), so each weight of #4.157 is a combination of g_{m−1}^{−2}, g_m^{−2}, and g_k^{−2} with coefficients in [−1, 1] built from φ_m, ζ₀, ζ₁, and 1_Z, the same in both runs (#4.109), and it changes by ≤ |δ_{m−1}| + |δ_m| + |δ_k|, with δ_{−1} := δ_0.
      {#4.168-0.1} By #C10.4.41 the Wilson density at spacing η is ≤ (½ + c_κ)|X|² where η²|X| ≤ 1, which holds at configurations regular with 2ε₁, as 2C₀^{ms}ε₁ ≤ 1 (#4.92). With d(d − 1)/2 plaquettes at a point, such an action over the block of x is ≤ C_actε₁², {#D.C_act} C_act := d²(1 + 2c_κ)(C₀^{ms})². So the weights contribute ≤ C_actε₁²(|δ_{j(x)−1}| + |δ_{j(x)}| + |δ_k|) per point and action.
      {#4.168-0.2} Through the data exp(ig_kB) at fixed B they enter by ≤ C_prc_K(1 + β₀)²(k − j + 1)ε₁δ′_k|δ_k| per data point of the scale j, by #4.54-0.1.2 with the data moved by |(g^A_k − g^B_k)B| ≤ g_k²|δ_k|δ′_k on the support of χ′ (#4.57) in place of |δD|, and g_k²/g_j² ≤ (1 + β₀)²(k − j + 1) by CRE (2.6).
      {#4.168-1} Through log d and E_k(Λ) they enter as in the coupling items of the Cauchy note's §8.6. The form ½⟨DH″B, ζDH″B⟩ carries no coupling at fixed B. Its background U^0_{k,Z} is U″_{k,Z} at the data M^·(U_0) on Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} and V″ = V off it, which do not contain exp(ig_kB) (LFR II (1.19), p.360 l.46–53; #4.57), and in each run, at its own g_k, the factor g_k² of the quadratic term of (1.20) (p.361 l.5–6) cancels the weight g_k^{−2} that (1.14)–(1.15) give A(ζ₀, U″_k) (p.359 l.36–44).
    - {#4.169} *The Localised Pieces of 𝐂_k.* LFR II localises 𝐂_k with the old terms: the terms of the first part of (1.49), except the first two, are treated by (1.59) or (1.60) and the decoupling of σ₀, then by the representation (1.61)–(1.64) (p.373 l.10–17), and re-summed into V(X^∼) and V(Y) ((1.68), pp.376–377). So the comparison of each piece is that of #4.209–#4.555 with the localised terms 𝐂(X) of 𝐂_k (p.367 l.50–p.368 l.4, (1.48)) in place of 𝐓(X), in three parts.
      {#4.169-0.1} (i) Their own run differences at a common configuration: the action pieces are sums over the plaquettes of X, bounded per point by #4.42 and #4.55 as in #4.160–#4.160-2, and the piece of −log d is the single term I(U₀) of (1.10), with |I(U₀)| < O(1)log M|Λ| on the analytically extended class ((1.11), p.358), which 𝐂_k contains ("including the term I(U₀) from the denominator", p.369 l.7) and which is not a polymer expansion.
      {#4.169-0.2} It is localised as the other terms are, through the representation of its background (1.61)–(1.64), so its pieces are I at the representation configurations, which lie in the class (#4.423–#4.423-4).
      {#4.169-1} Its run difference at a common configuration is that of #4.152–#4.155-3 for log d (on the class #4.155-1–#4.155-3), which holds at the points of the class by #4.567-3, and at the representation configurations of (i), which Bałaban builds from such a point and at which he localises I(U₀) (p.369 l.7, p.373 l.10–17).
      {#4.169-2} (ii) The variation along the joint line of (ii) of that item, term by term with Bałaban's class bounds of 𝐂(X); these terms are of the generation k, so no age factor and no generation sum enter. Its inputs, the fine side and the current of the joint line, are #4.313–#4.328-2 and #4.335–#4.366.
      {#4.169-3} (iii) The decoupled propagators: the relative walk-term bound (W-δ) for the decoupled propagators of the pieces, applied as in #4.427–#4.439.
    - {#4.170} *The exterior part W_ext.* U_k and U″_k have the same determining set and data off Λ (p.370 l.7–9), so W_ext is one weighted action at two configurations whose determining sets and data differ only on Λ (by (1.33)). Each of its two actions is a sum over the whole lattice, so #4.42 and #4.55 alone bound its run difference only by a sum over all points. The data on Λ is not close either.
        {#4.170-0.1} On the deep part {#D.Λ_1} Λ_1 := Λ ∖ Λ_0, {#D.Λ_0} Λ_0 := Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} (LFR I p.195 l.27–29), U″_k carries the large-field data V″ of (1.50), and U_k carries the averages of a configuration that is small inside Λ. So no short segment of data joins the two.
        {#4.170-1} The comparison is at equal couplings, except at #4.190–#4.195-2, and in the common gauge of #4.52–#4.52-1.1, with U_0 in the AL-gauge from the beginning (LFR I p.197 l.42).
        {#4.170-2} Here ε₁ is the larger of the constants of #1.3 and #4.43-1, {#D.ε̂} ε̂ := ε₁ + δ′_k, and {#D.w̄} w̄ := sup|w_e| ≤ g_k^{−2} + O(1)k (p.364 l.35–36). A point of Λ is a block of a layer of 𝐁″_k ∩ Λ or a bond of Λ^{(k)}; it is a point of the component's history at a layer ≥ n. A point of the history carries at most one block and d bonds, so a bound per point of Λ is at most d + 1 times the same bound per point of the history, a factor absorbed in C_h.
      - {#4.171} *The weight.* The weighted blocking artifact and the current of A(w_e, ·) need a_{j(x)}|∇w_e(x)| ≤ C_{∇e}w̄, as in #4.106–#4.124, with {#D.C_∇e} C_{∇e} := 4c_{2.24}b₂ḡ² + c_ζ. Indeed a_{j(x)}|∇ζ₀| ≤ c_ζ (#4.109, a_{j(x)} ≤ a_k), a_{j(x)}|∇(g″)^{−2}| ≤ 2c_{2.24}b₂ (#4.41-1-1, with φ_m as in #4.171-1), and 1 ≤ 2ḡ²w̄, since w_e = (g″)^{−2} ≥ g_k^{−2} ≥ ḡ^{−2}/2 off Z by (1 + β₀)² ≤ 2. At a point x of the layer m, (g″)^{−2}(x) − g_k^{−2} = β_m(1 − φ_m(x)) + Σ_{m<l≤k}β_l, as in the coupling-term item #4.593–#4.593-1, with the layers of the sequence of domains of g″_k(·), whose bound O(1)(k − j) is p.364 l.35–36.

The collar Λ_m ∖ Λ_m^{∼−1} is one layer of the cubes of which Λ_m is a union (CRE p.245 l.40–43), so its width is ≥ a_m, and φ_m is chosen, as ζ₀ and ζ₁ are, as a fixed smooth function with |∇φ_m| ≤ c_{2.24}/a_m, the same in both runs (balaban_proofs/BP_COUPLING_PROFILES.md #4.41-1-2–#4.41-1-4).

      - {#4.172} *The chain.* The domains of (1.50)–(1.55) are taken within Z, the union of the class of components (LFR I p.177 l.33, (1.1)); this is Bałaban's convention (RZ). There (Ω″_{h+1})^c, (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c, and (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c stand for their intersections with Z, so U_2 and θ live in Z, and (1.53) puts U_1 on Ω″^∼_{h+1} ∪ Z^c and U_2 on (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z. The same holds for the domains of the join in (1.52): Ω″^∼_{h+1} stands for Ω″^∼_{h+1} ∪ Z^c in 𝐁₁ and its complement for (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z in 𝐁₂.

So (1) and (3) fail, with the complements taken in the whole lattice, whenever (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c ∩ Z^c ≠ ∅, and (2) whenever (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z^c ≠ ∅. - {#4.209} *The functions of the configurations.* V(Y) of (1.68)–(1.69) re-sums the old terms 𝐓 ∈ {𝐄^{(j)}, 𝐑^{(j)}, 𝐁^{(j)}} at the configurations U″_k, U^0_k, U_{1,2}, U_1, U_{k,Λ}, and U_k. These configurations are linked by (1.51), (1.54), (1.57), (1.58), and (1.61)–(1.64) (pp.370–375). The re-summation uses the identities (1.59)–(1.60) and the decoupling expansion of RG II (1.9)–(1.10), which is the fundamental theorem of calculus in the parameters s(Δ) (RG II p.4 l.2–35).
  {#4.209-0.1} LFR II cites RG II's §§1–2 as "Sects. 6, 7 [I]", and its (1.9)–(1.10) and (1.23)–(1.29) as "(6.9)–(6.10), (6.24)–(6.29) [I]" (p.372 l.16–19, p.376 l.42); RG I has §§0–5 only. Each term of (1.10) is the Cauchy integral (1.23) of one old term and is bounded through that term's bound alone (RG II (1.24)–(1.29), pp.7–8).
  {#4.209-0.2} Here 𝐓 stands for the renormalised combinations, 𝐄^{(j)}(Λ_j, ·, z) − 𝐄^{(j)}(Λ_j, 1, z) − β_jA(h_z, ·) at the points z and 𝐑^{(j)}(X, ·) − 𝐑^{(j)}(X, 1) (CRE (2.43)–(2.44)), since for these terms the re-summation "includes renormalization in the form described in the proof of Theorem 2" (p.376 l.40–41). The completions that p.377 l.22–26 adds and subtracts are single terms of the new action at U_k, so the split below applies to them at that one configuration. With them, Σ_YV(Y) is Σ_X[𝐓(X, U″_k) − 𝐓(X, U_k)] re-expanded.
  {#4.209-1} The re-summation is linear in the old terms, but the operator that re-sums them depends on the run: each term of (1.10) evaluates an old term at the run's decoupled fluctuation field, built from that run's propagators H(s), G̃(s), and H₀(s) at complex s (RG II p.3 l.30–37, (1.23)). So the two runs' V(Y), which (1.68) (p.377 l.10–14) bounds with the weight exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), differ by the parts (i) and (ii) below at the chain's configurations and by the part (iii) of the decoupled propagators.
  {#4.209-2} The contour of the parameter t_□ in (1.23) is the circle 1/|t_□| = 8B₀C₁e^{16κ₁}α₂^{−1}g_k|B| of RG II (1.22) (p.7). It is a function of g_k|B| and Bałaban's constants, so at equal B and g_k the two runs use the same circle. The derivative at t_□ = 0 that (1.23) represents does not depend on the radius, so where the runs' g_k differ the smaller radius serves both, with the larger 1/|t_□| in (1.24).

    - {#4.247} *The re-summation as a function of the chain.* The regions that the terms of V(Y) read, the cubes □₀ of (1.59) and the domains Y_4 of (1.61)–(1.65), lie in Y by the nesting Y = Y_4 (LFR II p.376 l.39), Y_4 ⊇ Y_1 ⊇ X (p.373 l.15–17, p.374 l.33), and X ⊇ Y_0 ⊇ □₀ for the second-stage terms (p.372 l.17, p.373 l.10–15). V(Y) depends on U_k restricted to Y and on the fields A, B, and V″ localised in Y (p.377 l.7–8), and its bounds (1.68)–(1.69) are on Ũ^c_k(Y, α̃₀, α̃₁) (p.377 l.8–19). The shared fields A, B, and V″ are equal in the two runs (for A, the next item).
      - {#4.248} *The fluctuation fields A.* Bałaban's A of p.377 l.7 is "the system of the fluctuation fields {A_{j−1}}" (CRE (2.23), p.258 l.47–48), the second argument of the boundary terms 𝐁_k(U″_k, A) + 𝐁″_k(U″_k, A) of (1.49) (p.369 l.14), which are re-summed into V(Y) (p.372 l.21, l.30–31, p.373 l.10). The 𝐁-terms depend on U_k and A restricted to X and are invariant under the gauge transformations of 𝐔, 𝐉, and A, with 𝐉 and A transformed in the adjoint (CRE (2.41), p.261 l.58–62). The 𝐄- and 𝐑-terms do not depend on A.
        - {#4.249} On the component Z of the 𝐑-operation the A_j with h ≤ j ≤ k − 1 are integrated inside the 𝐑-operation, by LFR I's preliminary integrations (LFR I (1.25), p.182 l.25–33; (1.60)–(1.62), p.188 l.50–p.189 l.6; (1.71), p.192 l.28–35), before V(Y) is formed; that integration produces 𝐁″_k. Bałaban keeps the notation A, since A″_k "has the form (2.23) [III], with some new boundary terms only" (LFR I p.182 l.23–25). So the A of V(Y) is the remaining system.
          {#4.249-1} Its A_j are integrated by the postponed operations, 𝕋_h(Z_h) in (1.71) and the 𝐓^{(j)} on Z_{j+1} ∩ Ω_{j+1} of the other regions (CRE (2.20)–(2.21), p.258 l.19–31), outside V(Y). N₀, h, Z″_j, and Ω″_j of LFR I (1.10)–(1.12) are the same in both runs, since R_j = R̄(K − j) and N = N̄(K − k) in both (the Cauchy note's #CP.13 and (M) of its §2), so the remaining system is the same set of variables in both runs.
          {#4.249-2} Each A_j is a variable on the scale-j lattice, which at the shared scale j is the same lattice in both runs. The operator C that removes the δ-functions is determined by the sequence {Ω_j} (CRE p.267 l.40–44), and a matched pair has the same sequences of domains at the shared scales.
        - {#4.250} Run B's extra step has Ω_1 = Λ_1 = T in a matched pair ((M) of the Cauchy note's §2), so it postpones no fluctuation variable.
        - {#4.251} So the two runs' systems A are the same variables on the same sets with the same Lebesgue measure, as in the Cauchy note's §6.2, and their matching is the identity. V^B(Y)[c] below takes A as a further argument, with the same real value in both runs, like B and V″.

Its Jacobian is a constant, which cancels in the ratio of the Wilson loop expectation.
        - {#4.253} Both runs' 𝐁-terms are read at real A in the intersection of the two runs' supports of the restrictions |A_j| < g_j^{−1}δ_j (LFR I (1.8)–(1.9)). The rest of either support is a difference of the χ-functions, a run-dependent ingredient of the Cauchy note's §6.2.

The run differences of the postponed operations that integrate the remaining A, through Δ^{(j)}, C^{(j)}, χ, and z^{(j)}, are those of the Cauchy note's §6.2 and §10.

So each of these quantities moves by ≤ C_p|t|σ_c(x) times its scale factor, with C_p ≥ 4 a constant of B₀, c_K, and the constants c̄_e, c_W, C_r, and C_ℒ′ of #4.352.
    - {#4.463} The currents are frozen along the configuration line of (ii) and move only in its current part, by ΔJ_c, whose room and bound at the real members are those of #4.335.

    {#4.464} Each move other than the current is therefore ≤ C_p|t|σ_c(x) times its scale factor. So, the currents being moved separately, ϱ(x) ≥ c_ρα_m at the real points x of the layer m, with {#D.c_ρ} c_ρ := min(1/(4(1 + β₀)C_p), 2B₃c₂/(1 + β₀)², c_𝔯M/(2C_{K₂})), the last two for #4.377–#4.377-1 and #4.312-1. Then each move is at most ¼ of its threshold, and the joint line stays in the space at the thresholds α̃′ for |t| ≤ 1/r(Y).
  - {#4.465} *The choice β = 1/8.* Each of the 119 bare β of CRE, LFR I, and LFR II (29 on 10 pages of CRE, 59 on 11 of LFR I, and 31 on 7 of LFR II) is of one of the following kinds.
    - {#4.466} The upper bounds hold at 1/8: LFR I p.182 l.17 (0 < β ≤ ½), p.191 l.34–35 and p.198 l.16 (β ≤ 1/4), p.199 l.13 (¾ < 1 − β), p.200 l.22–23 (21/8 ≤ 3(1 − β/2) and ≤ 4(1 − β/2)), p.200 l.28 and l.39 (room 1 − β), p.187 l.25–31 (β ≤ ½), and LFR II p.376 l.5–6 ((1 − β)L ≥ 1 + 3β at L ≥ 2).
    - {#4.467} RG I lies outside this count. Its class parameter, written β_I as in the Cauchy note, enters the margins of its Lemma 4 (pp.275–280), and the Cauchy note fixes {#D.β_I} β_I := 2^{−7} (its #C5.26), within the bound β_I ≤ 1/4 of its §5. Its upper bounds hold there at L ≥ 2: (1 + 7β_I)L^{−2} ≤ 1 (p.279 l.28, "for β not too large") and (1 + 8β_I)L^{−2} ≤ 1 (p.280 l.18), which are at most 11/16 and ¾ for β_I ≤ 1/4 and L = 2. Its other restrictions, the upper bounds on α₀ and α₁ of p.278 l.46 and l.64 (#4.476), are choices of α₀ and α₁ made after β_I.
    - {#4.468} The steps that need β not too small need only β > 0 with another constant chosen after it: κ large at LFR II p.389 l.12 (βκ ≥ 6·2^d), and LFR II p.389 l.39 and p.388 l.34; R large at LFR I p.184 l.4 (B₃e^{−2δM₂R_j}22d² < β/10); the gains (1 + cβ)κ of LFR I p.192 l.11, CRE p.262 l.27–28, and LFR II pp.376–391; and the margin α₃ of RG I p.280, proportional to β, through the thresholds of kind γ small. These choices are made after β.
    - {#4.469} The steps homogeneous in β hold for every β: LFR I (1.31) (p.184 l.8–9, at L² > 2), and p.186 l.42–p.187 l.13, where the small factors are chosen as αβ (p.186 l.42) and the step needs 8α ≤ 1 (p.187 l.13).
    - {#4.470} CRE p.276 l.30 enlarges the class by 1 + β, and the definitions of CRE p.261 l.15–37 and LFR I pp.181–182 and pp.186–191 carry β as a parameter.
    - {#4.471} The other letters β of these pages are other constants: the exponent of Theorem 2 (CRE p.263 l.16–42, p.281 l.45, p.283 l.28–32, p.284 l.15), the β-function (CRE p.255 l.52, p.282 l.43), the coupling parameter of CRE p.246 l.17–18, β′ of CRE (2.6)–(2.9), and the exponent of LFR II p.357 l.10, where any β > 0 holds.
  - {#4.472} The room at complex points. The class norms of the Cauchy note's #C8.2.1–#C8.2.7 and #C8.6.1–#C8.6.29-1 are taken on its norm classes at the radii r = α′/2 = α/(8B₃): d_j on the evaluation set ℰ_j(X; r) of the norm class 𝒫_j(X; r) (its #C5.8–#C5.8-1), as the supremum over the literal points whose orbits lie in 𝒫_j(X; r), Δ being constant on these orbits (its #C5.8-2), and the norms d^R_j of the 𝐑-differences on the same sets (its #C8.2.6).
    {#4.472-0} The norms b_i of the 𝐁-terms, which carry no age factor and are derived at every point of their classes (#4.595-1, #4.621-1), are taken on the classes themselves, and the bounds of (LF-2) on the norm classes (#4.556, #4.559-2). A bound derived on a class holds on its norm class where the class contains it: run A's class does (the Cauchy note's #C5.5-8). CRE's class Ũ^c_k(Y₄, α̃₀′/2, α̃₁′/2) contains the points over which the class norms are evaluated at complex data, the callers' points (R1) (#4.472-1, #4.521.6-1).
      {#4.472-0-1} The real backgrounds of the support lie in the norm classes (#4.460), so every use at real configurations is unchanged.
    {#4.472-1} The class norms are evaluated only at run A's configurations, in (i). At complex points they are evaluated only at the members at the callers' data of the fluctuation integral on the margin ball of the Cauchy note's #C8.2.2, at the composites over them, and at the comparison configurations c̃ over them. There both runs' members satisfy their classes on X^∼ (Bałaban's representation for U_k and Proposition 9 for the others, #4.521), so they are points of the kind (R1) of the Cauchy note's #C5.8, and the c̃ are points (R3) (#4.454).
    {#4.472-1.1} (LF-2) at complex V enters the Cauchy note's recursion through the 𝐑-differences, whose norms are taken on ℰ_j (its #C8.2.6), so its form linear in d_j is needed at the literal points of ℰ only (#0.1).
    {#4.472-1.2} At the other complex points of the members, U^0_k and U_k on Ũ^c_k(Y₄, α̃′/2), the callers' U_k at the other data and the members at the arguments of the kinds (R2), (N), and (R3) among them, (i) is read through RΔ on 𝒫_j(X; r⁺) with the size parameter d⁺ of #4.454.11-2, at the generations m/2 < j ≤ m at which the lift is formed (#4.219-1), as in #4.454.11–#4.454.12, the factor d_j that (LF-2) needs in the Cauchy note's recursion being supplied by #0.1's weighted-norm bound (#4.454.40-1).
    {#4.472-2} The polydiscs of #4.454 use d_j at their points of the kind (R3) (#4.454). The far domains at W in (i) do not use the norm d_j, only the plain class bound of Δ, in which d_j(X) is CRE's size of the domain X (#4.233-0.2, #4.233-1).
    {#4.472-2.1} #4.503 puts U^0_k and U_k in run A's half of the norm class; the lift half is #4.514 at the members for n ≥ n₀′, #4.234 at the decoupled configurations, and #4.550 at the composites. The joint line also uses the inputs of (ii) at the real points of the line, which #4.505–#4.513 carry to the complex points, and the inequality (W-δ) of (iii) for the split of each V(Y).
    {#4.472-3} The class bound (5.1c) at run A's configurations is derived, at real and at complex points, as follows: at the near domains satisfying (N) in the Cauchy note's #C5.14–#C5.29, and at the others through (RΔ^c-T); at the near domains at ∂Y_i through 𝒮_z at the data of a member and its continuation, and through the direct comparison of #4.454 at the decoupled and lifted data (#4.450-1). At complex points the membership it needs is derived in #4.454 from the Cauchy note's #C5.22–#C5.34.
    - {#4.473} *Bałaban's Statements at the Reduced Thresholds.* Bałaban's statements hold at the thresholds α_{i,j}/μ for the ten values μ ∈ {½, 1, 4B₃, 8B₃, 32B₃²L³, 8B₃C_{Q*}, 256B₃²L³, 64B₃C_{Q*}, 2^{13}B₃²L³, μ_mem} that the notes use, once C₀ and C₁ are at least λ_Q = max{1, 4B₃, 8B₃, 2^{13}B₃²L³, 64B₃C_{Q*}, C_mem} times his lower bounds, and so at every μ ≤ λ_Q, as #4.460–#4.464 takes them.
        {#4.473-0.1} Here {#D.μ_mem} μ_mem := 8B₃/C_mem ≤ 2, with C_mem of #4.532, is the value at which #4.531–#4.549 places the members' complex parts at the radii r (the values 256B₃²L³ and 64B₃C_{Q*} place the members in the class at real points for #4.454, and 2^{13}B₃²L³ places U_{k,Λ} and U_1 there; the age factor needs no room, RΔ being run at the radii (9/8)r at the values 8μ/9, and the membership at complex points is derived in #4.454 from the Cauchy note's #C5.22–#C5.34).
        {#4.473-1} At μ = ½, used for the margin of the X_s representation (the W-δ note's #W12.177–#W12.201-7), the lower bounds hold a fortiori and the upper bounds hold for γ small, and the same holds at μ_mem where it is below 1, μ_mem being a constant of d and L. The construction does not involve C₀ and C₁, and each of his restrictions on them is of one of three kinds, each of which holds at C₀/μ and C₁/μ. The uses of C₀, C₁, and the thresholds in CRE, LFR I, LFR II, RG I, and RG II are listed below.
      - {#4.474} *The construction.* In CRE, C₀ and C₁ occur, directly or through the thresholds, only in (2.28) (p.259 l.40–50), in the spaces of p.261 (l.5–37, l.60), in (3.43) (p.276 l.24–31), and in the remark of p.262 l.43–46.
        {#4.474-0.0} In LFR I the thresholds occur only in the spaces (1.64)–(1.69) (p.190 l.8–p.191 l.21, p.195 l.22–24), among them the domain of (1.70) (p.192 l.9), and in the remarks of p.191 l.34–43 and p.192 l.16–22. The C₀ of (1.70) (p.192 l.11) is the constant of a bound, and (1.70) at the full thresholds restricts to the smaller spaces, so it needs no identification. The α of LFR I pp.186–187 and pp.198–200 is an absolute constant (p.187 l.31, p.198 l.27, p.199 l.16, p.200 l.21), and the α₀ of p.200 l.35 is the exponent log L₀²/log L.
        {#4.474-0.0-1} In LFR II the thresholds occur only in the extensions of p.358 l.27–29, p.366 l.25–28, and p.367 l.46–48, in the spaces of (1.65) (p.375 l.17–35), in the analyticity domains of V and 𝐑′^{(k)} (p.377 l.8–9, p.390 l.11–12), which at the full thresholds restrict to the smaller spaces, in the bounds (1.47) (p.368 l.23–27) and p.379 l.31, and in the remark on these bounds of p.375 l.36–38. The α of LFR II p.377 l.11–14 and pp.388–391 is the constant of a bound.
        {#4.474-0.1} The cutoffs are ε_j = g_jA₀(log g_j^{−2})^{p₀} (CRE (2.4)), δ_k = g_k(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_k) (CRE p.265 l.39) in (3.16), and ϑ_k (LFR I p.193 l.21–23). The number of usual steps is N = R_j (LFR II p.384 l.17, LFR I p.177 l.25–33, N > N₀ by p.179 l.10), with R_j the power of L of the Cauchy note's #CP.13. None of these involves C₀ or C₁. So the effective actions, the expansions, and the 𝐑-operation are the same for all values of C₀ and C₁.
        {#4.474-1} The extensions are given by explicit substitution formulas, which do not involve C₀ or C₁ either: RG I (3.13) replaces J_{k+1} by 𝐉 and U_{k+1} by 𝐔 in (3.11)–(3.12) (p.272), (3.15) defines 𝐇_j and 𝐇_k by VAR (179)–(180) with 𝐔 and 𝐉 in their operators (p.273), and LFR II constructs its extensions "by replacing" the real arguments by the complex ones (p.358, p.366), with 𝐀₀ = 𝐇_{k,Λ}((1/i)log M^·(U₀(𝐔))) by VAR Sect. G (p.367 l.47–48).
        {#4.474-1-1} So the extensions at smaller thresholds are the restrictions of those at larger ones. The real configurations alone would fix an extension only on the graph 𝐉 = J(𝐔), since 𝐉 is an independent variable; the formulas fix it everywhere.
      - {#4.475} *Upper bounds.* The following are upper bounds on the thresholds:
        - {#4.476} RG I's restrictions O(1)Mα₁ ≤ β (p.278 l.46), (4B₃²O(1)M)²α₀ ≤ β (p.278 l.64), B₃³O(1)²M²α₀ < β (p.279 l.12), Mα₀ and Mα₁ small (p.275 l.28), α₀ and α₁ much smaller than the α′ of the domain of 𝐏^{(k)} (p.270 l.2–3), and α₂ and α₃ sufficiently small (p.279 l.47–49, p.280 l.31);
        - {#4.477} RG II's (LM)⁴α₀, (LM)⁴α₁ ≤ 1 (p.20 l.23), its α′ much bigger than α (p.6, p.10, p.15), its R₁ with the factor O(α₀ + α₁) (p.16), and α₅‖C‖ < ½ (p.17);
        - {#4.478} the smallness of LFR II (1.47) and of the bound of p.379 l.31;
        - {#4.479} the parts α²ε of the step statement of LFR I p.191 and of LFR II (1.65) (#4.488).

        {#4.480} At α_{i,j} = g_jC_i(log g_j^{−2})^{q_i} they hold for γ small at fixed C₀ and C₁, γ depending on all other constants (RG I Theorem 3, p.264 l.39–41), and they are weaker at smaller thresholds. In (1.47) the smallness comes from L^{−N} with N = R_j, and L^{−R_j} ≤ (log g_j^{−2})^{−ν} for every ν when γ is small, since R_j ≥ (log g_j^{−2})^r (the Cauchy note's #CP.14). So (1.47) bounds neither C₁ nor q₁.

So q₁ = q₀ > p₀ + 3r is taken, as at #4.420-1.1 (#T1.2), with C₁/C₀ large enough for these two relations, as in the W-δ note's #W8.13 and #W12.192 (C₁ = λ_RC₀); #4.290-1.1 uses q₁ = q₀.

Its condition c₂ ≤ c_* involves B₃⁺ (the Cauchy note's #C5.37-18), which is fixed after M (#C5.37-10), so that condition is imposed at stage 3′, after M (the table's #T3.13). α₂ divides by μ with α₀ and α₁;

      - {#4.488} *Mixed statements.* The step statement of LFR I p.191 l.39–43 is proved as (1.44)–(1.52) (p.191 l.42–44), where each step spends a part αβ2^{−(j−i)} of the margin of the space against the shift of the fluctuation field (p.186 l.42–p.187 l.31), and LFR II (1.65) is proved as LFR I (1.89) with ε_j replaced by α_{0,j} (p.375 l.24–27).
