Each part is listed under its kind.
      - {#4.489} *Lower bounds against sizes free of C₀ and C₁.* The following are lower bounds on the thresholds against sizes that do not involve C₀ and C₁:
        - {#4.490} the parts B₃δ′_k < αε of the step statement of LFR I p.191 and of LFR II (1.65) (#4.488);
        - {#4.491} RG I's ε₀ small (p.263), and ε₁ small against α₂ (p.273 l.13, p.280 l.49), with the radius α₂/3 and the factor α₂^{−1} of (3.17) against ε₁ (p.273);
        - {#4.492} RG II's 4B₀C₁e^{16κ₁}ε₁ ≤ ¼α₂ (p.7 l.9) and α₂^{−1}ε₁ (p.8), with C₁ there an absolute constant (RG II p.9 l.48); the constant C₃ of RG II p.20 l.24–25 carries RG II's own α₄ and α₆ (p.16, p.18), not the thresholds;
        - {#4.493} CRE (3.43) (p.276 l.29–31), whose enlarged background factor no note uses (#4.600) and whose fluctuation factor enters #4.595 only through its support, its radius C₁p₁(g_k) replaced by 2r^χ_k (#T11.12-2-1), so it puts no condition on the thresholds;
        - {#4.494} the membership of the real backgrounds in the spaces, derived at the reduced thresholds in #4.460–#4.464 from #3.70.

        {#4.495} The sizes are ε_j, δ_k, ϑ_k, and the fluctuation shifts. These restrictions are what "C₀, C₁ are sufficiently large" (CRE p.259 l.50) provides: each holds for all C_i above a lower bound K_i that is fixed by the constants chosen before C₀ and C₁.
      - {#4.496} *The order of the constants.* B₃ depends on d and L only (VAR Theorem 1, p.279 l.28), C_{Q*} (the Cauchy note's #C5.6-5) on d and L only, and C_mem = 4O(1)(1+β₀)²B₃(1 + C_m) with C_m a constant of δ₀(d, L) (#4.532). So λ_Q is fixed before C₀ and C₁, and C_i ≥ λ_QK_i is a choice that "sufficiently large" allows. Each of the three kinds then holds at C_i/μ:
        - {#4.497} the lower bounds, since C_i/μ ≥ K_i, as λ_Q ≥ μ for each value μ of #4.473 and each value 8μ/9: every value is at most one of λ_Q's six entries (32B₃²L³ and 256B₃²L³ below 2^{13}B₃²L³, 8B₃C_{Q*} below 64B₃C_{Q*}, μ_mem ≤ 2 ≤ 4B₃, and ½ below 1), and 8μ/9 ≤ μ;
        - {#4.498} the homogeneous relations, as at C_i;
        - {#4.499} the upper bounds, for γ at most the least of the values γ(C₀/μ, C₁/μ) over the ten values μ of #4.473 and the ten values 8μ/9 at which RΔ is run at the radii (9/8)r (#4.454, #4.473).

        {#4.500} N = R_j and the cutoffs are the same at every value μ of #4.473 and every value 8μ/9, as at Bałaban's thresholds μ = 1. So his statements hold at the thresholds α_{i,j}/μ, with α₂ and α₃ divided by μ with them, and his bounds at his thresholds restrict to these smaller classes.
      - {#4.501} *What it covers.* This covers the common polydisc α′_{i,j} = α_{i,j}/(4B₃) of the Cauchy note's #C5.5, its norm class r_{i,j} = α_{i,j}/(8B₃), the current bound r_{0,j}/C_{Q*} of the norm class, and the radii r_{i,j} of its class condition (b) (#C5.11), and r⁺_{i,j} = (9/8)r_{i,j} for RΔ at the moved points. In particular the inclusions that the Cauchy note's norms use hold there: RG I Lemma 4 (p.280, (3.53)) with α₃/μ, the class at the next scale (p.262 l.26–30, p.279 l.22–23), and (1.65) with α̃₀′/2 and α̃₁′/2 in both of its spaces.
    - {#4.502} *The Margin.* The Cauchy note's #C8.2.2 runs RΔ^c at the radii r of the norm class through the composites of its (5.1c𝐀), with the margin m_k, the fluctuation radius at which the fluctuation part of (I.3.28) satisfies (I.3.31) at the radii r, and the cutoff ball of (3.16) inside it with the ratio T₀ ≥ 2 (#T3.27; the Cauchy note's #C8.2.2-42, #C8.2.2-75–#C8.2.2-77). T₀ ≥ 2 uses q₀ > p₀, the choice of #4.460-0.1.
    - {#4.503} *The Room.* At a point (𝐔, 𝐉) of Ũ^c_k(Y₄, α̃₀′/2, α̃₁′/2), (1.65) at these thresholds puts U^0_k, with its current, in Ũ″^c_k(Y₁, α̃₀′/2, α̃₁′/2); the other members of 𝒞 are as at real points (#4.403, on LFR I (1.64)–(1.69)). The old terms are analytic on Ũ″^c_k(Y₁, α̃₀, α̃₁) with Bałaban's bounds (p.375 l.29–35).
      {#4.503-1} So each conditioned quantity of LFR I (1.64)–(1.68) is below ½λ_β times its threshold, and the room in each condition is at least ¼ of its threshold, as at real points (#4.460-1.2). For U_k itself, the point (𝐔, 𝐉), this holds directly, since Ũ^c_k(Y₄, α̃₀′/2, α̃₁′/2) imposes the conditions at the points of Y.
    - {#4.504} *The Alignment Field at Complex Points.* Let z ↦ (𝐔(z), 𝐉(z)) be the line of #4.559, with (𝐔(i), 𝐉(i)) = (𝐔, 𝐉), and A(z) the alignment field of run A's configuration of the chain at the point z of the line against Ũ(z). For a point x and a complex-linear functional ℓ of norm 1, {#D.f(z)} f(z) := ℓ(a_{j(x)}A(z)(x)) is analytic for |z| < 25 (#4.563). Let d̄′(x) be the coarse-side bound d̄(x) of #4.314 with ε₁′ (#4.560-0) for ε₁.
      {#4.504-1} The real points z of the line with |z| < 25 are regular with 2ε₁′ for ε₁, by the count of #4.560 with 26 for 25 and (T-c), so |f(z)| ≤ 2d̄′(x) ≤ 2C_U(M)ε₁′ there.   - {#4.557} *Lemma (Two Constants).* Let 1 < 𝔳 < 𝔳₁, let 𝔣 be analytic on |z| < 𝔳₁ with |𝔣| ≤ 𝔎 there, and let |𝔣| ≤ 𝔨 on the real segment (−𝔳, 𝔳), with 0 < 𝔨 ≤ 𝔎. Then |𝔣(z)| ≤ 𝔨^{𝔢(z)}𝔎^{1−𝔢(z)} for |z| < 𝔳, with {#D.𝔢(z)} 𝔢(z) := 1 − (2/π)|arg((𝔳 + z)/(𝔳 − z))|. For {#D.𝔳} 𝔳 := 24 and {#D.𝔳₁} 𝔳₁ := 25, |𝔣(z)| ≤ 𝔨^{15/16}𝔎^{1/16} for |z| ≤ 1.
  - {#4.558} *Proof.* On the upper half-disc {#D.D₊} D₊ := {|z| < 𝔳, Im z > 0}, {#D.𝔴} 𝔴 := (𝔳 + z)/(𝔳 − z) maps D₊ onto the open first quadrant, the segment onto the positive real axis, and the semicircle onto the positive imaginary axis. So {#D.𝔥} 𝔥 := 1 + (2i/π)Log 𝔴 is analytic on D₊, and Re 𝔥 = 𝔢 is 1 on the segment and 0 on the semicircle. Let {#D.𝔉} 𝔉 := 𝔣𝔨^{−𝔥}𝔎^{𝔥−1}. Then |𝔉| = |𝔣|𝔨^{−𝔢}𝔎^{𝔢−1} is bounded on D₊, continuous on its closure except at ±𝔳, and ≤ 1 on its boundary there.
    {#4.558-1} For 𝔭 > 0 let {#D.𝔉_𝔭} 𝔉_𝔭 := 𝔉·((𝔳² − z²)/(4𝔳²))^𝔭, with the principal power, since Re(𝔳² − z²) > 0 on D₊. Then |𝔉_𝔭| ≤ 1 on the boundary and 𝔉_𝔭 → 0 at ±𝔳, so |𝔉_𝔭| ≤ 1 on D₊ by the maximum modulus principle, and 𝔭 → 0 gives |𝔣| ≤ 𝔨^𝔢𝔎^{1−𝔢} on D₊. On the lower half-disc the same follows for z ↦ conj(𝔣(z̄)), since 𝔢(z̄) = 𝔢(z), and on the segment it is the hypothesis.
      {#4.558-1.1} For |z| ≤ 1, |arg(𝔳 ± z)| ≤ arcsin(1/𝔳), so 𝔢(z) ≥ 1 − (4/π)arcsin(1/𝔳), which exceeds 15/16 at 𝔳 = 24: arcsin x = arctan(x/(1 − x²)^{1/2}) ≤ x/(1 − x²)^{1/2} and π > 3 give (4/π)arcsin(1/24) < (4/3)575^{−1/2} < 1/16, as 575 > (64/3)² = 4096/9. Since 𝔨 ≤ 𝔎, 𝔨^𝔢𝔎^{1−𝔢} = 𝔎(𝔨/𝔎)^𝔢 ≤ 𝔨^{15/16}𝔎^{1/16}. For 𝔨 > 𝔎 the bound 𝔨^{15/16}𝔎^{1/16} ≥ 𝔎 holds trivially, so the Lemma applies with any real-segment bound 𝔨.

With d_{al} ≤ C_U(M)ε₁′ and ε/a_n ≤ 1, this is the bound C_y(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁′², with {#D.C_y(M)} C_y(M) := C_bd(1 + C_U(M))C_U(M) + C_b, and g_{j(x)} ≤ (1 + β₀)ḡ ≤ 1 for ḡ small (#4.41-1-1).

So at the point of the class, z = i (#4.559), Lemma (Two Constants) (#4.557) gives |d_y| ≤ C_dc(M)g_{j(x)}^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{5(1−ε₀)/16}ε₁′², with {#D.C_dc(M)} C_dc(M) := max(C_y(M), 2C^c_act).

Through the weights they enter linearly, as A(w^B − w^A, ·), w^X the action's weight (#4.160) at run X's couplings (#4.41-0), so on the class they are bounded directly by the weight difference times the disc bound C^c_actε₁′² of an unweighted density (#4.563-3). Through the data exp(ig_kB) they enter through a data derivative times |g^A_k − g^B_k||B|, which Cauchy's estimate bounds on the class on the data domain of U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(·), the data V′ of VAR Sect. G with |V′ − 1| < C_{V′}ε₁′ (#4.561.1-2), on which (T-c) gives U″_k analytic.
      {#4.567-0} The supremum in Cauchy's estimate is given by the bounds of #4.563-2–#4.563-3-1, which use only U^r and (19) at ε₂, and Proposition 9 at C₁ = C_{V′} gives (19) at ε₂ on this whole domain.

A move W_d of a datum with |W_d − 1| ≤ ρ_V := ½C_{V′}ε₁′ ≤ ¼ ((T-c), #4.561-1.2) gives |W_dV′ − 1| ≤ ρ_V|V′| + |V′ − 1| ≤ (9/16 + ¼)C_{V′}ε₁′ < C_{V′}ε₁′, so the radius is ≥ ½C_{V′}ε₁′ in |W_d − 1|, and ≥ e^{−1/4}ρ_V in the exponent X of W_d = e^{iX}, by |e^{iX} − 1| ≤ |X|e^{|X|}. Both bounds are per point of the support of the action's weight, which lies in Z (#4.160), keep the real form of #4.168, linear in the coupling differences, and are absorbed as the real ones are.
        {#4.567-1-1} The radius persists along the coupling segment. There the data exp(ig′B) differ from the class's exp(ig_kB) by e^{iX}, X = (g′ − g_k)B. By #C5.7-3–#C5.7-8, g′/g_k ∈ [(2/3)^{1/2}, 2^{1/2}], so |g′ − g_k| ≤ g_k and |X| ≤ g_kb_k ≤ ε′_k/25 ≤ ε₁′/100 (#D.ε′_k, #4.560.1-1).

Then |V′_t| < 1.15 under C_{V′}ε₁′ ≤ ½. So ρ_V|V′_t| + |V′_t − 1| < (0.575 + 0.3)C_{V′}ε₁′ < C_{V′}ε₁′, and the radius ρ_V holds at every coupling of the segment.

Through log d and E_k(Λ) the couplings enter by the Cauchy note's §8.6 (#C8.6.3–#C8.6.7), E_k(Λ) not depending on the configuration; at a point of the class these read U_0 and d only through Bałaban's bounds of LFR II pp.357–358 with (1.10)–(1.11) (#T11.30, #T11.30-0), which hold there by #4.567-3.
      {#4.567-3} Bałaban states them for G^c-valued 𝐔 in U^c_k(Z, α_{0,k}, α_{1,k}) with ε_k replaced by O(α_{0,k} + α_{1,k}) (#T11.30-0), d and U_0 reading 𝐔 only on Z ((1.1)–(1.3), #T11.30). The class is the norm class (#4.472, #4.559-2), so the point is a pair in the norm class 𝒫_k(X; r) (#T11.14) of the domain X of the term read, which contains the component Z whose d is read: a domain Y of a factor V(Y) contains the components of Z^∼ that it meets (p.377 l.6–7), and a polymer of LFR II (1.91), the connected domain that its X_{j_h} and its domains Y determine, contains them (p.388 l.14).
        {#4.567-3-1} So its orbit contains a pair whose restriction to X satisfies (i)–(iii) of run A's U^c_k(X, r_{0,k}, r_{1,k}) (#C5.5-1), and its lift's orbit a pair satisfying those of run B's U^c_{k+1}(X, e^{2β_I}r_{0,k}, e^{2β_I}r_{1,k}) (#C5.5-2, #C5.6-3). These conditions are pointwise or per cube (RG I (1.11)–(1.14), p.262), so they hold on Z ⊂ X, and RG I (1.17) (p.263 l.7–17) gives (iv) on Z at 2B₃r_{0,k} = ¼α_{0,k} for run A and at 2B₃e^{2β_I}r_{0,k} < 0.4α_{0,k} for run B, as in #C5.5-6, with e^{2β_I} < 1.6 (#C5.7-3).

        {#4.567-3-3} So, at each such coupling, the restriction to Z lies in run A's U^c_k(Z, ·, ·) and the lift's in run B's U^c_{k+1}(Z, ·, ·) at that coupling's thresholds, unions of G^c-orbits (RG I p.262 l.13), each run on its own lattice at the data of the point, which are the lift's averages: M^{k+1}(ι_X𝐔) = M^k(Mι_X𝐔) = M^k(𝐔) on X^∼, by the iteration (43) of CMP98 (p.024 l.2–4) and Mι_X𝐔 = 𝐔 (#C3.2). Each point at which #C8.6.5–#C8.6.7 read d is Bałaban's denominator at such a coupling with its own cutoff (#C8.6.5-1), so his bounds apply there in his own setting.
    - {#4.568} The absorption. With the prefactors C_dc(M), max(C_F(M), 2c_4), and #4.55-0.1's 2C(M)²(1 + β₀)², g_{j(x)}^{−2}ε₁′² and N_k carry factors of the kind of the result of (c): linear in k and powers of log g_k^{−2}, with k + 1 ≤ 8n + j(C) and log g_k^{−2} bounded as in #4.55-0.1, ε₁′ being g_k times a power of log g_k^{−2} (#4.562-1), with the constants of ε′_k (C_c, β₀ and CRE's in α̂_i, b_k's A₁ and M₀, and those of p₀ and p₁). So #4.55-1-1 at s = 5/16 bounds the changes of #4.565-1 and #4.566 on the class by C_hθ̃^n per point, with θ̃ unchanged.

    {#4.569} So the per-point bounds of (b) and (c) on the class, which the complex version of the Lemma of the Cauchy note's §8.6 needs for d, and the bounds of the five actions and of the form in 𝐂_k − W_ext, are derived on the class. The variation (ii) of V(Y) at the complex points is bounded in #4.553–#4.553-3 and #4.520-2.

{#4.571} (e) *The Carried Boundary Terms.* In (e), k is the fluctuation step, and {#D.k_s} k_s := K − j(C) is the stopping scale of the Cauchy note's §8.2, the k of §1, which sets the thresholds k_s/8 and k_s/4.
- {#4.572} *The objects.* A boundary term 𝐁^{(i)} of CRE (2.40)–(2.42) is localised in X ∈ 𝐃_i with X ∩ Ω_i ≠ ∅ and X ∩ Z_i^∼ ≠ ∅, and is bounded by B₀exp(−κd_i(X)) on its class (p.261 l.47–66). After the step that creates it, it is a fixed function, evaluated at the later backgrounds: the form 𝐁^{(i)}(U_k, …) of (2.40), with 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) remaining in the action (3.25). Here Z_i = Λ_i^c (p.255 l.25), and Γ_m = Ω_m^{(m)} ∖ Ω_{m+1}^{(m)} is the layer of the scale m (p.255 l.15–16).
  {#4.572-1} The class norm of its two-run difference is b_i, the smallest number with |𝐁^{B,(i)}(X) − 𝐁^{A,(i)}(X)| ≤ b_iB₀exp(−κd_i(X)) on the class: the norm of the Cauchy note's §8.2 with B₀ in place of E₀. The class is the intersection of the two runs' classes Ũ^c_i(X, α̃₀, α̃₁), on which both runs' terms are analytic and bounded.
    {#4.572-1.1} The thresholds (2.28) of the layer n carry each run's own coupling there, g^A_n and g^B_{n+1}, with g^B_{n+1}/g^A_n = (1 + (g^A_n)²δ_n)^{−1/2} (δ_n of #C1.1-4) and (g^A_n)²|δ_n| ≤ ½ for γ small (#C5.7-3). As d log(g(log g^{−2})^q)/d log g = 1 − 2q/log g^{−2} ∈ (0, 1] for γ small and |log(1 + x)| ≤ 2|x| for |x| ≤ ½, the two runs' thresholds at the layer n differ by a factor in [e^{−(g^A_n)²|δ_n|}, e^{(g^A_n)²|δ_n|}]. So the intersection contains either run's class with the thresholds of each layer n scaled by e^{−(g^A_n)²|δ_n|} ≥ 1 − (g^A_n)²|δ_n|.
  {#4.572-2} By (2.47) (p.263 l.50–p.264 l.8), the part 𝐁^{(i,m)} of the generation i on the layer Γ_m, m < i, carries the factor 2^{−(i−m)}, from exp(−d_i(X)). So the generations i ≥ m sum to ≤ 2B₁ per point of Γ_m, and their differences to ≤ 2B₁max_{i≥m}b_i. The generations i < m on Γ_m are not in (2.47); they carry the inward weight of #4.657.
- {#4.573} *Where they enter.* At a fluctuation step k, 𝐁_k enters CRE (3.26) only through its first expression: as the integrand 𝐁_k(U_k(…)) − 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) of the t-integral, and, multiplied by t, in the measure (3.27) of that integral (p.271 l.7–8, l.22). The output of that expression goes into 𝐁^{(k+1)} only (p.271 l.29–31, p.279 l.16). The s-integral and the logarithm in (3.26) are taken at t = 0 (p.271 l.14–15), so the 𝐁-terms do not enter the step's 𝐄- and 𝐑-outputs; 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) remains in the action as a frozen function.
  {#4.573-0.1} Two more expressions of the t-integrand go into the boundary terms only (p.277 l.10–17): the coupling term A(g_k^{−2}(·) − g_k^{−2}, ·), localised in Z_k, and V^{(k)}(S_{k+1}), the expressions above expanded in the perturbative terms of (1.22), each with a localisation in S_{k+1}.
  {#4.573-0.2} At an 𝐑-operation, the old terms whose domains meet a component Z belong to the first part of (1.49), which is integrated with Z (LFR II p.369 l.28–30). The terms disjoint from Z are expanded around the new background U_k. There 𝐓(X, U_k) stays as a frozen function (taken at U_k, p.373 l.5–6), and the brackets 𝐓(X, exp iη𝐇″_k(g_kB)U^0_k) − 𝐓(X, U^0_k) of (1.59)–(1.60), with their analogues along the chain of (d), give "a term which is small, and satisfies the exponential bound (2.42) [III] in d_k(Y₀)".
  {#4.573-1} Bałaban takes these "together with other terms of the first part of the effective action" (p.372 l.27–33), so they too are integrated with Z. So the 𝐑-operation carries the frozen boundary terms disjoint from the components with the factor 1.
    {#4.573-1.1} The boundary terms that it creates itself are those of the preliminary integrations of LFR I §1, localised in X ∈ 𝔻_m, for some m ≥ j + 1, with X ⊂ Ω_{m+1}^c, X ∩ Ω_m ≠ ∅, and X ∩ (Z_{j+1} ∖ Z″_{j+1}) ≠ ∅ (LFR I (1.63), p.189 l.40–47), and bounded by C₀exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)) on the spaces Ũ_k^{(n)c} of pp.190–191 (LFR I (1.70), p.192 l.7–14). They are 𝔹_k^{(n)} = Σ_{i≤n}ℂ_k^{(i)}, with ℂ_k^{(n+1)} the logarithm of the integral (1.60) plus the coupling term A(1/(g_k^{(n+1)}(·))² − 1/(g_k^{(n)}(·))², U_k^{(n+1)}) (LFR I (1.61)–(1.62), p.189 l.16–30).
    {#4.573-1.2} Z_{j+1} is identified with Z_{j+1} ∩ Z (LFR I p.177 l.33–35), so these terms meet the components renormalised at the step. Where the integrations of a component end at some n, Bałaban leaves them "as a part of all boundary terms" (LFR I p.191 l.44–47), and from then on they are carried like the others. So their two-run difference at creation, #4.623–#4.650, is a source of the recursion of #4.658. The old 𝐁-terms enter the quotients of the Cauchy note's §8.6 through V(Y) of (d).
- {#4.574} *Deep terms.* A term is deep at a step i > k_s/8 if its domain contains a point of a layer ≤ k_s/8 at that step.
  - {#4.575} A boundary term of the generation i that is still carried at a later step contains a point of a layer ≤ i. Its domain X meets Z_i^∼, one layer of MR_i-cubes around Z_i (p.245 l.40–43), so X has a point y in an MR_i-cube touching Z_i. By (2.9), MR_ia_i ≤ (1 + L^{−1})MR_{i+1}a_{i+1} ≤ 2MR_{i+1}a_{i+1}, so y lies within three layers of LMR_{i+1}-cubes around Z′_i, the union of the LMR_{i+1}-cubes meeting Z_i (p.264 l.52–55). By (3.2)–(3.5), Ω_{i+1}^c ⊇ (B^{i+1}(P^1_{i+1})^c)^{∼3} ⊇ Z′_i^{∼8} (p.265 l.2, l.17–22, l.43), so y ∉ Ω_{i+1}.
    {#4.575-1} The layer of a point changes only when a component containing the point is renormalised, since an 𝐑-operation acts inside the renormalised components: its domain Λ = (Ω_{k₀+1}^{∼4})^c ∩ Z and the sets Z″_k ⊂ Λ lie in Z (LFR I p.192 l.43, p.195 l.42); then X meets that component, so the term belongs to the first part of (1.49) and is integrated with it (LFR II p.369 l.28–30). So y stays at a layer ≤ i while the term is carried.
  - {#4.576} The output domains of a step contain the domains of their inputs: at a fluctuation step the polymers of the cluster expansion are unions of the inputs' domains with further cubes (RG II p.12 l.9–11, l.23, (2.9), (2.13); CRE p.278 l.16–31), and at an 𝐑-operation the same holds for the expansions of LFR II p.387 l.40–42, p.388 l.2, l.14. So a term built from a deep input is deep, a non-deep term is built from non-deep inputs only, and by the first item a non-deep boundary term at a step > k_s/8 has a generation > k_s/8, as have its boundary inputs.
  - {#4.577} The norms D, S, and b of the Cauchy note's §8 at the steps > k_s/8 are taken over the non-deep terms. A deep term at a step j > k_s/8 has a point y at a layer ≤ k_s/8, and y ∈ Λ_j^c, since Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j ⊂ Ω_{k_s/8+1}. Let Z′ be the component of Λ_j^c containing y (LFR I p.177 l.16–17); its history reaches a layer ≤ k_s/8.
    - {#4.578} Let the term, of the generation i and with the domain X, meet a component Z ≠ Z′ renormalised at the step j > k_s/4. X is connected (RG I p.257 l.7–9), so it passes from y through Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j to Z, and crosses every layer Γ_l, k_s/8 < l < j. Bałaban's bound of exp(−d_i(X)) for a generation-i term with a point in Γ_n, ≤ 2^{−(i−1−n)} (p.264 l.2–3), gives exp(−d_i(X)) ≤ 2^{−(i−1−k_s/8)} for i > k_s/8 + 1.
      {#4.578-1} The layers i ≤ l < j cost ≥ R(j − i) π_i-cubes, and the layer j − 1 alone ≥ RL^{j−1−i} (#4.652, in the units of the step i by #4.582-1), so exp(−½δκd_i(X)) ≤ exp(−½δκRL^{j−1−i}), δ of #4.652. With ½δκR ≥ σ ≥ (d + 1)log L + 1 (#4.654–#4.655) and L^{j−1−i} ≥ j − i, this pays the L^{d(j−i)} points of the scale i in a point of the scale j up to a factor e^{−(j−i)} ≤ L^de^{−(j−1−i)}. Since j − k_s/8 > k_s/8, one of the two factors is ≤ L^de²2^{−k_s/16} at every generation.
      {#4.578-2} So the deep terms meeting Z are ≤ C_Dk̄Ē₀2^{−k_s/16} per point of Z at the scale j, with {#D.k̄} k̄ := max(k_s, j) ≥ j bounding the number of generations i ≤ j, {#D.Ē₀} Ē₀ := max(E₀, B₀, C₀^𝔹, R₁) bounding the frozen 𝐄-, 𝐑-, and 𝐁-terms and the 𝔹-terms of #4.623 as in the Cauchy note's §8.6, and C_D a constant of C_X, L, and d, C_X the Cauchy note's domain count at a point (§8.5).
      {#4.578-3} The rest of the exponent, exp(−(κ − 1 − δκ)d_i(X)), controls the sum over X as exp(−(κ − 1)d_j(X)) does in Bałaban's (2.48) (p.263 l.50–52): C_X, the sum at the rate (β/16)κ, bounds the sum at the rate κ − 1 − δκ, since (β/16)κ ≤ ½(κ − 1) ≤ κ − 1 − δκ for β ≤ ¼, δ ≤ ¼, and κ ≥ 2. Their two-run difference is ≤ twice this, by the triangle inequality. They enter ν_j of the Cauchy note's §8.6.
    - {#4.579} Otherwise the term meets no component renormalised at the step j other than Z′. If Z′ is renormalised, the term belongs to its first part and is bounded in #C8.6.24-1–#C8.6.24-2. If Z′ is of the second class, the term enters 𝐓′_k(Z′), an ingredient of Z′'s large-field operation, and stays deep with Z′ (LFR II p.378 l.8, l.20–22).
      {#4.579-1} If Z′ is not among the components renormalised at the step j (LFR I p.177 l.33), the term is carried with Z′ and stays deep. If Z′ is alive at the stopping scale, the pair is old and is bounded by the triangle inequality in the Cauchy note's §6.2. A deep term that meets a component renormalised at a step j with k_s/8 < j ≤ k_s/4 is bounded by the triangle inequality in #C8.6.24-1, which covers every component renormalised at a step ≤ k_s/4.
  - {#4.580} *Deep V(Y) in a Young Polymer.* Let a component be renormalised at the step j > k_s/4, Bałaban's k in LFR II (1.61)–(1.68), and let V(Y) be a factor of LFR II (1.91) in a polymer X′ whose components of Bałaban's Z, those that X′ contains, are all young. By LFR II p.377 l.5–8, Y ∩ Z^∼ is a union of components of Z^∼, and these lie in X′, so every point of Y ∩ Z lies at a layer > k_s/8.
    {#4.580-1} Let Y be deep, with a point y at a layer ≤ k_s/8. Then y ∉ Z, and y ∈ Λ_j^c, since Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j ⊂ Ω_{k_s/8+1}. The component W of Λ_j^c containing y is not one of the components that make up Z (LFR I p.177 l.33), so W ∩ Z = ∅. In this item the old terms' generation is i, Bałaban's j in (1.66).
    - {#4.581} *The Constituents.* V(Y) re-sums, at fixed Y = Y₄, the terms of the expansions (1.61)–(1.64) of the terms of p.373 l.10–13: the terms of the first part of (1.49) other than its first two, and the terms with the localisation domains Y₀ of (1.59)–(1.60), which contain a component of Λ^∼ (p.372 l.17–18). Each of them has a localisation domain X that meets Z (p.373 l.13–14).
      {#4.581-1} Y₄ = Y₁ ∪ Y′₂ ∪ Y′₃ ∪ Y′₄, with Y₁ the smallest 𝐃_k-domain containing X and the components of Z that meet X (p.373 l.15–16), and Y₀ in (1.66) is the smallest 𝐃_k-domain containing X (p.376 l.9). Each constituent has the factor (1.66) (p.376 l.19), and Y₄ ∖ Z = (Y₀ ∖ Z) ∪ ⋃_{i=2}^4(Y′_i ∖ Z) (p.376 l.23). So every constituent of a deep V(Y) has y in Y₀ ∖ Z or in some Y′_i ∖ Z. The V(Y) of (1.70) and (1.91) is this re-summation minus the completions of p.377 l.22–26, which #4.588–#4.589 bound.
    - {#4.582} *The Crossing.* Let a constituent have some Y′_i nonempty, i₀ the first such index. Each Y′_i connects Y′_i ∖ Z with Λ (p.376 l.24–25), and Λ = (Ω^{∼4}_{k₀+1})^c ∩ Z ⊂ Z (LFR I p.192 l.43). If y ∈ Y′_i, a path in Y′_i joins y to Λ. If y ∈ Y₀, X has a point y′ within one M-cube of the scale of y's layer, so at a layer ≤ k_s/8 + 1, since the layers are wider than RM in their own units (PRT2 (2.2), p.224 l.10–13).
      {#4.582-0.1} A path in X, which is connected (RG I p.257 l.7–9), joins y′ to a point of X, a contour realising the scaled distance d((Y₁⁰)^c ∩ Y₁ ∩ Y′_{i₀}, X) of the third term of (1.66) (PRT2 (2.46), p.231 l.9–13, cited at LFR II p.376 l.13–16) joins that point to Y′_{i₀}, and a path in Y′_{i₀} joins its end to Λ.
      {#4.582-0.2} The path leaves W only through Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j, before it reaches Λ ⊂ Z, so it crosses each layer Γ_l with k_s/8 + 1 < l < j inside W, outside Z: {#D.N.4} N := j − 2 − ⌊k_s/8⌋ layers at least. A layer is crossed by at most three consecutive pieces, in X, along the contour, and in Y′_{i₀}.
      {#4.582-0.3} The tree lengths and volumes are counted in the scale of each layer. CRE states this for the operation ∼ (p.263 l.6–8) and for volumes (p.263 l.21–22); for tree lengths Bałaban's bound of exp(−d_i(X)) by 2^{−(i−1−n)} (p.264 l.2–3) forces it, since that bound fails under single-scale counting. For an old term of the generation i, d_i(X) is taken in the layers of the step i.
      {#4.582-1} A layer Γ_l with l ≥ i is measured there in the finer units a_i ≤ a_l, so its crossing costs ≥ RL^{l−i}. A layer with l < i is measured at the step i in units no coarser than its own at the step j, since a point's layer index never decreases over the history. A fluctuation step k adds Ω_{k+1} inside the current top layer Ω_k and keeps Ω_1, …, Ω_k (CRE (3.5), p.265 l.42–44). An 𝐑-operation on a component Z replaces Ω_l by Ω″_l = (Z″_l^c ∩ Z) ∪ (Ω_l ∩ Z^c) ⊇ Ω_l, since Z″_l ⊂ Z_l, and keeps Ω_l for l ≤ h (LFR I (1.10)–(1.12), p.179 l.12–38); LFR II works with the same Ω″_l (p.362 l.10).
        {#4.582-1.1} So a piece of extent t in the units of its layer at the step j has an extent ≥ t in the units of the step i, for the old terms integrated with Z and for the completions of #4.588 alike. So pieces of extents t₁, t₂, and t₃ in the layer's units, with t₁ + t₂ + t₃ > RM, cost ≥ t₁/M − 1 of d_i(X), ≥ t₂ of the scaled distance, and ≥ t₃/M M-cubes of Y′_{i₀}.
        {#4.582-1.2} Half of the exponential that remains after Bałaban's extraction (p.376 l.37), exp(−½βκd_i(X) − ¼δd((Y₁⁰)^c ∩ Y₁ ∩ Y′_{i₀}, X) − Σ_i¼(κ₁ − 1)M^{−d}|Y′_i|), therefore gives e^{−σ_V} per crossed layer, with {#D.σ_V} σ_V := c_VR − ½βκ and {#D.c_V.2} c_V := min(½βκ, ¼δM, ¼(κ₁ − 1)).
      {#4.582-2} The order of choice is κ before R. κ_B and the condition (κ-½) (#4.583) do not involve R, since Bałaban's resummations hold at every step k with one κ while the widths MR_k vary with k (the Cauchy note's #CP.13). R is then fixed so large that σ_V ≥ 1.
    - {#4.583} *The Bound.* The other half of that exponential controls Bałaban's resummations of p.376 l.39–42, over the Y′_i, the X, and the generations, as the whole does. Those sums need the rates only above the constants of the counting of trees, domains, and points (Sects. 6, 7 [I] and Sects. 2, 3 [III], p.376 l.42), which Bałaban's large κ and κ₁ also exceed at half the rates.
      {#4.583-0.1} For κ this is the condition (κ-½): κ ≥ 2κ_B, with κ_B the threshold on κ of Bałaban's resummations of p.376 l.39–46 and of the small constant of p.377 l.4–5, and ½βκ ≥ 1, for the generation sums of the boundary terms (CRE p.264 l.2–3).
      {#4.583-1} κ can be chosen arbitrarily large if the other parameters are fixed accordingly (CRE p.260 l.27–28), at fixed β, as Bałaban does when he takes βκ ≥ 6·2^d "for κ large enough" (LFR II p.389 l.12). The δ-sum costs a factor of the type δ^{−d}, absorbed with the other constants in α, "arbitrarily small for γ small" (p.377 l.14). So the constituents of a deep V(Y) with a nonempty Y′_i sum to ≤ C_Vα e^{−σ_V max(N, 0)}exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), with C_V a constant of the halved resummations.
      {#4.583-2} Under the condition σ_V ≥ 1 on Bałaban's R (#4.582-2), of the kind of (⋆) (#4.655), and with j > k_s/4, N ≥ k_s/8 − 2, so e^{−σ_V max(N, 0)} ≤ e²e^{−k_s/8} ≤ e²2^{−k_s/16}. The two runs' sums of these constituents therefore differ by ≤ r_Dα exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), {#D.r_D} r_D := 2e²C_V2^{−k_s/16}, by the triangle inequality.
    - {#4.584} *The Exceptional Constituents.* The constituents with all Y′_i empty have only the first two terms of (1.66), with Y = Y₁ = Y₄ and Y₀ ∖ Z = Y₁ ∖ Z (p.376 l.43–46).
      - {#4.585} *The crossing through X.* The domain X of the term meets Z (p.373 l.13–14) and is connected (RG I p.257 l.7–9). y lies in Y₀ ∖ Z, so X has a point y′ within one M-cube of the scale of y's layer, at a layer ≤ k_s/8 + 1, as in #4.582. A path in X joins y′ to Z. It leaves W only through Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j, so it crosses each layer Γ_l with k_s/8 + 1 < l < j inside W, N layers at least, each with an extent > RM in the layer's units. Each crossing costs ≥ R − 1 of d_i(X): the piece t₁ of #4.582-1.1, with t₂ = t₃ = 0.
      - {#4.586} *The bound.* Bałaban extracts exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)) from the second term of (1.66), since d_k(Y₀) ≥ d_{k,Z}(Y) (p.376 l.44–45), and exp(−βκd_i(X)) remains. Half of it gives exp(−½βκ(R − 1)) ≤ e^{−σ_V} per crossed layer, since c_V ≤ ½βκ. The other half controls Bałaban's resummations, which the exponential remaining after his extraction controls (p.376 l.37–42), over the generations (p.376 l.41) and over the X with Y₀ ∖ Z fixed (p.376 l.45–46), under (κ-½) (#4.583).
      - {#4.587} So the exceptional constituents of a deep V(Y) sum to ≤ C_Eαe^{−σ_V max(N, 0)}exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), with C_E the constant of that halved resummation. With N ≥ k_s/8 − 2 and σ_V ≥ 1, the two runs' sums differ by ≤ r_Eα exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), {#D.r_E} r_E := 2e²C_E2^{−k_s/16}, by the triangle inequality.
    - {#4.588} *The Completions.* At p.377 l.22–26 Bałaban adds to the action the missing terms with localisation domains X meeting Z, the 𝐄-terms of the new action and the 𝐑-terms and boundary terms of the first k − 1 operations RT, at U_k. He re-sums them in the domains Y of p.377 l.5–7 and subtracts them from V(Y), and the result is the V(Y) of (1.70) and (1.91).
      {#4.588-1} A completion of the generation i ≤ k has its inductive bound exp(−κd_i(X)) on its class, which p.376 l.5–9 turns into the first two terms of (1.66): exp(−βκd_i(X) − (1 + 3β)κd_k(Y₀)), Y₀ the smallest 𝐃_k-domain containing X, for i < k, and exp(−(1 + 4β)κd_k(X)), with Y₀ = X, for i = k. Bałaban says that they "may be resummed in domains Y described above" (p.377 l.24–25), the Y ∈ 𝐃_k whose intersection with Z^∼ is a union of components of Z^∼ (p.377 l.6–7), so the assignment of a completion to a domain Y is a choice of the construction, the same in both runs.
      {#4.588-2} The completions are re-summed by the rule of the exceptional constituents (p.376 l.43–46, p.377 l.1–7): X goes to Y₁(X), the smallest domain of 𝐃_k containing X and the components of Z that meet X (p.373 l.15–16). Then Y ∖ Z = Y₀ ∖ Z, which Bałaban states for these domains at p.376 l.44 and which depends only on X and Z, so d_k(Y₀) ≥ d_{k,Z}(Y), and this is how the first two terms of (1.66) give (1.68) there.
      - {#4.589} *The bound.* With this rule the completions of a deep V(Y) are bounded as the exceptional constituents. y lies in Y₀ ∖ Z, X meets Z by definition and is connected, and the layers of the step i are no coarser than those of the step j (#4.582-1), so #4.585 applies.
        {#4.589-1} Half of exp(−βκd_i(X)) gives e^{−σ_V} per crossed layer, and the other half controls the re-summation over the X, the generations, and the three types, under (κ-½). So the completions of a deep V(Y) sum to ≤ C_Cαe^{−σ_V max(N, 0)}exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), with C_C the constant of that halved re-summation, and the two runs' completions differ by ≤ r_Cα exp(−(1 + 2β)κd_{k,Z}(Y)), {#D.r_C} r_C := 2e²C_C2^{−k_s/16}.
- {#4.590} *The step map.* At the fluctuation step k the boundary terms are among the activities of the expansion of the Cauchy note's (8.1), and its marking "RMark" applies: the two-run difference of an output is a sum of terms, each linear in one marked activity, with the other activities at run B or at run A.
  {#4.590-0.1} So the two-run difference of 𝐁^{(k+1)} has three parts. (i) The terms with the frozen 𝐁-difference of one input marked. (ii) The terms with the step's own two-run difference marked, applied to run B's boundary terms: the measure difference of (8.1), which contains 𝐁_k through (3.27), and the variation of the old terms at the two runs' backgrounds. (iii) The 𝐁-parts of the output differences generated by the other marked activities.
  {#4.590-1} The t-integral is a product of the integrand 𝐁_k(U_k(…)) − 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) and the measure (3.27), which contains t𝐁_k. Its two-run difference telescopes into the integrand's difference against run A's measure plus run B's integrand against the measures' difference, and the measures' difference is, by the interpolation of the Cauchy note's (8.1), a sum of terms each linear in one marked activity, t times a frozen 𝐁-difference among them. So RMark applies with two insertions, one in the integrand and one in the measure, and every term is linear in one marked activity.

As in #4.572-1.1, the intersection contains either run's space with the thresholds of each layer n scaled by e^{−(g^A_n)²|δ_n|}. The domains X of (1.63) are physical sets of the layers of the matched pair, the same in both runs, as are the sets Z_{j+1} ∩ Ω_{j+1} and Ω_{j+1}^c ∖ Z″_{j+1} of the integration variables (LFR I §1).
  - {#4.626} *The identity.* (1.60) is a fluctuation integral "of the same type as the integral studied in Sect. 3 [III]" (p.189 l.32). The variables A_j and B_j are block variables at the shared scale j, the same in both runs.
    {#4.626-1} So the interpolation of the Cauchy note's (8.1) applies verbatim, with 𝐏_t built from the exponent of (1.60) and the Gaussian forms of A_j and B_j interpolated as Δ_t there, at run A's cutoffs. By (1.62), ℂ^{(ν+1)}_k is the logarithm of the integral of (1.60), its factor z^{(j)} included, plus the coupling term, so ℂ^{B,(ν+1)}_k − ℂ^{A,(ν+1)}_k is the right side of (8.1), the cutoff shells, the coupling term's difference, and log z^{B,(j)} − log z^{A,(j)}.
      {#4.626-1-1} The factor exp E^{(j)}_0 stands before the integral (p.188 l.50), so E^{(j)}_0 is no part of ℂ^{(ν+1)}_k. It is a sum of constants per variable, those of the first exponential of CRE (3.15) on the sets of (1.60) (p.189 l.10–13, CRE p.267 l.49–51), one of the normalisation terms localised in Z (LFR II p.378 l.2), and its run difference, ≤ d(𝐠)g_j²|δ_j| per variable, is that of the Cauchy note's #C6.2.8-2.
      {#4.626-1-2} z^{(j)} is the product of factors attached to the bonds c of the scale j + 1 of the integration set (CRE p.270 l.15), the Jacobian of eliminating the variables B(b₀(c)) with δ(Q̃B), which yields the operator C determined by V^{(j)} (RG I p.268 l.2–3). The operator h has hB supported on the bonds b₀(c) and LQ̃h = I (RG I p.267 l.18–23), so the coefficient of B(b₀(c′)) in (Q̃B)(c) is 0 for c′ ≠ c and {#D.ω_c} ω_c := L^{−1}h(c)^{−1} for c′ = c. So the δ-functions eliminate these variables one bond at a time, and z^{(j)} = Π_c|det ω_c|^{−1}.
      {#4.626-1-3} A gauge transformation u conjugates ω_c by Ad u, since the average M of RG I (2.4) is gauge covariant, so det ω_c is gauge invariant; it is analytic in V^{(j)}, as M is (RG I (0.10)), and nonzero at V^{(j)} = 1, where h(c) exists. So there is {#D.r_det} r_det := a radius, depending on d, L, G, and M only, with |log det ω_c(V) − log det ω_c(1)| ≤ 1 for |V − 1| ≤ r_det on the blocks of c, in the cube gauge, uniformly in c by translation invariance.
      {#4.626-1-4} The class configurations 𝕌 = U′U have |V^{(j)} − 1| ≤ ½r_det there for γ small, by the cube bounds (1.65) and (1.67) on A, U^u = exp iηA, and the bounds of A′ in (i) and (ii) (p.190 l.13–53), the factors L₀^{2(·)} being ≤ L₀^{2N₀}, a polynomial in log g_{k_R}^{−2} (p.192 l.18–22). So by Cauchy's estimate each factor's run difference is ≤ {#D.C_det} C_det := 2C_∂V/r_det times the depth on the blocks of c, ≤ C_deth_n (#4.630), with {#D.C_∂V} C_∂V := the supremum over the class of the ℓ^∞ norm of the derivative of V^{(j)} in U_k^{(ν+1)}, finite since M is analytic and ℍ_Z^{(j)} small (#4.632).
      {#4.626-1-5} By Bałaban's rule (p.189 l.38–40) each factor is localised in the smallest 𝔻_{j+1}-domain containing c, at most two π_{j+1}-cubes (RG I p.257 l.7–11), with d_{j+1} ≤ 1 and ≤ 2d(M + 1)^d such bonds, so these terms add ≤ 2d(M + 1)^de^{(1+3β)κ}C_deth_n/C₀^𝔹 to c_{ν+1}.
    {#4.626-2} The measure ⟨·⟩_t is of Bałaban's kind, since 𝐏_t is a convex combination of two admissible exponents. RMark (#CS8.5) then gives localised terms in the domains of (1.63), each linear in one marked activity, bounded by C_ptC_XC_KP[ι_G + a_jι] times exp(−κ′d_m(X)) ≤ exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)), with κ′ of RMark (#T3.34) and a_j the fluctuation-domain weight g_jP_a(log g_j^{−2}) of the Cauchy note's #C8.2.2-84, not the unit of the scale j. Bałaban's resummation into the smallest 𝔻_m-domain (p.189 l.38–40) is a fixed rule of the domains, the same in both runs.
  - {#4.627} *The marked activities.* They are the parts of 𝐏^B − 𝐏^A, with these bounds per point:
    - {#4.628} the fluctuation parts of the frozen 𝐄-, 𝐑-, and 𝐁-differences, at U_k^{(ν)}(exp i[g_jCB_j − hD̃(g_jCB_j)]V^{(j)}) minus U_k^{(ν+1)}. Their norms are d and d^R of the Cauchy note (#C8.7.1) and b of #4.572-1, and they are bounded as the parts (i) and (iii) of the step k + 1 are (#4.591-3, #4.592-1), with the fluctuation g_jCB_j of (1.59) in place of g_kCA_k, by C_B𝒟^∗_{k_R} (#4.592), with the factor O(δ′_j) of the fluctuation (p.191 l.55–p.192 l.4);
    - {#4.629} the fluctuation parts of the earlier differences ℂ^{B,(i)}_k − ℂ^{A,(i)}_k, i ≤ ν. By (1.70) and the inclusion of the shifted configuration in Ũ_k^{(ν)c} ⊂ Ũ_k^{(i)c} (p.191 l.33–42), each is analytic there with the bound c_iC₀^𝔹exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)). As in #4.591–#4.591-1, its fluctuation part carries the factor C^ℂ_δδ′_j, {#D.C^ℂ_δ} C^ℂ_δ := the constant with which the bounds of these terms involve δ′_j (p.192 l.2), the analogue of #4.591-1's C_ε.
      {#4.629-1} The terms of the generation i are localised in Z_{h+i} ∖ Z″_{h+i}, and for h + i > k₀ these regions contain the common domain Ω_{k₀+1}^c ∖ Ω″_{k_R} (p.191 l.52–55), and there are at most k_R − k₀ = N₀ such i, since h + ν ≤ h + N = k_R (LFR I (1.11)). For h + 1 ≤ h + i ≤ k₀ the regions are pairwise disjoint (#4.629-1-1), so a point lies in at most one of them. So at a point at most N₀ + 1 ≤ C_ovN₀ generations have terms, {#D.C_ov} C_ov := 2.
        {#4.629-1-1} Let h + 1 ≤ j < j′ ≤ k₀. By LFR I (1.11), Z″_l = (Ω_l^{∼5})^c ∩ Z for these l, so Z_j ∖ Z″_j ⊂ Z_j and Z_{j′} ∖ Z″_{j′} ⊂ Ω_{j′}^{∼5}. Ω_l^{∼5} adds five layers of the cubes of Ω_l, of the side MR_la_l (LFR I p.179 l.7–8), so its points lie within the ℓ∞-distance 5MR_la_l of Ω_l. By BP_LAYER_WIDTHS.md #4.18-1, on Z, Ω_{l+1} lies eight layers of MR_{l+1}a_{l+1}-cubes inside the complement of Z′_l ⊇ Z_l = Λ_l^c ⊇ Ω_l^c (CRE p.264 l.52–56), so its ℓ∞-distance from Z_l and from Ω_l^c is ≥ 8MR_{l+1}a_{l+1}, h ≤ l ≤ k_R − 1.
        {#4.629-1-2} For j′ ≥ j + 2 this gives Ω_{j′}^{∼5} ⊂ Ω_{j′−1} ⊂ Ω_{j+1}, as 5 < 8, so in every case Z_{j′} ∖ Z″_{j′} ⊂ Ω_{j+1}^{∼5}. The points of Ω_{j+1}^{∼5} lie within 5MR_{j+1}a_{j+1} < 8MR_{j+1}a_{j+1} of Ω_{j+1}, so not in Z_j, and the two regions are disjoint.
        {#4.629-1-3} So the sum of these terms per point is ≤ C_ovN₀C^ℂ_δδ′_jC₀^𝔹max_{i≤ν}c_i. With Bałaban's N₀δ′_j < 4N₀²δ′_{k_R} (p.192 l.1–4) this is ≤ 4C_ovC^ℂ_δN₀²δ′_{k_R}C₀^𝔹max_{i≤ν}c_i;
    - {#4.630} the perturbative part 𝐏^{(j)}(g_j, A_j, B_j) and the fine actions at the fluctuated configurations. Their difference at equal coupling is the classical depth of U_k^{(ν)} at the fluctuated data, ≤ h_n = C_hθ̃^n per point at the history's birth scale (#4.459-0.2). Their coupling part is ≤ C_gg_j²|δ_j|, as in #C8.2.1-5;
    - {#4.631} the coupling terms A(1/(g_k^{(ν)}(·))² − 1/g_j², ·) of (1.60) and A(1/(g_k^{(ν+1)}(·))² − 1/(g_k^{(ν)}(·))², U_k^{(ν+1)}) of (1.62). The functions g_k^{(ν)}(·) are built from the β_l of the history, so the two runs' functions differ by ≤ C_β(k_R − m + 1)max_{m≤l≤k_R}d_l at a point of the layer m, with the growth that Bałaban's bound of the terms already absorbs, as in #4.593. So this part is ≤ (C_β/b′)max_{k_s/8<l≤k_R}d_l times Bałaban's bound, and the rest is a variation at the two runs' configurations;
    - {#4.632} V^{(j)} = exp(iℍ_Z^{(j)})V_Z^{(j)} (1.58). ℍ_Z^{(j)} is an analytic function of U_k^{(ν+1)} on Z, ≤ O(1)e^{−R_j}ε_j on (Ω_{j+1}^c ∖ Z″_j)^{(j)} (p.188 l.31–34). Its run difference at the two runs' configurations is a variation, ≤ O(1)e^{−R_j} times the depth by Cauchy's estimate on its domain;
    - {#4.633} the Gaussian forms ⟨A_j, C*Δ^{(j)}_{Λ_{j+1}^c}CA_j⟩ and ⟨B_j, C*Δ^{(j)}CB_j⟩. Their difference is bounded by the multiscale (10.6) of #4.100–#4.108, which rests on (W-δ), ≤ e times the form's bound, and its insertion is a marked quadratic activity of RMark (#CS8.5) with Gaussian part ι_G(Y) ≤ C_G″|Y|‖K‖_Y, K the form's kernel and ‖K‖_Y the larger of its row and column sums.
      {#4.633-1} K is symmetric, K(y′, y) = K(y, y′)^T, as the operator of a quadratic form taken symmetric at real backgrounds and continued analytically in the background, so its row and column sums agree, and the row sums are bounded through the multiscale (10.6), as in the Cauchy note's #C10.5.1 (RMark's quadratic case, with the factors |Y| in C_pt);

The test (1.59) is the soft (1.27) after its change of variables (#3.20, #3.69), and on B_j it does not depend on the background, so its shell is the coupling part of δ^s_j/κ_s (#3.28-2–#3.28-2-3, #3.32).
  - {#4.635} *The variation on Ũ_k^{(ν)c}.* Each run's term of the generations i ≤ ν, and each run's 𝐄-, 𝐑-, and 𝐁-terms, at the two runs' fluctuated configurations, is a variation. It is bounded as in #4.595–#4.621, with the room of the descending spaces in place of CRE's prefactors.

At a point of the layer m, the prefactor of the space Ũ_k^{(i)c} is {#D.P_i(m)} P_i(m) := 1 − βΣ_{i′=h+1}^{h+i}2^{−|m−i′|} − βΣ_{q>m}2^{−(q−m)} in (1.64) and (1.68) ((1.66) has m = j). So P_i(m) − P_{ν+1}(m) ≥ β2^{−|m−j|}, with j = h + ν + 1, the sum over i′ containing i′ = j.

Write {#D.j_i} j_i := h + i < j, P_i^{fr} for the frozen prefactor of Ũ_k^{(i)c}, and f(m) for the list of scale factors of (1.66) at the index m, with the α's included.

For m < m′, entry by entry, f(m′) ≤ (α_{m′}/α_m)L^{−(m′−m)}f(m): the plaquette, gradient, and p-entries gain L^{−2(m′−m)} or more (for the p-entry of the current with m < p ≤ m′ the ratio is L^{−2m′−p+3m} ≤ L^{−2(m′−m)}), the current entry L^{−3(m′−m)}, and the A′ entries L^{−(m′−m)}, the weakest, which is why Bałaban needs L₀² ≤ L/3 (p.191 l.35).

For T ≥ 1 it is ≤ {#D.C_αT} C_{αT} := sup_{T≥1}T^{−1/2}(1 + log T)^{q_c} (log x_m ≥ 1), and for T < 1 it is ≤ (1 + β₀)(m′ − m + 1)^{1/2} by CRE (2.6). With β₀ = 1/7 (#T1.2), log(N₀ + 1) ≤ ½(N₀ − 1)log 2 + log 4, and R_{k_R} ≤ 8L(log g_{k_R}^{−2})² (#T2.23, r = 2), this gives N₀ ≤ N₀^+(k_R), {#D.N₀^+(i)} N₀^+(i) := 1 + 2(log(32L(L + 1)) + 2log log g_i^{−2})/log L at a step i, with log g_i^{−2} ≥ 1 for ḡ small.

The prefactors used below are the frozen ones, at m equal to the space's index, where the sum over i′ is < 2, and those of (1.68) at m above the space's index, where it is < 1; the sum over q is ≤ 1. ## 5. The Large-Field Dressings of the Loop {#S5}

{#5.1} Here 𝒲^A[τ] and 𝒲^B[τ⁺] are the normalised dressed loops of the Cauchy note's #C1.2 on a matched pair τ⁺, τ of its §6.2, each with its own κ divided out. They have the form of the map's #MD2.0.3.2: e^{𝓔_k} times the leading word f_k plus the words tr(Y_{W₁}U_{(1)} ⋯ Y_{W_m}U_{(m)}) with the weights Q_k(𝔅).
  {#5.1-1} They are functions of the integration variables of 𝐓, which are the same in both runs (the Cauchy note's #C6.2.1; map #MD2.0.3.3, #MD2.0.3.66) and are written V below. a_j (#T2.3), j(x), C₀ (#T4.4), C₀^{ms} (#4.7-2), and the profile ρ̄(x) (#4.38) are those of §4(b), and {#D.m_W} m_W := ⌊k/8⌋. |·| and ‖·‖ are the norms of #T6.23, and {#D.‖dπ‖} ‖dπ‖ := sup_{|Y|=1}‖dπ(Y)‖_op for the representation π of the loop.

{#5.2} (a) *What the Main Proof Uses.*
- {#5.3} (LF-W) enters the main proof only at the Cauchy note's #C6.2.22, in the second term of ∫|𝒲^Bρ^B − 𝒲^Aρ^A| dV ≤ B_W∫|ρ^B − ρ^A| dV + ∫|𝒲^B − 𝒲^A|ρ^A dV, for the young matched pairs, k − j₀ < ⌊k/2⌋. The unmatched set (the Cauchy note's §6.1) and the old pairs use only |𝒲| ≤ B_W pointwise in V (the Cauchy note's #C6.1.3-1 and #C6.2.2), and the all-small-field pair has no large-field dressing.
  {#5.3-0.1} The young pairs need the second term, summed over them, to be ≤ B_Ws^{W,tot}_Kδ_LFZ^A_{ℓ₀} plus the dev part inside s′_K (#5.62), with s^{W,tot}_K summable in K. The young pairs, after run B's own-support shells are removed (the Cauchy note's §6.2), then change F by ≤ B_Wδ_LF(3s_K + s^{W,tot}_K): 2B_Wδ_LFs_K from the densities and the normalisation, B_Wδ_LFs_K from the dev part, and B_Wδ_LFs^{W,tot}_K from the dressings.
- {#5.4} *The Pairs With m_W ≤ k − j₀ < ⌊k/2⌋.* By the argument of the Cauchy note's #C6.2.2 with m_W in place of m, the oldest component X of such a pair meets the large-field region at every scale from j₀ to k, so P(X) ≥ m_W + 1. The bounds |𝒲^B|, |𝒲^A| ≤ B_W hold pointwise in V (#3.40). Also ρ^A ≥ 0 on the real integration region (LFR I p.176 l.20) and Z^A_τ ≤ M^A_τ. With these and the Cauchy note's (11.3) (#C11c.5) with the weight {#D.ω(X)} ω(X) := e^{C_PP(X)},

Since Ω_i = T for i < j₀ (#C6.2.1-7, j₀ the pair's birth scale), the nonempty layers Ω_i ∖ Ω_{i+1} of every step have i ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k − m_W ≥ 7k/8. For these pairs #5.9–#5.50 derive, at every V of the real integration region of τ,

D^{dev} is the weighted difference mass of the dev insertions, which #5.43 bounds by the recursion of the Cauchy note's §8.3 inside s′_K, with its depth term at the large-field backgrounds. s^W_K and s^{W,0}_K are defined at #5.53. (W) is the form (LF-1) of the Cauchy note's #CP.2 for the loop, and (5.2) is its integrated form.

{#5.9} (b) *The Run-Dependent Factors and the Assembly.*
- {#5.10} On a young pair with k − j₀ < m_W, four kinds of factors of 𝒲 depend on the run.
  - {#5.11} The transports of f_k and the U_{(i)}, read on the run's background (map #MD2.0.3.5).
  - {#5.12} The insertions Y_W of the species dev, att(j, Z), att(j, coll), and wrap(j) (map #MD2.0.3.16). There is no lw, since lw is made at step 1 only and j₀ > k − m_W ≥ 2.
  - {#5.13} The cluster weights φ_k(Γ) of Q_k and the local terms of 𝓔_k. These are numbers given the labels in each run (map #MD2.0.3.64), so they do not depend on V.
  - {#5.14} The parts produced by the 𝐑-operations of τ's components (the D2.7 closure 15.3–15.6).
- {#5.15} E_const,k is the same number on every labelled term of a run (map #MD2.0.3.8, #MD2.0.3.52). It is a factor of the run's whole numerator, the same on τ and on ℓ₀, so it is not a large-field dressing and is not compared here.
- {#5.16} *The Assembly.* Let a product have factors with |x^A_i| ≤ x̄_i and |x^B_i − x^A_i| ≤ Δ_ix̄_i. The telescoping identity gives |Π_ix^B_i − Π_ix^A_i| ≤ (Π_i(1 + Δ_i) − 1)Π_ix̄_i ≤ (e^{Σ_iΔ_i} − 1)Π_ix̄_i. The products Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W) majorise the sums over 𝔅, since |Q_k(𝔅)| ≤ Π_{W∈𝔅}e^{θ(W)} (map #MD2.0.3.50) and the dressing is multilinear in the species.
  {#5.16-1} Here ȳ_W is the bound of run A's insertion and d_W the bound of the two runs' difference. Then Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}(ȳ_W + d_W)) − Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W) ≤ (exp(Σ_We^{θ(W)}d_W) − 1)Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W), and |e^{𝓔^B} − e^{𝓔^A}| ≤ (e^{|𝓔^B − 𝓔^A|} − 1)|e^{𝓔^A}|. So (W) follows once the factors' relative differences sum to ≤ Σ_XC_Ms^W_KP(X) + s^{W,0}_K + D^{dev}, by (e^{a+b} − 1) ≤ e^b(e^a − 1) + (e^b − 1).

{#5.17} (c) *The Transports.*
- {#5.18} *The Alignment of the Backgrounds.* The transports are read on the term's background. This background is a VAR minimiser with the term's multiscale determining set, and its data are the term's integration variables, the same in both runs (map #MD2.0.3.5; by the D2.7 closure 15.5 the words are functions of U^{old} through the multiscale minimiser CRE (2.12)).
  {#5.18-0.1} At equal data the profile (#4.38) gives U^A = e^{iεA′*}MU^B in the gauge of the Cauchy note's #C9.4.1, with A′* = A₁* − HD(A₁*). Then VAR (55) and (57) (p.286 l.24 and l.42, with |·|_{(−1)} the supremum over the layers) and the gradient bound of HD used at the Cauchy note's #C9.6.1 give

{#5.19} (P′) a_{j(x)}|A′*(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇A′*(x)| ≤ ρ̄(x) + 8B₀C₂ρ̄_n² ≤ 2ρ̄(x),  {#D.ρ̄_n} ρ̄_n := sup_xρ̄(x).

  {#5.20} The second inequality holds under 16B₀C₂C_G(ε₀)c″_Kε₁ ≤ 1, since ρ̄_n²/ρ̄(x) ≤ 2C_G(ε₀)c″_Kε₁L^{−(1−ε₀)(2n−j(x))} and the finest layer n ≥ k − m_W has 2n ≥ k ≥ j(x).
- {#5.21} *The Coarse Links.* For a bond c of T_ε, RG I (0.4) gives MU^B(c) = e^{iY_c}W(c). Here W(c) is the transport of U^B along the L fine bonds of c, and {#D.Y_c} Y_c := Y_c(U^B) and {#D.h_c,x} h_{c,x}^{Γ,Γ′} := h_{c,x}^{Γ,Γ′}(U^B) are the exponent, a convex combination of the (1/i)log h_{c,x}^{Γ,Γ′}, and the loop holonomies of the Cauchy note's #C10.1.4-0-2 at W = U^B.
  {#5.21-0.1} In the axial gauge of the Cauchy note's #C10.4.9, each fine bond within 4dε of the block's centre is within 4dε(ε/L)|F| of 1, and the loop of h_{c,x}^{Γ,Γ′} has at most (d + 2)L ≤ (3d + 1)L fine bonds there. So |h_{c,x}^{Γ,Γ′} − 1| ≤ 4d(3d + 1)ε²|F|. For run B's background, |F| ≤ C₀^{ms}ε₁/a_{j′}² (#4.7-2), where a_{j′} ≥ a_{j(c)}/L is the finest layer within 4dε of c. With |log h| ≤ 2|h − 1| for |h − 1| ≤ ½, this gives

{#5.22} (Y) |Y_c| ≤ C_Y(ε/a_{j(c)})²ε₁,  {#D.C_Y} C_Y := 8d(3d + 1)L²C₀^{ms},  under 4d(3d + 1)L²C₀^{ms}ε₁ ≤ ½.

- {#5.23} *The Leading Word and the Arcs.* Hol_C(U^B) = Π_cW(c), the ordered product over the bonds c of C in T_ε. Hol_C(U^A) = Π_ce^{iεA′*(c)}e^{iY_c}W(c) up to a gauge transformation, which leaves the closed trace unchanged. Since π(W(c)) is unitary and ‖π(e^{iX}) − 1‖_op ≤ ‖dπ‖|X|, (P′) and (Y) give

{#5.24} (T) |f^B_k − f^A_k| ≤ Σ_{c⊂C}δ_c,  {#D.δ_c} δ_c := ‖dπ‖(ε|A′*(c)| + |Y_c|) ≤ ‖dπ‖(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + C_Y)(ε/a_{j(c)})^{2−ε₀}ε₁.

  {#5.25} The transports U_{(i)} between the slots of a word obey the same bound with the insertions' norms as the factor, since the insertions transform covariantly at their slots (map #MD2.0.3.6). So in every term of the dressing the transports differ relatively by ≤ Σ_{c⊂C}δ_c.
- {#5.26} *The Count.* A layer-j block of side a_j holds the initial points of at most 4a_j/ε bonds of the square C, at most a_j/ε on each side. There are at most L^d layer-j blocks per scale-(j + 1) point of Z_{j+1} ∩ X (the Cauchy note's §8.6, p_m(Z) ≤ L^d|Z_{m+1} ∩ Z|_{m+1}), and L^{−(1−ε₀)} ≤ θ̃. Put {#D.C^tr_W} C^{tr}_W := 4‖dπ‖(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + C_Y).
  - {#5.27} The bonds of C in the layers j < k contribute ≤ L^dC^{tr}_Wε₁θ̃^j per point of Z_{j+1} ∩ X, so ≤ L^dC^{tr}_Wε₁θ̃^{k−m_W}P(X) per component.
  - {#5.28} The at most 4ℓ_Ca_k/ε bonds of C in the stopping layer contribute ≤ {#D.s^W,tr_K} s^{W,tr}_K := ℓ_CC^{tr}_Wε₁L^{−(1−ε₀)k}, where ℓ_C is the side of C in stopping-scale bonds (the continuum note's #ND.1.1).

{#5.29} (d) *The Insertions, the Weights Q_k, and the Local Terms.*
- {#5.30} *The Variation.* Each insertion of run A is analytic in (𝐔, 𝐉) on the sub-domain 𝒟^{sub} of the SW closure §3(b1) about (U^A, J(U^A)), and it obeys its bound there (D(k)(iii); the SW closure §3(b2); for the attached species, the D2.6 closure 5.1). With Ũ = MU^B (#4.5-2-1) and J′ and δ𝐉 of #4.89, the alignment path {#D.(𝐔(t),𝐉(t))} (𝐔(t), 𝐉(t)) := (e^{i(t−1)εA′*}U^A, J(U^A) + (t − 1)δ𝐉) joins (Ũ, J′) at t = 0 to (U^A, J(U^A)) at t = 1. At equal data the alignment field is bounded by 2ρ̄_n by (P′), so #4.90 with d̄ = 2ρ̄_n gives a_{j(x)}³|δ𝐉(x)| ≤ x̄_J(2ρ̄_n + (ε/a_n)ε₁).
  - {#5.31} At a step i ≥ j₀ − 1, at a point of a layer l ≤ i, 𝒟^{sub} allows the phase (1 − β)α_{1,i}ε/a_i per fine bond, the gradient a_i²|∇A′| < (1 − β)α_{1,i}, and |𝐉 − J_i| < (1 − β)α_{0,i}a_i^{−3}. These are the top-layer radii with the layer's factor ≥ 1 − β.
  - {#5.32} On these layers i − l ≤ m_W, l ≥ k − m_W, and ρ̄ ≤ 2C_G(ε₀)c″_KL^{−(1−ε₀)(k−m_W)}ε₁. The phase gives the factor L^{i−l}, the gradient L^{2(i−l)}, and the current L^{3(i−l)}. So the path stays in 𝒟^{sub} for |t − 1| ≤ R_i, with

{#5.33} (R) 1/R_i ≤ c_{RW}(ε₁/((1 − β)min(α_{0,i}, α_{1,i})))L^{3m_W−(1−ε₀)(k−m_W)},  {#D.c_RW} c_{RW} := x̄_J(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + 1) + 4C_G(ε₀)c″_K.

  - {#5.34} By CRE (2.28) and (2.4), with q₀ = q₁ > p₀ (the SW closure §2) and C₀, C₁ ≥ A₀, α_{0,i}, α_{1,i} ≥ ε_i. By #4.458-0.1 at m = i ≥ k − m_W, with m_s = (1 + β₀)² (#D.m_s), as here k = K − j(C) = k_s (the Cauchy note's #C1.1, #D.k_s), ε₁/ε_i ≤ C_{αε}R_k(m_W + 1)^{1/2} with {#D.C_αε} C_{αε} := C(M)2^{p₀}(1 + β₀)². Also 3m_W − (1 − ε₀)(k − m_W) ≤ −(4 − 7ε₀)k/8.
  - {#5.35} For R_i ≥ 2, Cauchy's estimate on |t − 1| ≤ R_i shows that every insertion of run A changes along the path by ≤ {#D.v_i} v_i := 2/R_i times its bound, with

{#5.36} (V) v_i ≤ {#D.r̄_K} r̄_K := 2c_{RW}C_{αε}(1 − β)^{−1}R_k(m_W + 1)^{1/2}L^{−(4−7ε₀)k/8}.

  - {#5.37} This holds under ε₀ < 4/7 and the smallness conditions of the alignment listed after #4.91. No function of run B is evaluated on run A's lattice. Run B's insertion at (U^B, J(U^B)) is compared with run A's at (Ũ, J′), the lifts of the same multiplier λ^B (#4.91), and run A's change along the path is added.
- {#5.38} *The Generated Part.* At aligned arguments the two runs' insertions differ by what the two step maps generate from their ingredients. The loop's words are marked activities of the fluctuation measure, species-blind (the Cauchy note's #C8.3.3), and the attached members are fixed factors of the same measure ((T0) of the D2.6 closure). So (8.2)–(8.3) bound the frozen differences of the step's fresh ingredients at the step i + 1, the activities and fluctuation integrals that the step map makes, by (1 + C_g)𝒟^B_{i+1} times their bounds.
  {#5.38-1} Here C_g is that of the Cauchy note's #C8.2.1-5 and ε^* ≤ 1, with the depth term of 𝒟^B at the small-field points and (V) at the history's backgrounds.
  {#5.38-2} By #4.669, 𝒟^B_{i+1} ≤ C_𝒟Bm_i, with m_i and w_K of the Cauchy note's #C8.7.1-5 and {#D.C_𝒟B} C_𝒟B := the constant of that bound, a constant of §8.7's (#C8.7.3-7–#C8.7.3-16; not the C_m of its #C8.7.3-2). Since iθ̃^i ≤ kθ̃^{k−m_W−1} for k − m_W − 1 ≤ i ≤ k, (1 + C_g)𝒟^B_{i+1} ≤ {#D.η^gen_K} η^{gen}_K := (1 + C_g)C_𝒟B[(k + 1)θ̃^{k−m_W−1} + w_K] for these i.
  {#5.38-3} The pair's components are young: k − j₀ < m_W, so they are born at scales ≥ j₀ > k − m_W ≥ k − ⌊k/2⌋. So their operations 𝐓′_i(X), compared in total variation, differ by at most 3s_K times their bounds b̄(X), the V-terms V(Y) by at most r^V_K times theirs (r^V_K's range covers the steps i ≥ k − m_W − 1), and the step's polymer activities by at most 3C_Ms′_Kn(X)e^{C_Ms′_Kn(X)} times theirs, as in the Cauchy note's #C7.6-6-2-1-1 to #C7.6-6-2-5, at the pair's backgrounds.
  - {#5.38.1} An insertion made at the step i + 1 is, at aligned arguments, a function of these ingredients and of the carried insertions it touches, which #5.40 replaces one at a time. Hold the carried ones at run A's, and put x^ς := x^A + ς(x^B − x^A) for the fresh ingredients, abs(ς) ≤ 1/(2ρ^{LF}_K), with {#D.ρ^LF_K} ρ^{LF}_K := max(η^{gen}_K, ρ^E_K) and ρ^E_K of the Cauchy note's #C7.6-6-4.
  {#5.38.1-1} As in the Cauchy note's #C7.6-6-4 to #C7.6-6-6-2, each x^ς is within 2e^{κ_Id_i(X)} times run A's bound for the polymer activities and within twice it for the rest. So the amplitudes are enlarged by at most 2, and the decay of the polymer activities is lowered to κ − κ_I. The insertion made from the x^ς is analytic in ς and obeys its bound at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay, which is at least its bound.
  - {#5.38.2} For ρ^{LF}_K ≤ ¼, Cauchy's estimate on the disc of radius 1/(2ρ^{LF}_K) ≥ 2 bounds the generated difference by 4ρ^{LF}_K times the bound at the enlarged amplitudes. For ρ^{LF}_K > ¼ each run's insertion obeys its own bound, so they differ by at most twice it, which is less than 8ρ^{LF}_K times it. So in both cases the generated difference is at most 8ρ^{LF}_K times the insertion's bound at the enlarged amplitudes.
- {#5.39} *The Masses.* Let {#D.Ȳ_X} Ȳ_X := Σ_ZE_{j(Z)}(Z) + Ȳ^R_X (#5.39-3), the first sum over the components Z created in X's history, at their creation steps j(Z), of the lifetime totals E_j(Z) of the D2.6 closure 7.2 at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay of #5.38.1-1, which bound them also at the run's own amplitudes and decay. These totals contain Z's carried attached species with the carry factor 2, the species att(n, Z_n) of the later steps, the collar parts assigned to Z (map #MD2.0.3.43), and the exposed segments that pay e^{E^∂}.
  {#5.39-1} Then E_j(Z) ≤ ε^{(2)}_A(j)(d′_j(Z) + 1), with ε^{(2)}_A(j) closure 7.2's ε_A(j) at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay, of the same form and under the same smallness conditions for g small. Also d′_j(Z) + 1 ≤ 2|Z|_j, and the components created at one scale are disjoint. So Ȳ_X ≤ 2ε̄_AP(X), with {#D.ε̄_A} ε̄_A := sup_{j>k−m_W}ε^{(2)}_A(j) + ε^R_A (#5.39-3-3).
  {#5.39-2} The wrap species have no component, and #5.41.1–#5.41.5 treat them. Their weighted mass b_wrap is uniform in K, since it is part of the bound B_W of the continuum note's (8.1).
  {#5.39-3} *The 𝐑-Steps.* At an 𝐑-step n > k − m_W, the attached species present also include 15.6(e)'s charges, 15.4(iii)'s attached terms of E^{R,∂}_n(ℓ), and, at each second-class Y_i, item 7's block att(n, Y_i), the dev parts of the q = 0 clusters, and the pieces of the loop's words whose set 𝒦 contains Y_i, att(n, Y_i) by 15.6(e)'s scope rule (the D2.7 closure 15.5(i), 15.8(c)). These are not D2.6 species, so they are not in E_j(Z). {#D.Ȳ^R_X} Ȳ^R_X := the sum of their masses over the 𝐑-steps of X's history.
    {#5.39-3-1} Carried with the factor 2, the first are ≤ c^R_n(d′_n(Z_n) + 1) per component Z_n (15.3) and the second ≤ 13^dm^R_n#cubes_n(Z_n) (15.4(iii)), with c^R_n, m^R_n ≤ O(1)e^{−p₀(g_n)/4}, the root count N(Y_i) at a second-class Y_i included.
      {#5.39-3-1-0.1} The pieces of att(n, Y_i) are carried once, as one fixed member per class of second-class components (D2.7 closure 15.8-1). That member costs at most c^σ_n(d′_n(Y_i) + 1) per Y_i beyond its pieces' weighted masses (15.8-1(5-1)), with {#D.c^σ_n} c^σ_n := ν_r(C_dR_n^d + 4·3^dR_n) + (3/8)ν_e(2R_n + O(1)) + c_W + log 4, c_W the species constant of D2.6 closure 5.0 (D2.7 closure 15.8-1(5-1)).
    {#5.39-3-1-1} The word pieces at a second-class Y_i lie in no polymer, so they carry no e^{−p₀} factor. Summed over the bonds of C, 15.5(ii)(α) bounds their masses at Y_i by 4C_α(MR_n(d′_n(Y_i) + 1) + 2Mδ^{−1})δ^{−1} (15.8(c)), with C_α and δ of 15.5(ii). Weighted inside the member of 15.8-1, with C_α enlarged as in 15.8-1(6-1), they are ≤ 2c^w_n(d′_n(Y_i) + 1), {#D.c^w_n} c^w_n := 4C_α(MR_n + 2Mδ^{−1})δ^{−1}, a power of log g_n^{−2} of order ≤ r(d + 1).
    {#5.39-3-1-2} The q = 0 dev parts, the insertions e^{−d_c} − 1 of the two-loops note's *The clusters with q = 0* (#5.49-1), have weighted size Σ_cy_c ≤ m^w_Ψ per Y_i, with y_c = w^Ψ_c|e^{−d_c} − 1| of D2.7 15.8-1(4-1) and {#D.m^w_Ψ} m^w_Ψ := 2C_Ψ″e^{2C_Ψ″}: the weights w^Ψ_c are paid inside the Kotecký–Preiss sum of the two-loops note's tag 814 by 15.8-1(6), (6-0), and (6-3) (its tags 815.1–815.2).
    {#5.39-3-2} Item 7's block is a factor of the term, whose bound Y_i's large-field weight pays (15.8(c)). (W) bounds the difference relative to 𝒲̄ (#5.7), so the block counts in M_i with the mass 2, in units of item 5(b)'s bound at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay, since carried by D26 5.0 its bound is at most twice item 5(b)'s (15.8(c)). Its operation differs by ≤ 3s_K ≤ ρ^{LF}_K relative (#5.38-3), and its words as in #5.17–#5.43, so its generated difference is ≤ 8ρ^{LF}_K (#5.38.2).
    {#5.39-3-3} With d′_n + 1 ≤ 2|Z_n|_n, #cubes_n(Z_n) ≤ |Z_n|_n, the block's 2 ≤ 2|Y_i|_n, and the components at one step disjoint, Ȳ^R_X ≤ 2ε^R_AP(X), {#D.ε^R_A} ε^R_A := sup_{n>k−m_W}(c^R_n + 13^dm^R_n + 2c^w_n + c^σ_n) + 1 + m^w_Ψ. It and ε^{(2)}_A(j), powers of log g_n^{−2} at k − m_W < n ≤ k (#5.39-1), are at most powers of log g_k^{−2} + log(k + 1), since g_n^{−2} ≤ (1 + β₀)²(k − n + 1)g_k^{−2} for n ≤ k (CRE (2.6)).
- {#5.40} *The Carry.* Let D_i be the weighted difference mass, at aligned arguments, of the attached species present at the step i and of their descendants, and M_i their weighted mass at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay, with w(W) of the D2.6 closure §5.0. The carry lemma (closure 5.1–5.3) applies to the differences as to the insertions.
  {#5.40-0.1} Evaluation at the new background does not grow sup bounds, and the touched parts become descendants with the factor 1 + δ^{cl}_i, {#D.δ^cl_i} δ^{cl}_i := the closure's per-step growth factor (its δ_i, §5.0), named apart from the coupling difference δ_j (#D.δ_j). This factor is doubled for a descendant of several parents, since the difference of a product replaces one parent at a time.
  {#5.40-1} So D_{i+1} ≤ (1 + 2δ^{cl}_i)(D_i + v_iM_i) + 8ρ^{LF}_KM_{i+1} + 6τ^w_K (#5.38.2, #5.40-2), the last step's v_kM_k being the change along the path at the stopping scale. There are no attached species before j₀, at most m_W + 1 steps run from j₀ − 1 to k, Π_i(1 + 2δ^{cl}_i) ≤ e^{2Σ_iδ^{cl}_i} ≤ e^{2log 2} = 4 by the closure's Σ_mδ^{cl}_m = C_δc̄S_R ≤ log 2 (its 5.0), and M_i ≤ Σ_XȲ_X. Hence
  {#5.40-2} The old wraps that an attached group takes in (#5.41.4) differ by at most 2τ^w_K in total at each step (#5.41.2), and they enter with the doubled factor 1 + 2δ^{cl}_i ≤ 3 (δ^{cl}_i ≤ Σ_mδ^{cl}_m ≤ log 2, #5.40-1), so they add at most 6τ^w_K per step.

{#5.41} (D) D_k ≤ c̄^W_KΣ_XȲ_X + 24(m_W + 1)τ^w_K,  {#D.c̄^W_K} c̄^W_K := 4(m_W + 1)(r̄_K + 8ρ^{LF}_K).

- {#5.41.1} *The Wraps.* A wrap grows by up to L per step (map #MD2.0.3.34-4), so the carry of #5.40 does not apply to the wrap species, and they are present from step 1. The Cauchy note's #C7.8-1–#C7.8-3 bound them on the loop: the wraps of age m, born at the step k + 1 − m, have total weighted mass at most A_wL^me^{−a_wL^m} at every step, and those of age m ≥ m^w_K at most τ^w_K in each run (A_w, a_w, m^w_K, and τ^w_K of its #C7.8-2 and #C7.8-3).
- {#5.41.2} The old wraps, of age m ≥ m^w_K, are not compared: the two runs' differ by at most 2τ^w_K.
- {#5.41.3} A young wrap is born at a step i + 1 ≥ k + 2 − m^w_K ≥ k − m_W, since m^w_K ≤ m_W for K ≥ K₁ (the Cauchy note's #C7.4-7-2). At a birth step i + 1 ≥ j₀, the step at the scale i ≥ j₀ − 1, the generated difference is at most 8ρ^{LF}_K times its bound at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay (#5.38.2).
  {#5.41.3-0.1} At a birth step i + 1 < j₀, the step at the scale i < j₀ − 1, the ingredients are the all-small-field pair's (#5.6), and the difference is at most 4ρ^E_K times that bound, plus, for each run, 2e^{−C_Pk/4} times its own bound for the wraps through old components (the Cauchy note's #C7.8-4-1 to #C7.8-4-3).
  {#5.41.3-1} The bounds at the enlarged amplitudes and the lowered decay have total weighted mass at most A^{w,2}L^me^{−a^{w,2}L^m} at age m (its #C7.8-4-3). The wrap's dependence on the carried insertions it touches is the carry of #5.40: their differences stay, with the factor 1 + 2δ^{cl}_i, in D_i for the attached members and in D^{dev} for the dev insertions, and #5.41.4 passes those of the carried wraps.
- {#5.41.4} At every later step the change of the evaluation is at most r̄_K times the wrap's mass, by (V) at the steps ≥ j₀ − 1 and by (V) on the all-small-field pair before (the Cauchy note's #C7.8-5). A difference grows by at most 2L per step (its #C7.8-5-1), and the young wraps live at most m^w_K steps.
  {#5.41.4-1} No difference of an old wrap passes to a young one: by the D2.6 closure 2.1 *Merged groups*, a group that contains an old wrap takes the first inherited species in step order, so it is an old wrap (its #C7.8-6-1) or, if it also contains an attached member of an earlier step, an attached descendant of that member. In the second case the old wrap's difference passes to D_i (#5.40-2).

{#5.44} (e) *The 𝐑-Operations With the Loop.*

## (LF-2) at the Members of the Quotients (for #4.472-1.1) {#S0}
{#0.1} {#0.1.1} (LF-2) at complex V holds linear in d_j through the old 𝐑-terms read at the members of the quotients and at the arguments read through the merged generations. The members are bounded at Bałaban's own representative in a weighted norm, with only a block-anchored change of representative.

{#0.1.3} The member map is VAR's: the minimiser of (5) on 𝔘_k ∩ 𝔙_k(𝔅_k, V), whose data are the averages on the bonds of 𝔅_k and whose linearised residual group is N_𝔅 (#T11.19). With Q̃ the linearised average of VAR (3), Q̃D = D̄P (#T10.23), P the restriction to the points of 𝔅_k, and the axial representative of VAR's minimiser (REG (1.19), VAR (150), #T11.18) is U′_ax, with Q̃U′_ax = B on the bonds of 𝔅_k.
{#0.1.3-1} Bałaban's representative u_R = U′_ax^{u^{−1}} (VAR (152)–(153)) has u in the averaged gauge of REG (1.29), whose linear part is Q′ (#T11.18), so at first order u_R = U′_ax + ∂ζ^R with Q′ζ^R = 0 (at group level, #A.9.3); u_R is not in VAR's data set (#T11.18).

{#0.1.4} The weighted bound (KW) is run for the representative {#D.A_N} A_N := U′_ax + ∂ζ^N, where ζ^N = 0 on Λ₀, Q′ζ^N = −KU′_ax at the other points of 𝔅_k, and ‖A_N‖ is least under these conditions. Here Q̃ = Q − D̄K (#T11.19, #A.8), K the average over the contours from a block point to the sites of its block. K vanishes at the points of Λ₀, whose blocks are single sites, except in the crossing averages at the coarse bonds b with b₋ ∈ Λ₀, which average over the contours in the block B(b₋) ⊂ Λ₀ (REG p.81 l.36–44).
{#0.1.4-0.1} There KU′_ax(b₋) is a function of the fine data alone, of size ≤ C(d)Lθ_B, and B denotes the datum shifted by −KU′_ax(b₋), the crossing term S_b of #A.11.1.4.3.4 at j = 1, which occurs at every interface. Since Q(∂ζ) = D̄Q′ζ in the normalisation of RG I (0.4) (#A.11.2), QA_N = QU′_ax − D̄KU′_ax = Q̃U′_ax = B on the bonds of 𝔅_k, Q̃ here being #A.8's own-level average, without S_b, which #A.11.1.4.4.4's Q̃(U) includes.
{#0.1.4-0.2} A_N has the curvature of VAR's minimiser and its fine data on Λ₀. Minimality over ζ^N + N(Q′) gives ⟨∂*A_N, ζ⟩ = 0 for every ζ ∈ N(Q′), so ∂*A_N lies in the range of Q′*, which at the flat base is constant on each block of each layer j ≥ 1. u_R = A_N + ∂ω with {#D.ω} ω := ζ^R − ζ^N.
{#0.1.4-1} Since Q′ = P on Λ₀, ω vanishes on Λ₀; at a block point y, Q′ω(y) = KU′_ax(y); and ω minimises ‖u_R − ∂ω‖ under these conditions. This scalar problem is bounded through u_R and U′_ax alone, abs(Im ηω) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ at every point, uniformly in the volume and in the localisation domain (#A.9–#A.9.2).
{#0.1.4-1-1} The group-level transformation g of #A.9.3 has ‖Ad(g)‖ ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁ (#A.9.5), so conjugating the covariant members by it costs 1 + C(L, M)ε₁, inside the term C(L, M)ε₁ of the factor per level. The conjugated points keep CRE (2.34)–(2.37) within the class at r⁺ = (9/8)r: the members' representatives lie in 𝒫_j(X; (65/64)r) (#4.521, #4.540, #T3.13), and (65/64)(1 + C(L, M)ε₁) ≤ 9/8 for ε₁ small.
{#0.1.4-2} The Cauchy note reads (LF-2) at complex V through the 𝐑-differences, whose norms d^R_j are taken on its evaluation sets ℰ_j (its #C5.8 and #C8.2.6), so (LF-2) is needed linear in d_j at the literal points of ℰ, and elsewhere only as the plain class bound. A term 𝐑^{(j)} is read at three kinds of argument.

{#0.1.5} (α) While it is recent at the step k, k₁ < j ≤ k, at the fluctuated configuration U_k(…) and at the background U_{k+1} only (CRE (3.26), p.271 l.6–30). The regular part, which gives 𝐄^{(k+1)} and is renormalised at the points (N), (R2), and (R3), is taken at s = 0, so these are the callers' points of the kind (R1).

{#0.1.6} (β) Once it is merged into 𝐄_k, j ≤ k₁ (p.271 l.1–6), at the step's points of every kind. Their complex fields are of the scales ≥ k, within the class at r⁺ = (9/8)r there, and read at the scale j they are at most {#D.ϱ_k} ϱ_k := (9/8)(1+β₀)²N′(g_k)^{1/2}L/(MR_k) times the thresholds of the scale j.
{#0.1.6-1} This follows from the Cauchy note's #C5.27 at the distance k − j ≥ k − k₁, from x^{1/2}L^{−x} decreasing for x ≥ 1, from k − k₁ ≤ N′(g_k) (#C8.4.1-10), and from L^{−(k−k₁)} ≤ L/(MR_{k₁}) ≤ L/(MR_k), by the choice of k₁ (#C8.4.1-8) and R_{k₁} ≥ R_k (R̄ is nondecreasing, #CP.13). Since ϱ_k → 0 with g_k, the members' data there move by less than the margin-ball bound of #4.521 for γ small, and #4.521's derivation applies to the members.

{#0.1.7} (γ) Inside the quotients of the large-field renormalisation, at the members of a history (#4.245: the carried 𝐑-difference at run A's configurations), and at the composites and the comparison configurations over them. At the callers' arguments every member at which the frozen difference (i) is read is a literal point of the kind (R1) (#4.226, #4.521), and c̃ at the near domains at ∂Y_i is a point (R3) over it (#4.454), so (i) carries the factor d_j there for the 𝐄-terms. The step needed is (LF-2) linear in d_j at an argument that is itself such a member.

{#0.1.8} (γ) needs it for the old 𝐑-terms' part of (i) already at the callers' arguments, and (β) needs it at the members reached there. There the term's own members are minimisers at the member's averages at finer scales. By Proposition 9 (VAR p.309 l.8–13), the functional derivative of 𝓗 satisfies (190) (p.308), with "regularity and decay properties identical to the propagator H" (p.307 l.17–19), and B₅ enters only through the radius ε₂ = B₅ε₁ and the correction O(1)B₀C₄B₅ε₁ of (187).
{#0.1.8-1} So the complex parts of the members are those of the argument times C_H + δ_U, with C_H the sum of (190)'s kernel over the data in the units of the data and δ_U ≤ 1 the background's term (#A.11.1.1–#A.11.1.6), and the gain (9/8)(1+β₀)²L^{−1} per scale. The chains of members of members are not bounded in length, so the bound closes once the factor per level is < 1 (#0.1.10) and the members of an old term at a member c equal c where the old term's constraints refine those of c, so that the complex part is inherited and not amplified (#0.1.9).

{#0.1.9} The determining set 𝐁″_k of (1.50) restricted to Λ^c, and the field V″ there, coincide with those of the configuration U_k (LFR II p.370 l.7–8). So on the blocks that an old term's determining set shares with that of a member c = U_𝐁(D), the old term's members are at the data D, and the complex part there is that of the outermost argument's data or of one margin variable, amplified once by Proposition 9 as at #4.521, not along the chain.
{#0.1.9-1} In general 𝐑^{(i)} is localised in Λ_i^{∼−1}, the step i's small-field region (CRE (2.30), p.260), and later determining sets cover that region by coarser blocks unless it is frozen. Inside Λ the members' data are exp ig_kB·M^·(U_0^{(AL)}) on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} and V″ on Λ ∖ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} (1.50). In both places the old term's members read the member's finer averages, and the old term's member problem fixes c's averages on blocks refining c's determining set, c's blocks in Λ_i being of scales ≥ i (#0.1.40).
{#0.1.9-2} So the averages compose: near c the old term's admissible set lies in c's problem's space and contains c, so c is a local minimum for it (VAR p.301 l.44–45; BP_LFR2_CHI_K_LAMBDA #3.85–#3.85-1), hence its minimiser, VAR's problem having at most one critical orbit (p.278).

Bounded through Proposition 9, it carries C_H·θ again, so the chain closes when C_H(1 + 2C(d)C_H) = o(L) (#0.1.10), which C_H ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p+p_θ} satisfies (#0.1.12).

{#0.1.24-1} *The hitting estimate.* The boundary Hölder exponent ν of (K5) (#A.16-3) comes from random-walk hitting. Let a cell of Λ^c meet Q_r(x), r ≤ L/8. Each side interval of the cell has length ≥ L ≥ 8r and meets the corresponding one of Q_r(x), so it contains an interval of length r in that of Q_{2r}(x) beyond it. So the cell contains a box of sides ≥ 3r/4 in Q_{2r}(x), at distance ≥ (K₀ + 2)n from Q_r(x) in one coordinate, with n := r/C(d), C(d) ≥ 4(K₀ + 2).
