{#0.1.26.6-1} So the equation of #0.1.18 reads Ku = h₁ there, with {#D.K.5} K := Δ_j + a on all bonds, a = 1. K ≥ 1 on the torus, and its kernel is ≤ C(d)e^{−c(d)abs(b − b′)} (#0.1.17-1-0.1), so the conjugation by e^{±μabs(· − b₀)} changes it by ≤ C(d)μ in norm (Schur's test), and Combes–Thomas gives abs(K^{−1}(b, b′)) ≤ 2e^{−μabs(b − b′)} for μ = c(d), uniformly in the volume.
{#0.1.26.6-2} Splitting Ku = 1_{Q_{2R}(y)}h₁ + 1_{Q_{2R}(y)^c}Ku, with abs(Ku) ≤ C(d)sup abs(u) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}L^{d/2}θ (#A.10-1), gives sup_{Q_R(y)}abs(u) ≤ C(d)sup_{Q_{2R}(y)}abs(h₁) + C(d)e^{−μR/2}(1 + log L)^{p_θ}L^{d/2}θ ≤ C(d)(S + (1 + log L)^{p_θ}L^{−2}θ) + L^{−10}θ for R ≥ ρ₀, by the sizes of the Q₁-terms (#0.1.18-0.1).
{#0.1.26.6-3} So sup_{Q_{R/2}(y)}abs(F) ≤ 4sup_{Q_R(y)}abs(u), the scales 2^k ≤ R/2 add ≤ C(d)R sup_{Q_{R/2}(y)}abs(F) ≤ C(d)(θ_B + (1 + log L)^{p_θ}θ)/L + L^{−9}θ, since R ≤ L and L²S = θ_B, and the bound on v_{x̄}(y) holds there as at the sites of Λ. The same bound gives abs(u(b)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}L^{−2}θ + L^{−10}θ on the bonds of Q_R(y).

{#0.1.27} {#L6.KW} *The gradient part (KW).* Let {#D.λ} λ := λ_{x̄} on Q_{6L}(x̄), so u = v_{x̄} + w_{x̄} + ∂₁λ there, and let {#D.σ.2} σ := ∂₁*u − ∂₁*w_{x̄}, so that Δλ = −σ at the free interior sites of Q_{6L}(x̄) (Δ = −∂₁*∂₁, #A.10). The bound on ∂₁λ is (K6) (#A.17), proved through (K1)–(K5) (#A.12–#A.16), with (K0) (#A.11) for VAR's problem.
{#0.1.27-1} Hence ‖u‖_W ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^pC_H^{reg}θ_B for the response u to data B, C_H^{reg} the bulk constant, ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ} with constants of d only and no dependence on M or β₀ (in the N_b problem by the bounds on C̃ above and local regularity, in VAR's problem by #A.11.23-2 with θ_B for θ), and θ_B the supremum of the fine data and of the coarse block data (in the units of θ); in the N_b problem, with data g′ and response u = C̃g′, {#D.θ_B} θ_B := L² sup abs(g′), the units of the field, in which C̃ = O((1 + log L)²L²) (#0.1.17-2); the hole-filling's data sources are then of the bulk size.

{#0.1.28} The data of the chain are bounded in supremum, as θ_B of #0.1.27-1. The coarse data are block averages, ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p‖c‖_W, since the block averages of W are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p (#0.1.19-1). The chain of #0.1.40–#0.1.42 needs a bound on the fine data read in the weighted region of c, where abs(Im c) ≤ W‖Im c‖_W and W ≤ (1 + log L)^pL/ρ₀, t and t₃ being ≥ ρ₀.
{#0.1.28-0.1} In case (i) (#0.1.40-2) no such evaluation occurs, given #0.1.41: an old term's member equals c up to the response to the old term's own variables. In case (ii) (#0.1.42) the old term, of scale i < i_prev, reads c at the scale q ≤ i of its blocks.
{#0.1.28-0.1-1} Its analyticity domain is defined by the radii of its own scale i (CRE p.259, (ii) below (2.27): U_i^c(X, α_{0,i}, α_{1,i}); for the terms of 𝐑^{(i)} by p.260 below (2.30), "Terms of this representation have the properties (i)–(iii) formulated above"), so by #0.1.42 the datum carries (1+β₀)²(i_prev − i)^{1/2}L^{−(i_prev−i)} times the bound at i_prev, relative to the thresholds of the scale i.
{#0.1.28-1} At the scales q at least that of the lattice on which c's W is measured, the datum is a value or an average of c on that lattice, ≤ W‖Im c‖_W at its bonds; so for i_prev − i ≥ 2 the factor ≤ 2(1+β₀)²L^{−2} pays W ≤ (1 + log L)^pL/ρ₀, leaving (1 + log L)^p/(Lρ₀) within the factor per level C(d)(1 + log L)^{2p+2p_θ}/L of #0.1.42-1.
{#0.1.28-1-1} The evaluations in c's weighted region at blocks finer than c's occur only inside T_□: off T_□ run B's constraints are run A's composed with M (#4.445.1), and #4.445.2 adds the sources of the strip. Inside T_□, c is run B's composite c^B (#4.445.1) or a member with c^B's layers at complex data in the polydisc of #0.1.41, and its norm is ‖·‖_{W_ms} of #0.1.30 and #A.11.42, the supremum over the fine bonds b of abs(Im c)/W_ms with the field in the units of L^{j(b)}, j(b) the least j with χ_j(b) ≠ 0 (#A.11.49), with W_j measured from run B's layer Λ^B_j in its own units.
{#0.1.28-1-2} Run B's layers are the shells Ω^B_j ∖ Ω^B_{j+1} between nested boxes (#4.445.1). Around a codimension-k edge of the inner box the 2^k − 1 cells of the shell are joined through face-sharing chains, and near an edge of the outer box the shell is one orthant, so no two distinct local components of a layer meet, t₃ = L in every W_j, and W_ms ≤ (1 + log L)^p(L/ρ₀)^κ on □₀, t being ≥ ρ₀.
{#0.1.28-2} Run B's scale indices count from its finest spacing ε/L, and scales of the two runs are compared as block sizes. So every value of Im c there at a bond of any W_j's lattice is ≤ (1 + log L)^p(L/ρ₀)^κ‖Im c‖_{W_ms} in the units of L^{j(b)}, and so in those of an evaluation scale ≤ j(b), which every evaluation there has: χ_j ≠ 0 at a bond of run B's layer Λ^B_n only for j ∈ {n − 1, n} (#A.11.49), so j(b) ≥ n − 1, and an evaluation at blocks finer than c's there has a scale ≤ n − 1, and every average of such values is ≤ C(d) times that, to first order in the complex part (#0.1.39).
{#0.1.28-3} At i = i_prev − 1 the gain (9/8)(1+β₀)²L^{−1} then leaves the factor per level C(d)(1 + log L)^{3p+2p_θ}L^{−μ}ρ₀^{−κ} of #0.1.42-1, κ = 1 − μ, and for i_prev − i ≥ 2 the gain 2(1+β₀)²L^{−2} leaves less.

{#0.1.29} {#L6.balaban} *Bałaban's problem.* For VAR's problem the residual group is N_𝔅 (#0.1.3), and the components are those of the graph of the data bonds of Λ₀. t₃ is, as in the N_b problem, the distance to the contacts of codimension ≥ 2 between distinct local components (#A.10); the averages of W over blocks and over the coordinate planes through block centres remain ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p, by the Hölder bound above, since the exponent of L/t₃ there is close to 1 < 2, and so the weighted kernel sums are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p times the unweighted ones.
{#0.1.29-1} ∂*A_N lies in ran Q′* (#0.1.4-0.2), the block-constant fields transported by R(U(y, x)) (PBG (3.19), with the contour variables of the Cauchy note's #C10.1.4-1-1). So ∂*A_N is constant on each block of Λ, the layer sites included. So in (KW) λ solves Δλ = −σ at every site of Λ in Q_{6L}(x̄), the boundary is Λ₀, where λ = c_i up to the increments B − v_{x̄} − w_{x̄} on the data bonds, and the maximum principle needs no condition at the layer sites.
{#0.1.29-2} The hole-filling is run for the residual a = A_N − E of #A.11.5, not for A_N, whose energy near a face of Λ₀ is of order L^{d−1}θ_B² per block. a vanishes on the data bonds, so the mass term of E(Q_r) (#0.1.20) is absent and the fields w of #0.1.21 are a − ∂φ with φ constant on the components of the data graph, where a − ∂φ = 0.

{#0.1.30} Its linear term ℓ_E, tested with η²w, is bounded by the dual-norm sources S of #A.11.6-2: it vanishes where χ_dχ_f = 1, d*F_f being 0 on the free bonds of supp χ_f (#A.11.6-1), and on Q_r(x) it is ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)³S(Q_r(x))(E(Q_{C(d)r}(x)) + r^{−2}‖w‖²_{Q_{C(d)r}(x)})^{1/2}, T̂_f depending on dT only within C(d)m_f ≤ C(d)r. With S(Q_r)² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)r^{d−2}θ_B² (#A.11.6-2) and Ē of the bulk size L^{d−2}θ², this is a source of exponent d − 2 > α.
{#0.1.30-0.1} The region at distance L/32 to L/16 from Λ₀, where ∇χ_d ≠ 0, adds a source of exponent d. The coarse constraints are hard: Caccioppoli's test fields are corrected by the bumps β_c of #0.1.33.1, at a source cost with exponent d + 2 (#A.8). The rest of (KW) is unchanged, with the weighted L² decay of VAR's problem derived in #A.11 (K0), so ‖A_N‖_W obeys the same bound.
{#0.1.30-1} At the interfaces Λ_j/Λ_{j+1} with j ≥ 1 the same holds in the units of L^j for the representative {#D.A_♮} A_♮ := A_N + ∂ω_♮ of #A.11.49, with ω_♮ ∈ N(Q′), abs(Im ηω_♮) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ pointwise, and A_♮ = A_N at the points of R₀ outside the blocks of Λ₁ that meet R₁ (#A.11.50); for the complex part of the data (#0.1.11) the chain uses A_♮ in place of A_N and ω − ω_♮ in place of ω, at group level through the representative u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} of #A.9.6 with ‖Ad(g_♮)‖ ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁, and its norm is ‖·‖_{W_ms}, W_ms of #A.11.42, which has the properties of W used here (#A.11.43).
{#0.1.30-1-1} PRT2's random walk (2.141) and Proposition 2.6 (p.247), and PBG Corollary 3.6 (p.408), are used only for B₀, with Bałaban's constants O(1)(d, L). B₀ is also the constant of VAR's bounds abs(HB) ≤ B₀(L^jη)^{−1}abs(B) and abs(∇HB) ≤ B₀(L^jη)^{−2}abs(B) on Ω_j (p.285 l.27), and it enters VAR only as at #0.1.14.
{#0.1.30-1-2} For the scalar local propagators G′_□ of Δ′_a, the blocks of 𝔅 partition the region, and the per-block Poincaré bound, ‖λ‖²_B ≤ C(d)(S²‖∂λ‖²_B + S^dabs(Q′λ)²), gives the gap c(d)min(1, a)S^{−2} in each block's units with no interface term, since the coefficients of PBG (3.24) (p.394 l.29), a₁ = a₀ = a and a_{j+1} = aa_j/(aL^{−2} + a_j), obey a/2 ≤ a_j ≤ a for L ≥ 2 by induction.
{#0.1.30-2} At a background U, λ is read in the frame of a coordinate tree of each block, in which U = 1 on the tree. By VAR (2) (p.278), abs(U(∂p) − 1) < ε₀L^{−2j} on the plaquettes of Ω_j, so the loop of a bond of a block of side S = L^j with its tree paths, which bounds ≤ C(d)S plaquettes, has holonomy defect ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−1}, and the covariant difference differs from ∂λ by ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−1}abs(λ) on each bond.
{#0.1.30-2-1} The contours of Bałaban's average against the tree paths bound ≤ C(d)S² plaquettes, with defect ≤ C(d)ε₀, so the covariant mean differs from Q′λ by ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−d/2}‖λ‖_B. For ε₀ ≤ c(d) both are absorbed, and the covariant per-block Poincaré bound and the gap hold with other constants of d only.

{#0.1.31} *The two-layer gap.* The gap on the gauge orbit is used in three settings: #0.1.16 (Λ^c and Λ of PRT2 Lemma 2.4, the form (2.122)), #A.11.10 (the problem 𝒫₁ of #A.11.8, Λ₀ and Ω₁), and #A.11.29–#A.11.34 (the two-layer problem for V on the scale-j lattice, Ω_{j+1}^c and Ω_{j+1}). In units of the fine scale, there is a fine region F, with D = 0 on the bonds with both endpoints in F (the data bonds), and a coarse region C := F^c, a finite union of blocks of side L of one grid of which F is also a union, with QD(c) = 0 on every bond c of the grid with an endpoint in C.
{#0.1.31-0.1} Here Q is the average over x ∈ B(c₋) of the sums of D along the lines from x to x + Le_μ, at the flat base (CMP98 (124)–(125), p.36), so Q∂λ(c) = Q′λ(B(c₊)) − Q′λ(B(c₋)) with Q′ the block mean, and QD(c) = 0 holds also on the bonds of the grid between two blocks of F, whose lines run on data bonds. PRT2's Q₁ is L^{−1}Q ((2.125), p.245; (2.103), p.241), and CMP98 (125) carries the same L^{−(d+1)}, so CMP98's Q₀ is PRT2's Q₁.
{#0.1.31-1} The coarse norm carries L^d, so L^{−2}‖(Q₁B)↾_{Λ′}‖² = L^{d−4}Σ_cabs(QB(c))². The unit bonds from F into C, the crossing bonds, are free in every use: in #0.1.16 they are bonds of Λ, the set of bonds with at least one endpoint in Λ, on which B is free (PRT2 Lemma 2.4, p.245), and in (d) and (g) VAR does not constrain them (REG p.81 l.36–44).
{#0.1.31-2} By PRT2 (2.3) (p.224) and REG p.81 l.36, for j ≥ 1 the scale-j bonds of Λ_j are those with an endpoint in Ω_j^{(j)} and none in Ω_{j+1}^{(j)}, so no constraint of a finer scale on bonds into a coarser region enters, and the problems of #A.11.8 and #A.11.29 fix the data of the coarser layers by constraints of the one coarse scale.

{#0.1.32} The claim. With ℓ := L on the bonds with an endpoint in C and ℓ := 1 on the others, there is λ in the group {#D.N_F} N_F := {λ : λ = 0 on F, Q′λ = 0 at every block of C} such that ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖. By Q∂λ = Q′λ(B(c₊)) − Q′λ(B(c₋)), N_F keeps the zeros and the constraints of D. The construction (#0.1.34–#0.1.37.1) is run for a D vanishing also on a set 𝒳 of crossing bonds, one into each site of C joined to F. Every class of D modulo ∂N_F contains such a D, D − ∂λ₀ with λ₀ ∈ N_F (#A.11.9, with N(Q′) := N_F), and the λ for D is λ₀ plus that for D − ∂λ₀, since dD is unchanged.
{#0.1.32-1} For #0.1.16, F := Λ^c, C := Λ, and N_F = N_b. B ∈ 𝒮 is the least element of B + ∂N_b in ℓ², and ∂N_b vanishes on the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c, so with the lift below and the claim for D := B − Ã, ‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{−2}‖B↾_Λ‖² ≤ ‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{−2}‖(B − ∂λ)↾_Λ‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)²F(B), with B↾_Λ the restriction to the bonds with an endpoint in Λ, the crossing bonds included, on which ℓ = L, since (B − ∂λ)↾_Λ = Ã↾_Λ + (D − ∂λ)↾_Λ.

{#0.1.33} The lift for (2.122). For a field B let {#D.Ã} Ã := B on the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c plus Σ_cr(c)β_c over the bonds c of the grid with an endpoint in Λ, with {#D.r(c)} r(c) := QB(c) − Q(1_{Λ^c}B)(c), 1_{Λ^c} the indicator of the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c, and β_c the bump of #0.1.33.1 at the scale 1 in the block of c in Λ (B(c₋) if both are).
{#0.1.33-0.1} Then Qβ_c = δ_c on these bonds, abs(β_c) ≤ C(d)/L, abs(dβ_c) ≤ C(d)/L², and β_c is supported at distance ≥ L/8 from the faces of its block, off the bonds of Λ^c and the crossing bonds. So QÃ = QB on these bonds and Ã = B on the bonds of Λ^c, and {#D.D} D := B − Ã vanishes on the bonds of Λ^c, with QD = 0, and D = B on the crossing bonds.
{#0.1.33-1} Each bond lies on at most L of the lines of Q, so by Cauchy–Schwarz abs(Qg(c))² ≤ L^{2−d}‖g‖²_{Ω_c}, Ω_c := B(c₋) ∪ B(c₊), and L^{d−4}abs(r(c))² ≤ 2L^{d−4}abs(QB(c))² + 2L^{−2}‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖²_{Ω_c}. A block carries the bumps of at most 2d bonds, with ‖β_c‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−2} and ‖dβ_c‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−4}, so ‖dÃ‖² + L^{−2}‖Ã↾_Λ‖² ≤ C(d)(‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{d−4}Σ_cabs(QB(c))²) ≤ C(d)F(B). Then ‖dD‖² ≤ 2γ₀^{−1}F(B) + 2‖dÃ‖² ≤ C(d)F(B), γ₀ of (2.118) depending on d only (PRT1 p.29).

{#0.1.33.1} The bumps. In units η = 1, let c be a bond of direction μ and scale j with a block in the layer Λ_j, {#D.S.2} S := L^j, and Q_j the average over x ∈ B(c₋) of the line integrals of length S, as in #A.8, so that Q_j maps a constant field a to Sa (PBG's Q_j is S^{−1} times this). Let B be the block of c in Λ_j (B(c₋) if both are). At the flat base the one-step contours of a bond stay in its two blocks, and so do those of the composites (CMP98 (124), p.36; PBG (3.15), p.393).
{#0.1.33.1-0.1} So among the scale-j constraints, a field on the direction-μ bonds of B is read only by c and by the direction-μ bond c* of the scale j whose other block is B (the previous bond for B = B(c₋), the next for B = B(c₊)).
{#0.1.33.1-0.2} For B = B(c₋), a scale-(j−1) bond e at the position k(e) ∈ {1, …, L} along μ in B lies on k(e) of the one-step lines of c and on L − k(e) of those of c*, each of weight L^{−d}; a fine bond z enters Q_{j−1} only through the scale-(j−1) bonds e whose two blocks contain it, with k(e) − k(z) ∈ {−1, 0}, k(z) the position of z's scale-(j−1) block.
{#0.1.33.1-0.3} So the weights w_c and w_{c*} of z obey (k(z) − 1)w_{c*}(z) ≤ (L − k(z) + 1)w_c(z) and (L − k(z))w_c(z) ≤ k(z)w_{c*}(z), and by induction on j their sum is S^{1−d} on every direction-μ bond (for j = 1, k + (L − k) = L lines of weight L^{−d}); for B = B(c₊) the roles of k and L − k are exchanged.
{#0.1.33.1-1} Let ψ₁ and ψ₂ be sampled smooth functions on the sites of B, 0 ≤ ψ_i ≤ 1, abs(∇ψ_i) ≤ C(d)/S, at distance ≥ S/8 from the transverse faces, with ψ₁ supported at k ∈ [3L/4, 7L/8] and ψ₂ at k ∈ [L/8, L/4], each equal to 1 on ≥ c(d)S^d sites. For L ≥ 16, w_c ≥ 2w_{c*} on supp ψ₁ and w_{c*} ≥ 2w_c on supp ψ₂. With a_i := Q_j(ψ_ie_μ)(c) and b_i := Q_j(ψ_ie_μ)(c*), a₁ ≥ 2b₁ ≥ 0, b₂ ≥ 2a₂ ≥ 0, and a₁, b₂ ≥ c(d)S, so a₁b₂ − a₂b₁ ≥ (3/4)a₁b₂.
{#0.1.33.1-2} Let {#D.β_c} β_c := (x₁ψ₁ + x₂ψ₂)e_μ with a₁x₁ + a₂x₂ = 1 and b₁x₁ + b₂x₂ = 0; then abs(x_i) ≤ C(d)/S. So Q_jβ_c = δ_c on the scale-j bonds, abs(β_c) ≤ C(d)/S, abs(∂β_c) ≤ C(d)/S², ‖∂β_c‖² ≤ C(d)S^{d−4}, and β_c is supported in B at distance ≥ S/8 from its faces: off the data bonds, off the scale-(j − 1) blocks of B that touch its faces, and off every other layer.
{#0.1.33.1-3} In PBG's normalisation, Q_jβ_c = S^{−1}δ_c, so the bump with Q_j = δ_c is Sβ_c, of size C(d) and ‖∇(Sβ_c)‖² ≤ C(d)S^{d−2}. On Λ₀, whose blocks are single sites, β_c is the unit field on c.

{#0.1.34} Block potentials. For a block B of the grid let 𝐁_B be the ball of radius L/8 about its centre, and for x in the cube 5B of side 5L about B let {#D.φ_B} φ_B(x) := the average over a ∈ 𝐁_B of the sums of D along the lattice paths within distance 1 of the segment from a to x, averaged as for G^Y in #A.11.13. As there, (D − ∂φ_B)(b) on a bond b = (x, x + e_μ) of 3B is an average of sums of dD over strips of width ≤ C(d) along the segments.
{#0.1.34-1} A plaquette p at distance t from x lies in them for a fraction ≤ C(d)max(t, 1)^{1−d} of the a, the segments having length ≤ C(d)L and 𝐁_B the radius L/8. So abs((D − ∂φ_B)(b)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p⊂5B}abs(dD(p))max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d}, and since Σ_{p⊂5B}max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d} ≤ C(d)L, Schur's test gives ‖D − ∂φ_B‖_{3B} ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{5B}. Let {#D.φ̂_B} φ̂_B := φ_B − mean_Bφ_B.

{#0.1.35} The relative constants. For the bond c of the grid from B to B′ = B + Le_μ, Q∂φ_{B′}(c) = mean_{B′}φ_{B′} − mean_Bφ_{B′} and QD(c) = 0. So abs(mean_Bφ̂_{B′}) = abs(Q(D − ∂φ_{B′})(c)) ≤ L^{1−d/2}‖D − ∂φ_{B′}‖_{Ω_c} ≤ C(d)L^{2−d/2}‖dD‖_{5B′}. For B′ = B + Lv, v ∈ {−1, 0, 1}^d, a chain of at most d such steps through blocks in 3B′ gives the same bound with another C(d).
{#0.1.35-1} On the box P := 3B ∩ 3B′, which contains B and B′, g := φ̂_B − φ̂_{B′} has ‖∂g‖_P ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{5B∪5B′}, and mean_Bg = −mean_Bφ̂_{B′}, so Poincaré on P gives ‖g‖_P ≤ C(d)L²‖dD‖_{7B}. Each pair of neighbouring blocks is compared through its own constraints, so nothing accumulates along chains of blocks.

{#0.1.36} The interior. Let ψ_B be a sampled smooth partition of unity over the blocks, ψ_B supported in 2B with abs(∇ψ_B) ≤ C(d)/L, and {#D.Ψ_int} Ψ_int := Σ_Bψ_Bφ̂_B, a finite sum, since φ_B = 0 for the blocks with D = 0 on 5B. On a bond b = (x, x + e_μ) with x in the block B₀, the product rule ∂(ψφ)(b) = ψ(x + e_μ)∂φ(b) + φ(x)∂ψ(b) and Σ_B∂ψ_B = 0 give (D − ∂Ψ_int)(b) = Σ_Bψ_B(x + e_μ)(D − ∂φ_B)(b) − Σ_B(φ̂_B − φ̂_{B₀})(x)∂ψ_B(b), the blocks B in the sums lying in 3B₀. So ‖D − ∂Ψ_int‖_{B₀} ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{9B₀}, and ‖D − ∂Ψ_int‖ ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖.

The old term reads at a scale i < i_prev, since its generation precedes that of the term or step at which c is read.

## The Weighted Bound at Λ^c (for #0.1) {#SA}
- {#A.1} *Setting.* Inside a cube Q_s with s ≤ L/8 each direction μ meets at most one hyperplane {x_μ = h_μ} of the cells of Λ (side ≥ L), h_μ a half-integer. A cube is *good* if s ∈ [ρ, 3ρ] and the faces of Q_s and of Q_{9s/16} lie at distance ≥ ρ/(40d) from these hyperplanes. Per direction the excluded s have measure ≤ (1 + 16/9)ρ/(20d), so ≤ 5ρ/36 < 2ρ in all.
  {#A.1-1} Then the hyperplanes and the faces of Q_{9s/16} cut Q_s and {#D.A′_s} A′_s := Q_s ∖ Q_{9s/16} into C(d) boxes of a product grid with all sides between ρ/(40d) and 6ρ (*fat boxes*), each in Λ or in Λ^c; A′_s ⊂ A_s = Q_s ∖ Q_{s/2} (#0.1.21-2). The components of the mass graph (#0.1.18-4) are the residual group's domains of constancy.
  {#A.1-2} Let s ≤ s₃ (#0.1.20), Q_s = Q_s(x₀). Two cells of Λ^c that meet Q_s differ on hyperplanes that all cut Q_s, a product of intervals, so they meet in Q_s, in codimension k, k the number of these hyperplanes. For k = 1 they share a face. For k ≥ 2 the contact lies within C(d)s of x₀, and since t₃(x₀) ≥ C(d)s₃ excludes a contact of distinct local components there (#A.10), near every point of the contact the cells of Λ^c around it form one local component. So the cells of Λ^c meeting Q_s lie in one local component at Q_s, and every contact of codimension ≥ 2 among them is locally joined.
  {#A.1-3} Inside Q_s the cells are the orthant boxes about the point (h_μ) of the hyperplanes that meet Q_s, each a product of intervals that reach ∂Q_s. The part of such a box in A′_s is connected: its pieces {±x_μ > 9s/16} are fat boxes, and any two of different directions meet. Two boxes that share a face are joined across it in A′_s, near ∂Q_s. So {#D.Z_D} Z_D := the set of the sites of Λ^c in D is empty or connected through face-sharing fat boxes, for D = Q_s and D = A′_s, and it meets A′_s if it meets Q_s. In VAR's problem read Λ₀ and its data bonds for Λ^c and the mass bonds (#A.10).
- {#A.2} *Primitives.* On a box P with sides between ℓ and 4ℓ, the complete axial contraction from a base point b (a_1 = 0, and a_μ the sum of F_{νμ}, ν < μ, along e_ν from the faces {x_ν = b_ν} in turn, as in #0.1.26), averaged over b ∈ P, gives a₀ with ∂₁a₀ = F on P and ‖a₀‖_P ≤ C(d)ℓ‖F‖_P. Indeed, by Cauchy–Schwarz along the paths, the contraction from b has square norm ≤ C(d)Σ_{ν<μ}ℓ^{ν+1}‖F_{νμ}‖² over the section {x_1 = b_1, …, x_{ν−1} = b_{ν−1}} of P, whose mean over b is ≤ C(d)ℓ²‖F‖²_P. P is simply connected, so u − a₀ = ∂₁ψ_P on P, and ‖u − ∂₁ψ_P‖_P ≤ C(d)ℓ‖F‖_P. For D = Q_s, ψ := ψ_{Q_s}.
  {#A.2-0.1} For D = A′_s, let {#D.S_a} S_a := {x ∈ Q_s : ±x_μ > s/2}, a = μ±, be the 2d slabs of A_s, with sides s/2 and 2s, and ψ_a := ψ_{S_a}. Slabs of one direction are disjoint, and two or three of different directions meet in a box with sides ≥ s/2. On S_a ∩ S_b, ∂₁(ψ_a − ψ_b) = (u − ∂₁ψ_b) − (u − ∂₁ψ_a), so by Poincaré ψ_a − ψ_b = δ_{ab} + r_{ab}, with δ_{ab} its mean and ‖r_{ab}‖_{S_a∩S_b} ≤ C(d)s²‖F‖_{A_s}. On a triple overlap abs(δ_{ab} + δ_{bc} + δ_{ca}) ≤ C(d)ε_A, {#D.ε_A} ε_A := s^{2−d/2}‖F‖_{A_s}.
  {#A.2-0.2} Put c_{1+} := 0, c_a := δ_{a,1+} for the slabs a of directions ≠ 1, and c_{1−} := δ_{1−,2+} + δ_{2+,1+}. Then abs(c_a − c_b − δ_{ab}) ≤ C(d)ε_A for every two slabs that meet, by ≤ 4 triangle relations through a third direction (d ≥ 3). For (a, b) of directions ≠ 1 the triangle is (a, 1+, b). For (1−, b) with b of direction ≠ 1, 2, the triangles are (2+, 1+, b) and (1−, 2+, b). For (1−, 2−), each of δ_{1−,2+}, δ_{2+,1+}, and δ_{1+,2−} is split through 3+, and then (1−, 3+, 2−) is used.

Poincaré on each box and on each such pair bounds the differences of the box means along a chain by C(d)ρ^{1−d/2}‖∂f‖_{Z_D}.

  {#A.9.4-2} The source changes by ∂_U^Tf − ∂_{U_re}^*f = E₁^Tf, and G_𝐁(E₁^Tf) ≤ C(d)αr²ℓ^{−1}sup_{𝐁_x}abs(f) ≤ C(d)αr sup_{𝐁_x}abs(f), of the form of the term G_𝐁∂*f. So for ε₁ ≤ c(d, L, M) the bounds above hold at u_R(B_t), with other constants of d, L, and M.

  {#A.9.5} Write g_t = g₀e^{iηω_t} with ω_t = 0 at t = 0, and {#D.ω.5} ω_1 := ω_t at t = 1; the solution exists on [0, 1] by the bound below and continuity. The bounds above at u_R(B_t) give abs(ηω̃′_t) ≤ C(L, M)sup(L^{j″}η abs(∂_tu_R) + L^{j″}η abs(∂_tU′_ax)), and ∂_tu_R = (δ𝓗/δB)(B_t)[i Im B] and ∂_tU′_ax are bounded as the complex parts above, so abs(ηω̃′_t) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ and abs(ηω′_t) ≤ ‖Ad(g_t^{−1})‖C(L, M)ε₁ ≤ e^{2abs(ηω_t)}C(L, M)ε₁.
  {#A.9.5-1} With {#D.φ.5} φ(z) := (1 − e^{−z})/z, g_t^{−1}∂_tg_t = φ(ad iηω_t)(iη∂_tω_t), and 1/φ(z) = z/(1 − e^{−z}) = 1 + z/2 + z²/12 − z⁴/720 + …, whose coefficients sum in absolute value to < 2, so abs(η∂_tω_t) ≤ 2abs(ηω′_t) while ‖ad(iηω_t)‖ ≤ 2abs(ηω_t) ≤ 1.
  {#A.9.5-2} Let T be the largest t ≤ 1 such that the solution exists on [0, t] with abs(ηω_s) ≤ ½ at every point for s ≤ t. On [0, T], abs(η∂_tω_t) ≤ 2eC(L, M)ε₁, so abs(ηω_t) ≤ 2eC(L, M)ε₁t < ½ for ε₁ ≤ c(L, M), and since the system is finite with an analytic right side, T = 1. So abs(ηω_1) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ ≤ ½ at every point, and ‖Ad(g)‖ = ‖Ad(e^{iηω_1})‖ ≤ e^{‖ad(iηω_1)‖} ≤ e^{2abs(ηω_1)} ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁, Ad(g₀) being an isometry.

  {#A.9.6} *At the interfaces.* Where the chain runs at A_♮ = A_N + ∂ω_♮ for the complex part of the data (#0.1.11, #0.1.30, #A.11.50), the representative is u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} with {#D.g_♮} g_♮ := ge^{−iηω_♮^{im}}, where {#D.ω_♮^im} ω_♮^{im} := ω_♮ for the data i Im B, built in the transports of the real representative u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}}, as the first-order part A_N is. The maps of #A.11.50 are real-linear and preserve 𝔤 there, so abs(ηω_♮^{im}) = abs(ηω_♮(Im B)) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁, by the sup-to-sup bounds of #A.11.50 at the real background.
  {#A.9.6-0.1} ω_♮^{im} ∈ N(Q′) is block-anchored and vanishes on Λ₀, where Q′ = P, so g_♮ = 1 on Λ₀, and ‖Ad(g_♮)‖ ≤ ‖Ad(g)‖e^{2abs(ηω_♮^{im})} ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁.
  {#A.9.6-1} For the data Re B + is Im B, g_♮(s) := g(s)e^{−isηω_♮^{im}}, g(s) the g above at these data, is analytic in s and equals g₀ at s = 0, and g_♮^{−1}∂_sg_♮ = iη(ω′_0 − ω_♮^{im}) at s = 0. So the first-order part of u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} is A_N + ∂ω_♮^{im}, the A_♮ for the data i Im B. At s = 0 it is u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}}, as in #A.9.3, since g_♮ removes only ω_♮^{im}. For abs(s) ≤ c(L, M)/ε₁, abs(sηω_♮^{im}) ≤ ½, so Cauchy's bound on that disc gives its second-order terms ≤ C(L, M)ε₁², as above.
- {#A.10} {#KW} *The Gradient Part (KW).* The steps of #0.1 are written for Bałaban's problem, with {#D.A.2} A := A_N, the *boundary sites* those of the data bonds of Λ₀, on which A = B, and the *free sites* the other sites of Λ; for the N_b problem read u, the mass bonds, and the sites of the mass graph. Exponents are written for d = 4, as in the bound on v of #0.1. Δ is the lattice Laplacian, 2d times the generator 𝓛 of the simple random walk (Lawler–Limic p.17: 𝓛f(y) = −f(y) + Σ_xp(x)f(x + y)), so Δ = −∂*∂ on functions.
  {#A.10-1} {#D.θ} θ := C_H^{reg}θ_B ≥ θ_B is the bulk size: ‖A‖_{Q_{2L}(x₀)} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}L^{d/2}θ for every x₀ of the region of #A.11.21-1, and in their units in the regions of #A.11.21-2, by #A.11.23-2 (for every x₀ by the weighted L² decay of #0.1.17-2 in the N_b problem), with {#D.p_θ} p_θ := the least integer ≥ 4 that is at least the exponents of 1 + log L in the bounds derived in #A.11.20–#A.11.23 and #0.1.17-2, C_H^{reg}'s included. In the N_b problem E(Q_L(x₀)) ≤ Ē = C(d)(1 + log L)^{2p_θ}L^{d−2}θ² (#0.1.20) by Caccioppoli at the scale L.
  {#A.10-1-1} Every random-walk event used below depends on the walk only up to its exit from a cube of radius ≤ L, on which the torus, of side > 48L (#0.1.25), agrees with ℤ^d, so Lawler–Limic's estimates for ℤ^d apply.
  {#A.10-2} In VAR's problem the energy of A_N near a face of Λ₀ is of order L^{d−1}θ_B² per block, and Ē is the bulk bound ‖da‖²_{Q_L(x₀)} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{2p_θ}L^{d−2}θ² of the residual a = A_N − E (#A.11.5, #A.11.23-2). The curvature of A_N enters the rest only through F₁ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}θ, the part ∂₁*Δ^{−1}(χdE) of v_{x̄} (#0.1.25–#0.1.25-2), the interior bound of #0.1.26.4, and the source ℓ_E of the hole-filling (#0.1.30).
  {#A.10-3} A *local component* at a cube Q′ is a component of the graph of the data bonds (mass bonds) in Q′. Inside Q_{L/8} two cells of Λ₀ (of Λ^c) that share a face lie in one local component, two that meet only in codimension ≥ 2 do so only through a chain of face-sharing cells (#0.1.18-4-0.1), and sites of two distinct local components at distance ≤ ρ lie within C(d)ρ of a contact between them, the cells having sides ≥ L. t₃ is that of #0.1.18-4.
  - {#A.11} {#K0} {#A.11.1} (K0) Weighted decay for VAR's problem (at the flat base U = 1, and at a real base with the additive constant δ_U ≤ 1 of #A.11.1.1–#A.11.1.6). ℓ(x) denotes the side of the block of the layer containing x (1 on Λ₀, L^j on Λ_j), and "local units" are those of ℓ.

    {#A.11.1.1} *At a real base.* In #A.9–#A.11.1, M is PBG's block size and R₁M₁ is VAR's product, both M′ = M′(d, L) on the chain's sequences (BP_JOINS_BLOCK_SIZE #4.22, #4.23–#4.23-0, #4.26, #4.27–#4.27-0; #T2.7-1, #T2.10). So every C(L, M) there is a constant of d and L.
    {#A.11.1.1-0.1} PBG's constants are uniform in M ≥ M₁ (p.397 l.38), so the covariant maps' (P2) constant K below depends on M′ only through the factor e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′} of #A.11.1.3 (#A.11.1.4.3.2), their (P3) constant K₃ being a C(L, M′), and a = c(L, M′)a₁ with PBG's a₁ of Theorem 3.4, a constant of d and L (#T1.4). The large-field M (#4.22.2) enters only through ε₁. The steps of (K0) and (KW) are taken at the flat base U = 1. Their pointwise conclusions hold at a real base U (defined below), point by point, with an additive constant δ_U ≤ 1.
    {#A.11.1.1-0.2} *Real regular* means G-valued and satisfying PBG (3.35)–(3.36) (p.396) on PBG's class cubes, the unions of M′-blocks of #T11.25, with M′α₀ ≤ a₀, a₀ the threshold of PBG Theorem 3.1 (p.397 l.38), and with α₀ below the threshold of Theorem 3.12 ("for α₀ sufficiently small", p.423 l.34), which #A.11.1.3–#A.11.1.4 use, an upper bound on ε₁ (#A.11.1.6); the covariant maps' constants below are uniform in such α₀.
    {#A.11.1.1-1} At the minimisers this is VAR Theorem 1 (9)–(10) (p.279) on VAR's class cubes, which is how VAR applies PBG at its base (p.280 l.51–53; H₁ with PBG's B₀ at (103), p.293). These conditions ask for a gauge on each cube, so they are gauge invariant. U₀ = U_k(V₀) and the minimisers U_k(V′V₀) at real data are real regular (VAR Theorem 1; (172)–(173), p.305, with B₃(1 + 4C₁)ε₁ at p.305 l.41), and so are their G-valued transforms, such as u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}} (#A.9.3, #A.9.6). These are the {#D.real_base} *real bases* := the minimisers at real data on the chain's sequence and their G-valued transforms.
    {#A.11.1.1-1-1} Their data satisfy VAR (7) with the parameter C_Vε₁, {#D.C_V} C_V := 1 + C(d)LC₁: V₀ at ε₁; for V′V₀, abs(V′ − 1) < C₁ε₁ by (172), a plaquette inside a layer has four bonds, and on a plaquette crossing ∂Λ_j VAR (7) reads V̄ on the bonds outside Λ_j (p.278 l.40–45), an average along ≤ C(d)L finer bonds. VAR assumes C₁ to be an absolute constant (p.305 l.44), B₅ = 6B₁B₃C₁ being one with it, and C₁ = L³ at p.280 l.20, so it is taken as a constant of d and L, and so is C_V. VAR Theorem 1 at the parameter C_Vε₁, which is ≤ VAR's a₁ for ε₁ small, gives them (9)–(10) on each of VAR's class cubes with C_Vε₁ in place of ε₁.
    {#A.11.1.1-2} A *covariant map* is a family of real-linear maps 𝒯(U) from the data to fields, defined at the real regular U and at the configurations e^{iηA′} of (3.37)–(3.38) about the base 1 with α₁ ≤ a, with constants a = c(L, M), K = C(L, M) in (P2), K₃ = C(L, M) in (P3), and c = c(L) such that, in local units and with θ_B the supremum of the data (#0.1.27), the following hold. (P1) 𝒯(U^g)B^g = (𝒯(U)B)^g for every G-valued gauge g, B^g being the data transformed at the block points (REG p.78 l.14).
    {#A.11.1.1-3} (P2) If two real regular U, U′ agree on a union □′ of blocks, then abs((𝒯(U) − 𝒯(U′))B(x)) ≤ Ke^{−c·d(x, □′^c)}θ_B at every point x, with d(x, □′^c) := 0 for x ∉ □′. Here d is PBG's weighted distance (p.397 l.29), PRT2 (2.46) (p.231; PBG cites it as (2.36) of its [4], which is PRT2, p.433 l.53), in which a path in B^i(Λ_i) has (L^iη)^{−1} times its length. (P3) For A′ with values in 𝔤 and e^{iηA′} in (3.37)–(3.38) about 1 with α₁ = α, the map s ↦ 𝒯(e^{iηsA′})B(x) is analytic on abs(s) ≤ a/α and bounded by K₃θ_B there.

    {#A.11.1.2} *The comparison.* Let 𝒯 be a covariant map, U a real base (#A.11.1.1), y a point of the layer j, and W′ ≥ 1 a weight, with the flat constant K_♭ := sup_{B′}‖𝒯(1)B′‖_{W′}/θ_{B′}. Then abs(𝒯(U)B(y)) ≤ W′(y)K_♭θ_B + δθ_B, with δ := Ke^{−cM_□/(4L)} + 4K₃α_□/a and α_□ := C(d)L⁴C_VB₃M_□ε₁, a C(L)B₃M_□ε₁ with C_V of #A.11.1.1, so ‖𝒯(U)B‖_{W′} ≤ (K_♭ + δ)θ_B. Here M_□ is a multiple of R₁M₁ (VAR's M in Theorem 1), with M_□ ≥ C(d)LR₁M₁.
    {#A.11.1.2-0.1} Take the class cube □ of VAR (p.279 l.2–4) about y. If y lies at distance ≥ (M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁)L^jη from Ω_j^c, □ has the index j and the size 2M_□L^jη. Otherwise it has the index j − 1 and the size 2M′_□L^{j−1}η, with M′_□ the least multiple of R₁M₁ that is ≥ L(M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁). In both cases □ is a union of big blocks whose centre lies in a big block of y, C(d)R₁M₁ covering this shift and the margin 2R₁M₁ of □̃.
    {#A.11.1.2-0.2} Every layer of the chain's sequences (CRE's 𝐁, 𝐁″_k, and the joins) below the top one is at least R′M′ ≥ ½LM₁ wide in its units (BP_JOINS_BLOCK_SIZE #4.24, #4.27-0; BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.18-2-2, #4.17); the top layer of 𝐁₂ can be thin (BP_LAYER_WIDTHS #4.14). Write RM for this least width (PRT2 (2.2)). The widths used below are those of the layers j + 1 (first case, to miss Ω_{j+2}), j (second case, to miss Ω_{j+1}), and j − 1 (second case); when the layer j or j + 1 is the top one, the set to be missed is empty, so the top width is not used; by the choice of M₁/M′ in #A.11.1.6, RM ≥ C(d)L(M_□ + R₁M₁).
    {#A.11.1.2-1} In the first case □̃ contains y ∉ Ω_{j+1} and lies in Ω_j ∖ Ω_{j+2}. In the second it contains a point of Ω_j^c, lies in Ω_{j−1}, and misses Ω_{j+1}, which is at distance ≥ (RM − M_□ − C(d)R₁M₁)L^jη from y. The second case needs the index j − 1, so at j = 0 only the first case is used, and it suffices.
    {#A.11.1.2-1-1} On the data bonds of Λ₀ the maps to which this comparison is applied return the datum independently of U: Q(U) is the identity there, so H₁(U)B = B; ω_H and ω_♮ lie in N(Q′) and vanish on Λ₀, where Q′ = P, so A_N(U)B = A_♮ = B; and f_ξ = 0, so 𝒫_Uξ = 0 there (#A.11.1.4–#A.11.1.5). So 𝒯(U)B = 𝒯(1)B there, and the claim holds with the δ term unused. The other bonds of Λ₀ touch Ω₁, at distance ≥ RMη ≥ (M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁)η from Ω₀^c, where the first case applies. This covers the sequences whose Ω₀ is not the whole lattice, such as 𝐁₂, supported in (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c (LFR II p.370 l.23; #4.261).
    {#A.11.1.2-1-2} So □ is in VAR's class, with the index j_□ ∈ {j − 1, j} and the size parameter {#D.M̂_□} M̂_□ := M_□ in the first case and M′_□ in the second, M̂_□ ≤ C(d)LM_□, and M̂_□ ≤ M(C_Vε₁) = R₁M₁a₁/(C_Vε₁) for ε₁ small. VAR Theorem 1 gives a G-valued gauge u, extended G-valued to all points, with U^{u^{−1}} = e^{iηA₀} on □ and the bounds (9)–(10) at C_Vε₁ (#A.11.1.1). Let χ be 1 on the middle half □_{1/2}, a union of big blocks, and 0 off □, with abs(∇^kχ) ≤ C(d)(M̂_□L^{j_□}η)^{−k} for k ≤ 2.
    {#A.11.1.2-2} Then U_□ := e^{iηχA₀} on □, and 1 elsewhere, is real regular with α₀ = α_□/M′, the gauge 1 serving on every class cube, each of size ≥ 10M′, and M′α₀ = α_□ ≤ a₀ for ε₁ small; it lies in (3.37)–(3.38) about 1 with α₁ = α_□: by (9)–(10) and the product rule, abs(χA₀), abs(∇(χA₀)), and abs(∂*∂(χA₀)) are ≤ C(d)C_VB₃M̂_□ε₁(L^{j_□}η)^{−k}, k = 1, 2, 3, and the points of □ in the layer j_□ + 1 carry the factor L^k.
    {#A.11.1.2-3} By (P1), Ad(u(y)) being an isometry, abs(𝒯(U)B(y)) = abs(𝒯(U^{u^{−1}})B_u(y)), with B_u := B^{u^{−1}} and θ_{B_u} = θ_B. U^{u^{−1}} and U_□ agree on □_{1/2}. A path from y out of □_{1/2} has length ≥ M_□L^jη/2 − C(d)R₁M₁L^jη in B^{j_□}(Λ_{j_□}) ∪ B^{j_□+1}(Λ_{j_□+1}), so d(y, □_{1/2}^c) ≥ M_□/(4L), and (P2) gives abs((𝒯(U^{u^{−1}}) − 𝒯(U_□))B_u(y)) ≤ Ke^{−cM_□/(4L)}θ_B. Along s ↦ e^{iηsχA₀}, (P3) and Cauchy's bound on the disc abs(s) ≤ a/α_□, of radius ≥ 2, give abs((𝒯(U_□) − 𝒯(1))B_u(y)) ≤ 2K₃θ_B/(a/α_□ − 1) ≤ 4K₃α_□θ_B/a. Finally abs(𝒯(1)B_u(y)) ≤ W′(y)K_♭θ_B, and dividing by W′(y) ≥ 1 gives the claim.

    {#A.11.1.3} *H and H₁ are covariant maps.* (P1) holds by PBG (3.32)–(3.34) (pp.395–396) for G′, R, Q, Δ_a, and the G of (3.34), which is G₀ of Sect. D. J = D*η^{−2} Im ∂U (p.419 l.11) and C^{(2)}_j are covariant, hence so are Δ′_π (3.120), G (3.130), (QGQ*)^{−1}, and H (3.126) (p.420), and Δ_π^{(2)}, G₁, and H₁ by (3.128)–(3.129) (p.421) and (3.134)–(3.138) (pp.422–423).
    {#A.11.1.3-0.1} (P2): by Theorem 3.12 (p.423), Theorem 3.10's expansion (3.107)–(3.108) holds for H and H₁ at real U satisfying (3.35)–(3.36) with α₀ small. Each walk term depends on U only on X̃₀⁵ ∪ … ∪ X̃_n⁵ (p.416 l.7–8) and is bounded as in (3.108), with the factors of (3.133). If U and U′ agree on □′, the terms of the walks with every X̃ᵢ⁵ ⊂ □′ coincide.
    {#A.11.1.3-0.2} Any other walk has a domain Xᵢ with X̃ᵢ⁵ ∩ □′^c ≠ ∅, so d(ω, x, y′) ≥ d(x, Xᵢ) ≥ d(x, □′^c) − C(d)LM, by (3.93) (p.410) and the triangle inequality, X̃ᵢ⁵ lying within d-distance C(d)LM of Xᵢ, since it can reach the layer j − 1 (BP_JOINS_BLOCK_SIZE #4.25), where PRT2 (2.46) weights a path by (L^{j−1}η)^{−1}.
    {#A.11.1.3-0.3} Half of the factor e^{−½δ₀d(ω,x,y′)} gives e^{−¼δ₀(d(x,□′^c) − C(d)LM)}. The other half pays the sum over y′ by PRT2's count (2.57)–(2.59), as at #0.1.12, and the walk sum converges by the factors O(M^{−1/2})^{abs(ω)} as in PBG. So (P2) holds with c = δ₀/4 and K = C(L)e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′}, M = M′ (#A.11.1.1), δ₀ being the common rate of these operators (p.423 l.39–40).
    {#A.11.1.3-1} (P3): Theorem 3.4 (p.400) gives G′, (Q′G′²Q′*)^{−1}, R, and G₀ analytic on (3.37) for α₁ ≤ a₁, with the bounds of Theorems 3.1–3.3; the G of Theorem 3.4 is the G₀ = (Δ + DRD* + Q*aQ)^{−1} of Sect. D (p.421 l.33). Along s ↦ U(s) := e^{iηsA′}, abs(s) ≤ s₁ := a₁/α, J(U(s)), the continuation of D*η^{−2} Im ∂U with U(∂p)^{−1} in place of U(∂p)*, and Δ′_π(U(s)) of (3.120) (built from G′, R, D, and J) are analytic and bounded by C(L, M) in the norms of (3.131) (p.422). Both vanish at s = 0, where J = 0 and Δ_π = Δ (p.419; #A.11.25).
    {#A.11.1.3-2} By the Schwarz lemma, applied to each kernel entry, they are ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₁ on abs(s) ≤ s₁. So, for abs(s) ≤ s₂ := c(L, M)s₁, the series (3.130) for G converges as on p.422 l.12–13. (QGQ*(U(s)))^{−1} is the Neumann series about U = 1, with (3.132) at U = 1 and the difference QGQ*(U(s)) − QGQ*(1) ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₂ by Cauchy's bound, convergent for abs(s) ≤ c(L, M)s₂.
    {#A.11.1.3-3} H follows by (3.126); Δ^{(2)} and Δ_π^{(2)} by (3.134)–(3.136), with abs(H*J) ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₁; G₁ by (3.138) (p.423); (QG₁Q*)^{−1} as for G; and H₁ by (3.129). Each is analytic and bounded by C(L, M) on abs(s) ≤ s₂ (shrinking s₂ by a factor c(L, M) at each step), so (P3) holds with a = c(L, M)a₁.

    {#A.11.1.4} *A_N is a covariant map.* At a real regular U let {#D.A_N(U)} A_N(U)B := H₁(U)B − D_Uω_H(U)B, with ω_H(U)B the element of N(Q′(U)) least for ‖H₁(U)B − D_Uω‖. The part ⟨A, Δ_πA⟩ − 2⟨HC_π^{(2)}(A), J⟩ of (3.128) is invariant under the gauges of N(Q′(U)), A − DG′RD*A being so (p.419 l.26–28). Every A is carried by such a gauge to A − DG′RD*A, which has RD*(A − DG′RD*A) = 0 ((3.119), p.419), and Q(D_Uλ) = D̄Q′λ = 0 for λ ∈ N(Q′(U)) (PBG (3.115), p.418).
    {#A.11.1.4-0.0} So, as in #A.11.25, the minimisers of that part under QA = B form the class H₁(U)B + D_UN(Q′(U)), H₁(U)B being the minimiser with RD*A = 0 ((3.127)–(3.129), p.421). A_N(U)B is the ℓ²-least element of this class.
    {#A.11.1.4-0.1} #A.9's A_N at the base U is A_N(U)B + 𝒫_Uξ_ω + Π_Ue_a, with the terms of #A.11.1.4.1, which vanish at U = 1 and are bounded in #A.11.1.4.1.1–#A.11.1.4.3.3. At U = 1, where J = 0 and Δ′_π = Δ_π^{(2)} = 0, so H₁(1) = H₀, it is the split's A_N = H₀B − ∂ω_H (#A.11.25). (P1) holds since the ℓ² norm is Ad-invariant and D_U and Q′(U) are covariant.

    {#A.11.2} {#K0.a} (a) The normalisation and the variational form. In the normalisation of RG I (0.4), whose weights are L^{−d} (p.253), Q(∂ζ) = D̄Q′ζ: the line integral of ∂ζ along [x, x′] is ζ(x′) − ζ(x), and its average over x ∈ B(c₋) is Q′ζ(c₊) − Q′ζ(c₋), with the transports of PBG (3.19) at a non-flat base. PBG (3.114)–(3.115) (p.418) write the same identity with scaled derivatives, in the normalisation of CMP98 (14) (p.19), with weights L^{−(d+1)}; there it reads Q(∂ζ) = L^{−1}D̄Q′ζ, and Q̃ = Q − L^{−1}D̄K.
    {#A.11.2-1} QA_N = Q̃U′_ax = B, since Q∂ζ^N = D̄Q′ζ^N = −D̄KU′_ax (#0.1.4). By #A.8, ⟨dA_N, dt⟩ = ⟨μ, Q̃t⟩ = ⟨μ, Qt⟩ with D̄*μ = 0 for every t vanishing on the data bonds of Λ₀. So A_N minimises ‖da‖² on {#D.𝒞.2} 𝒞 := {a = B on the data bonds, Qa = B}, the problem being convex. Let {#D.ker Q} ker Q := {D : D = 0 on the data bonds, QD = 0}. The gauges ∂λ in ker Q are those with λ ∈ N(Q′), up to a constant: λ is constant on the data graph of Λ₀, and D̄Q′λ = 0 on the connected graph of 𝔅_k, so Q′λ is one constant, which λ takes on Λ₀. A_N is least in ℓ² on A_N + ∂N(Q′) (#0.1.4).

    {#A.11.3} {#K0.b} (b) The fine data. The *faces* are the facets, of side L, of the blocks of side L of Λ₀ that lie in ∂Λ₀; for a face f, {#D.Y_f} Y_f := the block of which f is a facet, and {#D.H₋(f)} H₋(f) := the half-space bounded by f's plane on the side of Y_f, f's interior half-space. Let B_f be B on the bonds of f's plane in Λ₀ and 0 on its other bonds, s the depth from the plane, and P_s(x′, y′) the probability that the walk from (x′, s) first meets the plane at y′. The walk meets the plane with probability 1, its normal coordinate being recurrent.
    {#A.11.3-1} P_·(·, y′) is nonnegative and harmonic on the ball of radius s/2 about (x′, s), and Σ_{y′}P_s(x′, y′) = 1. So Lawler–Limic Theorem 6.3.8 (p.131) gives, by (6.19)–(6.20) and, for the mixed second differences ∇_e∇_{e′}P, by (6.17) applied to the harmonic function ∇_{e′}P_·(·, y′) on the ball of radius s/4 about (x′, s), which is ≤ C(d)s^{−1}P_s(x′, y′) there by (6.19) at its points and the Harnack inequality (Theorem 6.3.9, with a constant of d for this pair of balls), Σ_{y′}abs(∇P_s(x′, y′)) ≤ C(d)/s and Σ_{y′}abs(∇²P_s(x′, y′)) ≤ C(d)/s² for s above a threshold of d, and ≤ C(d) below it.
    {#A.11.3-2} Put {#D.F_tan(s)} F_tan(s) := P_s(dB_f), harmonic at depth ≥ 1 with the values dB_f on the plane, and {#D.F_n·(s)} F_{n·}(s) := −Σ_{s′>s}∂*_tanF_tan(s′). Summation by parts moves one difference, and the two of ∂*_tanF_tan, onto P_s. So abs(F_tan(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1), abs(∂*_tanF_tan(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1)², and abs(F_{n·}(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1).

    {#A.11.4} {#D.F_f} F_f := (F_tan, F_{n·}) is closed: d_tanF_tan = 0, and ∂_nF_tan = d_tanF_{n·} by the telescoping sum of Δ_nF_tan = −Δ_tanF_tan = d_tan∂*_tanF_tan. It is co-closed at every bond off the plane. At the tangential ones F_{n·}(s) − F_{n·}(s − 1) = ∂*_tanF_tan(s), and at the normal ones ∂*_tanF_{n·} = −Σ_{s′}∂*_tan∂*_tanF_tan(s′) = 0.
    {#A.11.4-0.0} Let E_f be the axial field equal to B_f + Σ_{s′<s}F_{n·}(s′) on the tangential bonds at depth s and to 0 on the normal ones. Then dE_f = F_f, d*dE_f = 0 off the plane, E_f = B on f, and abs(E_f) ≤ C(d)θ_B(1 + log max(s, 1)). Since B_f is B on all the bonds of f's plane in Λ₀, F_f and E_f depend on f only through its plane and the side of H₋(f).
    {#A.11.4-0.1} The *strata* are the (d − 2)-dimensional faces of the faces, among them the strata of codimension ≥ 2 of ∂Λ₀ and the contacts of distinct local components (#A.10). The closure of f is the set of the data bonds in the plane of the outer sites of Y_f next to f that have an endpoint among these sites.
    {#A.11.4-0.2} Let {χ_f} be a partition of unity on the free bonds within L/16 of Λ₀, homogeneous of degree 0 about each stratum (angular sectors), with abs(∇χ_f) ≤ C(d)/max(r, 1), r the distance to the strata. On a free bond χ_f is its value at the endpoint farther from Λ₀ (either, if the two are equally far). On the data bonds χ_f := 1/n_b on the bonds b of the closure of f, n_b the number of faces whose closures contain b, so Σ_fχ_f = 1 on the edge bonds as well, and χ_f := 0 on the other data bonds.
    {#A.11.4-1} χ_f vanishes on the free bonds of H₋(f), at the sites x whose foot on f's plane lies off f with dist(x, f's plane) ≤ c(d)dist(x, ∂f), and, for each other face f′ whose closure meets that of f in S, at the sites x with dist(x, f′) ≤ c(d)dist(x, S). On the free sites such a partition is {#D.χ_f} χ_f := ψ_f/Σ_{f′}ψ_{f′} with {#D.ψ_f} ψ_f := ζ(dist(·, f)/dist(·, Λ₀))ζ₁(s_f/dist(·, Λ₀)), s_f the signed depth from f's plane, positive off H₋(f), ζ = 1 on [1, 1 + c(d)] and 0 on [1 + 2c(d), ∞), and ζ₁ = 0 on (−∞, 1/(4√d)] and 1 on [1/(2√d), ∞).
    {#A.11.4-1-1} Let p be the point of Λ₀ nearest to x and σ ∋ p a block of Λ₀. Then x − p = Σ_μλ_μn_μ, λ_μ ≥ 0, over the outward normals n_μ of the facets of σ through p, one per direction. Those with λ_μ > 0 are faces, since otherwise the block across, which contains p + εn_μ for small ε > 0, would contain points closer to x. So some λ_μ ≥ dist(x, Λ₀)/√d, that face has ψ = 1, and Σψ ≥ 1. The distances are homogeneous of degree 1 about each stratum.
    {#A.11.4-2} For c(d) small, ζ or ζ₁ vanishes where the conditions above require: on H₋(f), s_f ≤ 0; where the foot lies off f with s_f ≤ c(d)dist(x, ∂f), dist(x, f) = dist(x, ∂f), so either s_f ≤ dist(x, Λ₀)/(4√d) or the ratio is ≥ 1/(4√dc(d)); and where dist(x, f′) ≤ c(d)dist(x, S) for another face f′, dist(x, S) ≤ √2(dist(x, f) + dist(x, f′)), so the ratio is ≥ dist(x, f)/dist(x, f′) ≥ (1/√2 − c(d))/c(d).
    {#A.11.4-2-1} Here the closures of f and f′ are products of a point and intervals in single coordinates, meeting in S, and the distance to the intersection of two such products is ≤ √2 times the sum of the distances to them, coordinate by coordinate. Let D := dist(x, Λ₀). If r ≥ 3D/2 + 4 at x, then the ball B(x, 3D/2 + 4), of diameter < L for L ≥ 128, meets no stratum and meets at most one hyperplane of the block faces in each direction.
    {#A.11.4-2-2} So ∂Λ₀ ∩ B(x, 3D/2 + 4) consists of hyperplane sections of the ball, each inside one face, at most one per direction, and two of different directions within (1 + 2c(d))(D + 1) + 1 of x would meet within √2((1 + 2c(d))(D + 1) + 1) < 3D/2 + 4 of x in a stratum. Hence at both endpoints of a bond at x only the face of p is within the factor 1 + 2c(d) of dist(·, Λ₀), with s_f = dist(·, Λ₀), and every χ_f is constant on the bond. On the other bonds abs(∇ψ_f) ≤ C(d)/max(D, 1) ≤ C(d)/max(r, 1).
    {#A.11.4-3} There the arguments of ζ and ζ₁ are ratios to dist(·, Λ₀) ≥ 1/2 of 1-Lipschitz functions, bounded by 2 where ψ_f ≠ 0, and at most C(d) faces meet Q_{L/8}(x). So abs(∇χ_f) ≤ C(d)/max(r, 1). On supp χ_f, dist(·, Λ₀) ≤ dist(·, f) ≤ (1 + 2c(d))dist(·, Λ₀) and s_f ≥ dist(·, Λ₀)/(4√d), so dist(·, f) ≤ C(d)s. Also dist(·, Λ₀) ≤ r.
    {#A.11.4-3-1} For x ∈ supp χ_f, the points q of H₋(f) off Λ₀ and of Λ₀ off H₋(f) have abs(q − x) ≥ min(r, L/8)/(6√d). Otherwise, with R′ := abs(q − x), s_f ≤ R′ or dist(x, Λ₀) ≤ R′, so dist(x, f) ≤ 5√dR′ by these bounds, and B(x, 6√dR′) meets no stratum and meets f.
    {#A.11.4-3-2} Its sections of ∂Λ₀ are then as above, that of f's plane lies in f, and the segment from x to q crosses a second one: x is free, Λ₀ lies next to f on the side of H₋(f) and the free set on the other, and q lies in Λ₀ off H₋(f) or off Λ₀ in H₋(f). That section is orthogonal to f's plane and within R′ of x, so the two would meet within √2(1 + 2c(d))R′ < 6√dR′ of x, in a stratum. Let χ_d be a cutoff in the distance to Λ₀, equal to 1 below L/32 and 0 above L/16.

    {#A.11.5} Put {#D.E.5} E := B on the data bonds and {#D.E.6} E := χ_dΣ_fχ_fE_f on the free bonds. Then abs(E) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B. The coarse data of the residual, {#D.B′.2} B′ := B − QE, are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)Lθ_B in field units, θ_B bounding the coarse data as well (#0.1.27), and ‖E‖_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)L^{d/2}θ_B per block y. The residual {#D.a} a := A_N − E vanishes on the data bonds and has Qa = B′.
    {#A.11.5-1} Its linear term is {#D.ℓ_E(T)} ℓ_E(T) := ⟨dE, dT⟩, which depends only on dT. So each of its terms below may be evaluated at its own representative {#D.T̂_f} T̂_f := T − ∂Ĝ_f, with the cone potential Ĝ_f defined now.
    {#A.11.5-1-1} Let {#D.m_f} m_f := max(dist(·, Y_f), 1). Put {#D.Ĝ_f} Ĝ_f := 0 on Y_f and at the sites of Λ₀ joined to Y_f by data bonds of f's closure (the seam sites), and {#D.Ĝ_f.2} Ĝ_f := G^{Y_f}_T at the other sites, G^{Y_f}_T being G^Y of (d) for Y = Y_f, with T for D and m_f for m (min(m_f, L) in the shift of c_Y and in the radius of B_Y; m_f ≤ C(d)L on supp χ_dχ_f). T vanishes on the data bonds, so T̂_f = 0 on the bonds of Y_f and on the data bonds of f's closure.
    {#A.11.5-2} Off Y_f and the seam sites, T̂_f = T − ∂G^{Y_f}_T obeys the strip bound of D̃^Y. On a bond from a seam site y′, T̂_f differs from T − ∂G^{Y_f}_T by G^{Y_f}_T(y′), which, compared with the sum of T along a path of data bonds from Y_f to y′, is ≤ C(d) times the sum of abs(dT) over the plaquettes within C(d) of y′, so the strip bound holds there with m_f = 1.

    {#A.11.6} So abs(T̂_f(x, x + e_μ)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p∈Q_{Cm_f(x)}(x)}abs(dT(p))max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d}. The Schur test of (d) gives ‖T̂_f/m_f‖_Q ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}‖dT‖_{Q⁺}, Q⁺ the neighbourhood of Q at the scale of Q, and m_f ≤ max(dist(·, f), 1) ≤ C(d)max(s, 1) on supp χ_f.
    {#A.11.6-1} With the discrete product rule, d*F_f = 0 on the free bonds of supp χ_f, and T̂_f = 0 on the data bonds of f's closure, ℓ_E(T) = −Σ_f⟨χ_dF_f, ∇χ_f ∧ T̂_f⟩ + ⟨χ_dΣ_f∇χ_f ∧ (E_f − E_{f₀}), dT⟩ + (the same two terms with ∇χ_d), f₀ at each bond a face with χ_{f₀} ≠ 0 there, so that the bond lies off H₋(f₀), where E_{f₀} is defined, up to commutator terms of the same form.
    {#A.11.6-2} In the overlaps of the sectors dist(·, Λ₀) is comparable to r, abs(F_f) ≤ C(d)θ_B/r, and abs(E_f − E_{f₀}) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B. So abs(ℓ_E(T)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)³Σ_yS_y‖dT‖_{y⁺}, with S_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}L^{d/2−1}θ_B per block y of side L, S_y² being the sum of θ_B²/min(max(r, 1), L)² over the free sites of the block within L/16 of Λ₀, near which lie C(d) strata of size L^{d−2}, the cap at L covering the terms with ∇χ_d, of size ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B/L, in the shell L/32 ≤ dist(·, Λ₀) ≤ L/16. On a cube Q_ρ, ρ ≤ L, about a point of a stratum, S(Q_ρ)² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)ρ^{d−2}θ_B², a source of Morrey exponent d − 2 > α.

    {#A.11.7} {#K0.c} (c) The coarse data and the gauge.

    {#A.11.8} *The two-layer problem 𝒫₁.* Let {#D.Ω₂} Ω₂ := ∪_{j≥2}B^j(Λ_j) (PRT2 (2.4)), and let 𝒞₁ ⊂ 𝒞 be cut out by the further constraints Q₁A = Q₁A_N on the scale-1 bonds with an endpoint in Ω₂, the crossing bonds from Λ₁ into Λ₂ included (constrained by no layer at the scale 1, which VAR leaves free: a bond of a plaquette of Λ_j that is not in Λ_j has both endpoints in Λ_{j−1}, VAR p.278 l.39–42, and REG p.81).
    {#A.11.8-0.1} With Q₁A = B on the other scale-1 bonds of Ω₁ and Q_j = Q^{(j−1)}Q₁ (PBG (3.15), p.393), they fix Q_jA at A_N's values on the bonds of the layers Λ_j, j ≥ 2, and on those read by VAR's coarse crossing constraints at Λ_j/Λ_{j+1}, j ≥ 1, which are constraints on Q_jA (#A.11.29); so these constraints hold on 𝒞₁ and are redundant there. A_N ∈ 𝒞₁, so A_N is least on 𝒞₁.
    {#A.11.8-1} 𝒫₁'s gauge group {λ: λ = 0 on Λ₀, Q′₁λ = 0 on Ω₁} lies in that of the full problem, so A_N is least on its orbit under it; in (c)–(f) N(Q′) denotes this group. 𝒫₁ has the single interface Λ₀/Ω₁; in (c)–(f) ℓ is its local unit, 1 on Λ₀ and L on Ω₁, and {#D.ℓ_ms} ℓ_ms := L^j on Λ_j is that of the full problem, so ℓ ≤ ℓ_ms.
    {#A.11.8-2} Let {#D.𝒰} 𝒰 := the union of the blocks Ω_c of these bonds c, and {#D.Ã′} Ã′ := 1_𝒰A_N + Σ_c(B′(c) − Q(1_𝒰A_N)(c))β_c over the other block bonds c, with the bumps β_c of #0.1.33.1, supported in the interior of Ω_c, of size 1/ℓ, with Qβ_c = δ_c. E is supported within L/16 of Λ₀ and Λ₁ is ≥ RM wide, so QE = 0 on the bonds with an endpoint in Ω₂, and a has the data Q₁A_N there.
    {#A.11.8-3} Then QÃ′ = B′ on the other block bonds, QÃ′ = Q₁A_N on these bonds, Ã′ = 0 on the data bonds, and per block off the 2L-neighbourhood of 𝒰, ‖dÃ′‖_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)ℓ^{d/2−1}θ_B and ‖Ã′‖_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)ℓ^{d/2}θ_B, in the units of θ; near 𝒰, Ã′ is bounded through ℳ of (f).

    {#A.11.9} VAR has no constraints on the bonds of the scale j from Λ_j into Λ_{j+1} (#A.11.8), and PRT2 Lemma 2.4's problem has none on the unit bonds from Λ^c into Λ, which are bonds of Λ (p.245; #0.1.31). Let 𝒳 be a choice, for each j, of one scale-j crossing bond into each sub-block y′ ⊂ Λ_{j+1} joined to Λ_j. Every class of ker Q modulo ∂N(Q′) has representatives vanishing on 𝒳 (Q_j vanishing there at the scale j): a λ ∈ N(Q′) with the prescribed means Q′_jλ(y′) at the endpoints of 𝒳, its block means restored by bumps in the other sub-blocks, removes the 𝒳-values.
    {#A.11.9-1} The problem for a − Ã′ ∈ ker Q is gauge-invariant: its class minimises {#D.Φ(D)} Φ(D) := ‖dD‖² + 2Re(ℓ_E(D) + ⟨dÃ′, dD⟩) on ker Q modulo ∂N(Q′), and ⟨dD, dT⟩ = −ℓ_E(T) − ⟨dÃ′, dT⟩ for every T ∈ ker Q and every representative D. For a weight g > 0, the g-Landau representative of a class is the one with ‖gℓ^{−1}D‖ least on D + ∂N(Q′), ℓ on a bond being the larger of its endpoints' values.

    {#A.11.10} {#K0.d} (d) The gap in local units. The claim is ‖ℓ^{−1}D₁‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖ for the 1-Landau representative D₁ of every class, for L ≥ 128 (#0.1.37). Let D ∈ ker Q vanish on 𝒳. Its values on the other crossing bonds are of two kinds.

    {#A.11.11} (α) Where the two endpoints in the finer layer are joined by a path of length ≤ C(d) of constrained bonds (data bonds of Λ₀; at the scale j, scale-j bonds of Λ_j), the value differs from that on the bond of 𝒳 by a sum of dD over C(d) plaquettes. At the scale j it is a sum of averages of dD over squares of side L^j, the lines of the four averages of a scale-j plaquette being paired by translation.

    {#A.11.12} (β) At a contact of codimension 2 between two distinct local components K₁, K₂ of Λ₀ (#0.1.29), a corner site x′ has crossing bonds b₁ ∈ 𝒳 to K₁ and b₂ to K₂, and the jump {#D.J(x′)} J(x′) := D(b₂) − D(b₁), which is D(b₂) since D(b₁) = 0, is gauge-invariant. It is bounded through the coarse crossing constraints.
    {#A.11.12-0.1} In the cross-section of the contact, the blocks of side L about it are Y₁ ⊂ K₁, y ⊂ Λ₁, Y₂ ⊂ K₂, and a fourth, and y shares a face with Y₁ and with Y₂, say Y₁ = y + Le₁ and Y₂ = y − Le₂. Their coarse crossing averages are QD(Y₁, y) = avg_{x∈Y₁}D([x, x − Le₁]) and QD(Y₂, y) = avg_{x₂∈Y₂}D([x₂, x₂ + Le₂]), and both vanish.
    {#A.11.12-1} Pair {#D.x₂.2} x₂ := x − Le₁ − Le₂, so that both lines end at {#D.z₁} z₁ := x − Le₁. The loop x → z₁ → x₂ → x′ → x, closed through straight paths in K₂ and in K₁ and through b₂ and b₁, has D = 0 on its data bonds. So its integral is the difference of the two line integrals plus ±J(x′), and it equals the sum of dD over the cone Σ(x) from x′ over the loop, of area ≤ C(d)L².
    {#A.11.12-1-1} Averaging over x ∈ Y₁ gives J(x′) = ±avg_xΣ_{p∈Σ(x)}dD(p). A plaquette p at distance t(p) from x′ lies in Σ(x) for at most C(d)L^dmax(t(p), 1)^{2−d} of the x, so abs(J(x′)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p∈Q_{CL}(x′)}abs(dD(p))max(t(p), 1)^{2−d} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}‖dD‖_{Q_{CL}(x′)} for d = 4.
    {#A.11.12-2} At the scale j the same holds in #A.11.31 for the differences of V, the coarse crossing averages being means of scale-j means (PBG (3.15), p.393).

    {#A.11.13} *The field e.* It is built from the blocks of side L of Λ₀. For a free site x within L/8 of Λ₀ let {#D.m(x)} m(x) := max(dist(x, Λ₀), 1). For a block Y of Λ₀ within C(d)m(x) of x let c_Y(x) be the point of Y nearest x, moved by m(x)/4 towards the centre of Y, and B_Y(x) the ball of radius m(x)/8 about it, which lies in Y for d ≤ 4, its centre being at distance ≥ m(x)/(4√d) from the faces of Y. Put {#D.G^Y(x)} G^Y(x) := avg_u∫_{c_Y(x) + m(x)u/8}^{x}D, the average over u in the unit ball of the sums of D along the lattice paths within distance 1 of the segments.
    {#A.11.13-1} c_Y and m are Lipschitz, so {#D.D̃^Y} D̃^Y := D − ∂G^Y is on a bond (x, x + e_μ) an average of sums of dD over strips of width ≤ C(d) along the segments, and a plaquette p at distance t from x lies in the strips of a fraction ≤ C(d)max(t, 1)^{1−d} of the u. Hence abs(D̃^Y(x, x + e_μ)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p∈Q_{Cm(x)}(x)}abs(dD(p))max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d}.
    {#A.11.13-2} By Cauchy–Schwarz with Σ_{p∈Q_{Cm}(x)}max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d} ≤ C(d)m(x), and since Σ_{x: abs(x − p) ≤ Cm(x)}m(x)^{−1}max(abs(x − p), 1)^{1−d} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L), one unit per dyadic distance t ≥ m(p) at which m(x) ≍ t, ‖m^{−1}D̃^Y‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖², summed over the C(d) blocks Y used at each x.
    {#A.11.13-3} Let ψ be smooth, equal to 1 on [0, 1] and to 0 on [2, ∞), {#D.ψ_Y} ψ_Y := ψ(dist(·, Y)/m), and {#D.φ_Y} φ_Y := ψ_Y/Σ_{Y′}ψ_{Y′} on the free sites within L/8 of Λ₀. The nearest block has ψ_Y = 1, so Σ_Yφ_Y = 1, abs(∇φ_Y) ≤ C(d)/m, and dist(·, Y) ≤ 2m on supp φ_Y. At a free site x adjacent to Λ₀ put {#D.φ_Y(x)(x)} φ_{Y(x)}(x) := 1 and {#D.φ_Y(x)} φ_Y(x) := 0 for Y ≠ Y(x), Y(x) the block of the endpoint of x's bond in 𝒳; this keeps these properties.

    {#A.11.14} Put {#D.e} e := 0 on the data bonds, {#D.e(b)} e(b) := D(b) − G^{Y(x)}(x) on a crossing bond b into x, and {#D.e(b).2} e(b) := −χ_d(b)Σ_Y(G^Y − G^{Y₀})(b⁻)∂φ_Y(b) on the free bonds, Y₀ any block with ∂φ_{Y₀}(b) ≠ 0; the subtraction is allowed since Σ_Y∂φ_Y = 0.
    {#A.11.14-1} *The curl of e.* With {#D.Ψ} Ψ := Σ_Yφ_YG^Y on the free sites and {#D.Ψ.2} Ψ := 0 on Λ₀, the discrete product rule gives D = e + ∂Ψ + R where χ_d = 1, with {#D.R.4} R := Σ_Yφ_Y(b⁺)D̃^Y(b) on the free bonds and {#D.R.5} R := 0 on the others; on a crossing bond into x both sides are D, since Ψ(x) = G^{Y(x)}(x).
    {#A.11.14-2} On the free bonds e = χ_de₀, {#D.e₀} e₀ := −Σ_Y(G^Y − G^{Y₀})(b⁻)∂φ_Y(b), and on the plaquettes of free bonds de₀ = Σ_YD̃^Y ∧ ∂φ_Y, since Σ_Y∂φ_Y = 0. So abs(de) ≤ C(d)Σ_Yabs(D̃^Y)/m + C(d)L^{−1}abs(e₀) there, up to commutator terms of the same form. On the plaquettes meeting Λ₀, de = dD − dR, and R is there a sum of dD over C(d) plaquettes. So ‖de‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖² + C(d)‖ℓ^{−1}e₀‖², the last norm over the free bonds within L/16 of Λ₀, and the bounds below hold for e₀ and for e.
    {#A.11.14-3} *The size of e.* The terms of e₀ at x involve {#D.F_YY′(x)} F_{YY′}(x) := G^Y(x) − G^{Y′}(x) for blocks Y, Y′ within 2m(x) + 1 of x, and abs(e) ≤ C(d)m^{−1}Σabs(F_{YY′}) on the free bonds. The same holds on the crossing bonds with m = 1, up to sums of dD over C(d) plaquettes, since D(b) − G^{Y_b}(x) is such a sum for b into x from Y_b: at m(x) = 1, G^{Y_b}(x) averages sums of D along lattice paths of length ≤ C(d) from Y_b to x, D vanishes on the bonds of Y_b, and any lattice loop of length ≤ C(d) bounds ≤ C(d) plaquettes, whatever the choice of the paths.

    {#A.11.15} Two such blocks differ by Lv with v ∈ {−1, 0, 1}^d, since 4m(x) + 2 < L, and x lies within C(d)m(x) of the set S where they meet, of codimension k ≥ 1, the number of nonzero entries of v. (1) If Y and Y′ are joined by a chain of ≤ C(d) blocks of Λ₀ that meet S, consecutive ones sharing a face, F_{YY′}(x) is the average of the integrals of D around the loops x → y → y₁ → … → y′ → x, y ∈ B_Y(x), y′ ∈ B_{Y′}(x), and y_i in the balls of the chain, closed through the boxes formed by consecutive blocks, where D = 0.
    {#A.11.15-1} These integrals are sums of dD over ≤ C(d) triangles with a vertex at x and the other two in the balls, and a plaquette at distance t from x lies in the triangles for a fraction ≤ C(d)max(t, 1)^{2−d} of the points of the balls. So abs(F_{YY′}(x)) ≤ C(d)(Σ_{t ≤ Cm}t^{3−d})^{1/2}‖dD‖_{Q_{Cm}(x)} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}‖dD‖_{Q_{Cm}(x)} for d = 4.

    {#A.11.16} (2) Otherwise k ≥ 2, and the argument of (β) runs with the apex at x. A path Y, y₁, …, y_{k−1}, Y′ of blocks about S, consecutive ones sharing a face, gives k coarse constraints. Where a y_i lies in Λ₀, F_{YY′} = F_{Yy_i} + F_{y_iY′}, each of kind (1) or (2) with a shorter path, so let all y_i lie in Λ₁, where the constraints are those of Q.
    {#A.11.16-1} For x̂ ∈ Y, the loop from x̂ along the k lines of length L to x̂ + Lv, then by straight paths in Y′ to y′ ∈ B_{Y′}(x), along the segments y′ → x → y, y ∈ B_Y(x), and by a straight path in Y back to x̂, has D = 0 on its data bonds. Its integral is the sum of the k line integrals plus the integral along y′ → x → y. The line integrals average to the k vanishing constraints, so averaging over x̂, y, and y′ gives F_{YY′}(x) as an average of sums of dD over the cones from x over the loops, of area ≤ C(d)L².
    {#A.11.16-1-1} As for J, a plaquette at distance t from x lies in the cone for at most C(d)L^dmax(t, 1)^{2−d} of the x̂, so abs(F_{YY′}(x)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}‖dD‖_{Q_{CL}(x)} for d = 4.
    {#A.11.16-2} Summing, ‖ℓ^{−1}e‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)L^{−2}Σ_pabs(dD(p))²N(p) + C(d)‖dD‖², with {#D.N(p)} N(p) := Σm(x)^{−2} over the x for which p ∈ Q_{Cm}(x) in case (1), or p ∈ Q_{CL}(x) in case (2).
    {#A.11.16-3} In case (1), N(p) ≤ C(d)Σ_{t dyadic ≤ CL}t^dt^{−2} ≤ C(d)L^{d−2}. In case (2) the x lie within C(d)m of a set S of codimension k ≥ 2, with at most C(d)L^{d−k}m^k of them at the dyadic scale m within CL of p, so N(p) ≤ C(d)L^{d−k}Σ_{m dyadic ≤ L}m^{k−2} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)L^{d−2}. Hence ‖ℓ^{−1}e‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)²L^{d−4}‖dD‖² + C(d)‖dD‖², which for d = 4 with #A.11.14-2 gives ‖ℓ^{−1}e‖² + ‖de‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)²‖dD‖².

    {#A.11.17} For D ∈ ker Q, the two-layer gap (#0.1.31–#0.1.37.1, with F := Λ₀ and C := Ω₁, N_F being N(Q′)) gives λ′ ∈ N(Q′) with ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ′)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖, ℓ as in (c). D − ∂λ′ lies in the class of D, so ‖ℓ^{−1}D₁‖ ≤ ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ′)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖, which is the claim.

    {#A.11.18} {#K0.e} (e) Combes–Thomas in the multiscale metric. For a fixed site x₀ let {#D.f.5} f := e^{δρ_loc(x₀, ·)} or e^{−δρ_loc(x₀, ·)}, ρ_loc (#A.9.1-1) being the distance of the metric ds = dx/ℓ_ms of the full problem, and δ ≤ c(d)(1 + log L)^{−2}. Then abs(f(x) − f(x′)) ≤ C(d)δℓ^{−1}f(x) for neighbours, since ℓ ≤ ℓ_ms, and abs(f² − f(c)²) ≤ C(d)δf(c)² on the part of each Ω_c that enters Q((f − f(c))D)(c).
    {#A.11.18-1} On the coarser side Ω_c spans O(1) local units. At a coarse crossing bond c the block B(c₋) spans L local units of Λ₀, but D = 0 on its data bonds, so the lines of c carry D ≠ 0 only on the unit crossing bond and in B(c₊), and the variation of f across B(c₋) does not enter. Let D be the f-Landau representative of the minimising class of (c).

    {#A.11.19} (i) The gap for fD. Since QD = 0, the Q-defects of fD are Q(fD)(c) = Q((f − f(c))D)(c). Q has the weight ≤ ℓ^{1−d} on a bond (#A.8-1), so by #A.11.18 and Cauchy–Schwarz, abs(Q(fD)(c)) ≤ C(d)δℓ^{2−d/2}‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖_{Ω_c}. With the bumps β_c of #0.1.33.1, ‖ℓ^{−1}β_c‖ + ‖dβ_c‖ ≤ C(d)ℓ^{d/2−2} (#0.1.33-0.1), so with {#D.β^g} β^g := Σ_cQ(gD)(c)β_c for a weight g, β^f has ‖ℓ^{−1}β^f‖ + ‖dβ^f‖ ≤ C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖, and fD − β^f ∈ ker Q.
    {#A.11.19-1} Let D″ be the 1-Landau representative of the class of fD − β^f, so that fD − β^f = D″ + ∂μ with μ ∈ N(Q′), and put {#D.ν.4} ν := f^{−1}μ − Σ_yQ′(f^{−1}μ)(y)b_y ∈ N(Q′), with the bumps b_y of #A.9.1. Since Q′μ = 0, Q′(f^{−1}μ)(y) = Q′((f^{−1} − f(y)^{−1})μ)(y), so f∂ν = ∂μ + R with abs(R) ≤ C(d)δℓ^{−1}(abs(μ) + mean_yabs(μ)) on each block y. The per-block Poincaré bound on N(Q′) gives ‖ℓ^{−1}R‖ ≤ C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−2}μ‖ ≤ C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}∂μ‖.
    {#A.11.19-2} D − ∂ν lies in the class of D, so the minimality of D gives ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖ ≤ ‖ℓ^{−1}f(D − ∂ν)‖ = ‖ℓ^{−1}(D″ + β^f − R)‖. By (d), ‖ℓ^{−1}D″‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD″‖, with dD″ = d(fD) − dβ^f. With ‖ℓ^{−1}∂μ‖ ≤ ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖ + ‖ℓ^{−1}β^f‖ + ‖ℓ^{−1}D″‖, this gives ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖d(fD)‖ + C(d)δ(1 + log L)‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖, so ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖d(fD)‖ for δ ≤ c(d)(1 + log L)^{−1}.

    {#A.11.20} (ii) The test. {#D.T.3} T := f²D − β^{f²} ∈ ker Q, and ‖f^{−1}dβ^{f²}‖ ≤ C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖ as in (i). The commutators of d with f give ⟨dD, d(f²D)⟩ ≥ ‖d(fD)‖² − C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖‖d(fD)‖ − C(d)δ²‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖², and abs(⟨dD, dβ^{f²}⟩) ≤ C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖(‖d(fD)‖ + δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖). By (i), all error terms are ≤ C(d)δ(1 + log L)‖d(fD)‖², absorbed for δ ≤ c(d)(1 + log L)^{−1}.
    {#A.11.20-1} By #A.11.9-1, ⟨dD, dT⟩ = −ℓ_E(T) − ⟨dÃ′, dT⟩, which is bounded through #A.11.6-2 and ‖dT‖_y ≤ f(y)(‖d(fD)‖_{y⁺} + C(d)δ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖_{y⁺}). Hence, with (i), ‖d(fD)‖² + ‖ℓ^{−1}fD‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^8Σ_yf(y)²(S_y² + ‖dÃ′‖_y²), the sum over the blocks of all layers.
    {#A.11.20-2} Off the 2L-neighbourhood of 𝒰 the blocks lie in Λ₀ ∪ Λ₁, with the sources of (b)–(c), of the same size in the local units of both layers in d = 4; Λ₀ carries no unknowns. On that neighbourhood the sources are those of Ã′, over the blocks of side ℓ_ms, on each of which f varies by ≤ C(d)δ, bounded through ℳ in (f).
    {#A.11.20-3} The blocks of a finer layer whose sources are those of (b) (Λ₀) or are bounded through ℳ (the layers of 𝒰) are grouped into the cubes of the next coarser grid, those deeper than L included, and the weight is taken at its maximum on each cube. On these cubes the finer sources are bounded per cube, by the Morrey bounds of (b) on Λ₀ and through ℳ on the further layers, with the size of those of a coarser block in the local units in d = 4.
    {#A.11.20-4} So counted, the number of blocks at multiscale distance ≤ r is ≤ C(d)(1 + r)^d in each layer and ≤ C(d)(1 + r)^d(1 + r/RM) in all, each layer being ≥ RM wide in its own units.

VAR bounds it by PBG (3.133) (VAR p.297; its [5] is PBG, p.309).

A_N is least on A_N + ∂N(Q′) (#A.11.2-1), so A_N = H₀B − ∂ω_H with {#D.ω_H} ω_H := the element of N(Q′) least for ‖H₀B − ∂ω‖, the scalar problem of (f) with the source H₀B.

Then A_N = A_N^{(j)} + H₀(B − B^{(j)}) − ∂ω^f_j, and A_N^{(1)} = A_N.

    {#A.11.26} (s1) The propagator. With the factor (L^{j_x}η)^{−1} or (L^{j′}η)^{−1} of the variational normalisation (p.422 l.32–33), it gives that H₀B and its derivative at x ∈ Λ_{j_x} are, in the units of Λ_{j_x}, ≤ C(L)Σ_{y′}L^{abs(j_x − j′)}e^{−δ₁d(y, y′)/2}abs(B(y′)), each B(y′) in the units of its layer.
    {#A.11.26-1} Here d is the distance (2.46) of PRT2 (p.231), which PBG p.397 l.29 cites as "(2.36) in [4]". By (s1), abs(ηω_H(B^{(j)})) ≤ C(L)θ_B everywhere, and abs(ηω^f_j) ≤ C(L)θ_B everywhere and ≤ C(L)(e^{−δ₁RM/4} + e^{−δRM/32})θ_B on the blocks of Ω_j at distance ≥ RM/8 from Ω_j^c, whose multiscale distance to Ω_j^c is ≥ RM/8, since a path from Ω_{j+1} to Ω_j^c crosses Λ_j, which is > RM wide (PRT2 (2.2)).

    {#A.11.29} {#K0.g1} (1) The reduction. At the flat base Q_{j+1} = Q^{(1)}Q_j (PBG (3.15), p.393), so the constraints on Λ_j ∪ Λ_{j+1} are constraints on {#D.V} V := Q_jA: V = B on the bonds of the layer Λ_j ∖ Λ_{j+1}, Q^{(1)}V = B on Λ_{j+1}, and VAR's coarse crossing constraints (REG p.81), with no constraint on the scale-j bonds crossing into Λ_{j+1}; the crossing bonds at Λ_{j−1}/Λ_j carry the constraints of REG p.81, among the finer ones below.

H_j = GQ*(QGQ*)^{−1} (PRT1 (1.103), p.34), G and ∇G have kernels ≤ O(1)e^{−δ₀abs(y − y′)} between the cubes Δ̃(y), Δ̃(y′) of the scale-j lattice with O(1) and δ₀ depending on d only (PRT1 Proposition 1.2, (1.110), p.35), and QGQ* lies between two positive constants of d (p.34 l.27, (1.100)–(1.101)).
    {#A.11.29-0.2} Conjugation by e^{±δabs(· − y′)} changes the kernel of QGQ* by at most C(d)δabs(y − y″)e^{−(δ₀ − δ)abs(y − y″)}, an operator of norm ≤ C(d)δ for δ ≤ δ₀/2 by Schur's test. So for δ ≤ c(d) the conjugate stays ≥ c(d)/2, and (QGQ*)^{−1}(y, y′) ≤ C(d)e^{−δabs(y − y′)}. Hence H_j, dH_j, and Δ_j = H_j*d*dH_j have kernels ≤ C(d)e^{−δ_redabs(y − y′)}, with {#D.δ_red} δ_red := c(d).
    {#A.11.29-1} With {#D.V_N} V_N := Q_jA_N on all scale-j bonds, {#D.Z} Z := A_N − H_jV_N lies in ker Q_j, and ⟨dZ, dφ⟩ = 0 for every φ ∈ ker Q_j supported in Ω_j at distance ≥ 2√d from Ω_j^c, in the units of L^j: A_N + tφ satisfies the constraints of A_N, the coarser ones being constraints on V = Q_jA (PBG (3.15)) and the finer ones depending only on the fine bonds within distance 1 of Ω_j^c, whose points next to Ω_j lie in Λ_{j−1}, and Q_j(H_jV_N + tφ) = V_N, so both first variations vanish. Also ⟨dZ, dH_jD⟩ = 0 for every scale-j field D, since Q_j(H_jD + tZ) = D.
    {#A.11.29-2} For a scale-j bond c let {#D.b_c} b_c := the bump β_c of #0.1.33.1 at the scale j, read in the units of L^j, in which a field is S = L^j times its value in the fine units. Its construction uses only the averages Q_j at the flat base, so it applies to every scale-j bond, with B either block of c. Then Q_jb_c = δ_c, with Q_j normalised as in PRT1 (1.18) (p.20), abs(b_c) ≤ C(d) and abs(∂b_c) ≤ C(d) (#0.1.33.1-2), and b_c is supported in a block of c at distance ≥ 1/8 from its faces.

    {#A.11.30} As for 𝒫₁ in (c), the further constraints Q^{(1)}V = Q_{j+1}A_N on the scale-(j + 1) bonds with an endpoint in Ω_{j+2}, the crossing bonds from Λ_{j+1} included, give a two-layer problem for V, with the layers Λ_j and Ω_{j+1}, at whose minimum V_N lies up to an exponentially small source. For a variation D of V, supported on the bonds of Ω_{j+1} and its crossing bonds, ⟨V_N, Δ_jD⟩ = ⟨dH_jV_N, dH_jD⟩ = ⟨dA_N, dH_jD⟩ (#A.11.29-1), and ⟨dA_N, dH_jD⟩ = ⟨dA_N, dc_D⟩ with {#D.c_D} c_D := (1 − χ)H_jD + Σ_c(Q_j(χH_jD)(c) − D(c))b_c, χ a cutoff equal to 1 at distance ≥ 3√d from Ω_j^c and 0 within 2√d of it.
    {#A.11.30-0.1} Indeed Q_jc_D = 0, so Q_j(H_jD − c_D) = D, and H_jD − c_D vanishes within √d of Ω_j^c: D = 0 on the cubes c near Ω_j^c, a term b_c has Q_j(χH_jD)(c) ≠ 0 only if a path of c reaches distance 2√d from Ω_j^c, and supp b_c lies within (7/8)√d of each path of c, being in a block of c at distance ≥ 1/8 from its faces (#A.11.29-2). So A_N is stationary along H_jD − c_D (#A.11.29-1). Also abs(c_D) and abs(dc_D) are ≤ C(d)Σ_{y′}e^{−δ_redabs(· − y′)}abs(D(y′)), where abs(· − y′) ≥ RM − 4√d, and c_D ≠ 0 only on Ω_j^c and within 3√d + (7/8)√d ≤ 4√d of it.
    {#A.11.30-1} Its gauge group {#D.N_V} N_V := {λ′: λ′ = 0 at the scale-j sites of Λ_j and off Ω_j, Q′^{(1)}λ′ = 0 at the blocks of Ω_{j+1}} leaves ⟨V, Δ_jV⟩ and the constraints unchanged, and V_L denotes the least element of V_N + ∂₁N_V in ℓ² of the scale-j lattice: Q^{(1)}V_L = Q^{(1)}V_N on Ω_{j+1}, and ∂₁*V_L lies in the range of Q′^{(1)*}, constant on the blocks of Ω_{j+1}.
    {#A.11.30-2} On the union of the blocks Ω_c of these bonds its data is extended by V_N, with the source ⟨σ̃∂₁V_N, ∂₁D⟩ = ⟨dH_jV_N, dH_jD⟩ (#A.11.36), dH_jV_N = dA_N − dZ_j with dZ_j of #A.11.46, and ‖V_N‖_y ≤ C(d)‖A_N‖_{y⁺} by Cauchy–Schwarz on the averages of Q_j, so ℳ of (f) and (s3) bound it. So the interface Λ_j/Λ_{j+1} is the problem 𝒫₁ of (a)–(f) on the scale-j lattice, with ⟨V, Δ_jV⟩ in place of ‖dA‖², V = B on the layer as the data, V_L in place of A_N, and N_V in place of N(Q′).

    {#A.11.31} {#K0.g2} (2) The transfer. Δ_j∂₁ = 0 and γ₀‖∂₁V‖² ≤ ⟨V, Δ_jV⟩ ≤ γ₁‖∂₁V‖² (PRT1 (1.67), p.29).

    {#A.11.32} (c) holds with ⟨D, Δ_jD⟩ in place of ‖dD‖² and ⟨σ̃∂₁Ã′, ∂₁D⟩ (σ̃ of #A.11.36) in place of ⟨dÃ′, dD⟩ in Φ, and (d) concerns only the gauge group and ‖∂₁D‖, so both hold with γ₀ and γ₁. In (e) the weights are e^{±δρ_j}, with {#D.ρ_j} ρ_j := the distance of ds = dx/max(ℓ_ms, 1) in the units of L^j. On paths in Ω_j, where ℓ_ms ≥ 1, it is the multiscale length, and everywhere abs(ρ_j(y) − ρ_j(y′)) ≤ abs(y − y′).
    {#A.11.32-0.1} For x ∈ Λ_j, ρ_j(x, Ω_j^c) ≥ min(dist(x, Ω_j^c), RM), since a path from Ω_{j+1} to Ω_j^c crosses Λ_j, which is > RM wide (PRT2 (2.2)); so for x, z ∈ Ω_j, ρ_j(x, z) ≥ min(ρ_loc(x, z), ρ_j(x, Ω_j^c)), and ρ_j is, up to O(1), the distance (2.46) of PRT2 for the layers Λ_{j″}, j″ < j, merged into one layer of the scale j, for which the count of #A.11.20-4 and PRT2 (2.58) hold.
    {#A.11.32-0.2} The commutators of Δ_j with {#D.f.32} f := e^{±δρ_j} are O(δ) for δ ≤ c(d)δ_red. The commutator [σ̃, f] acts on the curvatures and is O(δ) by the decay of σ̃'s kernel and the geometry of #A.11.32-1, and the crossing unit bonds in the Q-defects are read in the same way.
