    {#A.11.33} (f) holds for V_L, whose minimality on V_N + ∂₁N_V is the scalar problem on N_V, with the per-block Poincaré bound on the blocks of Ω_{j+1}, and the hole-filling of #0.1 is written for Δ_j (step (1)).

    {#A.11.34} (b) holds with the extension of (3) in place of E_f.

    {#A.11.35} {#K0.g3} (3) The fine data for Δ_j. Let f be a face of the layer toward Λ_{j+1}, H₋ the closed half-space of f's plane on the side of the layer, H₊ the other one, s the depth from the plane, and {#D.V_f} V_f := V on the bonds of H₋ in the layer and 0 on the other bonds of H₋, so abs(V_f) ≤ θ_B. Here f's plane and H_± are those of ℤ^d, and the layer is lifted from the torus to a window of ℤ^d about f, so that V_f has finite support.
    {#A.11.35-0.1} For N_w ≥ 1 let Q_{N_w} be the cube of side 2N_w (the convention of Q_r) about a fixed point of f's plane, and c^{N_w} the minimiser of ⟨V_f + c, Δ_j(V_f + c)⟩ over the c vanishing on H₋ and outside Q_{N_w} (the class of N_w).
    {#A.11.35-1} Its curvature {#D.F^N} F^{N_w} := ∂₁(V_f + c^{N_w}) is unique. The claim is abs(F^{N_w}(x)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1) at the points x of H₊ within N_w^{1/2} of the centre of Q_{N_w}. Then a subsequence of the c^{N_w} in the axial gauge from the plane converges pointwise as N_w → ∞ to some c_f.
    {#A.11.35-2} {#D.E^σ_f} E^σ_f := V_f + c_f solves ⟨σ̃∂₁E^σ_f, ∂₁w⟩ = 0 for every w of finite support vanishing on H₋ (σ̃ of #A.11.36): the equation of c^{N_w} passes to the limit, since F^{N_w} converges pointwise within N_w^{1/2} of the centre and σ̃'s kernel from supp w to the plaquettes beyond is ≤ C(d)e^{−c(d)N_w^{1/2}}, against ‖F^{N_w}‖² ≤ γ₀^{−1}γ₁‖∂₁V_f‖², which is finite in the finite volume and uniform in N_w. So {#D.F_f.2} F_f := ∂₁E^σ_f obeys the claim on all of H₊, and abs(E^σ_f) ≤ C(d)θ_B(1 + log max(s, 1)) in this gauge.

    {#A.11.36} (i) The local flux. For a 2-form F and a plaquette p of the fine lattice in the block x̄, let {#D.M̃F(p)} M̃F(p) := (dH_jK_{x̄}F)(p), K_{x̄}F the potential of F along the coordinate paths from the centre of x̄, averaged over the d! orders of the coordinates. If F = ∂₁V, K_{x̄}F − V is a gradient, which dH_j annihilates (the minimum of ‖dA‖² under Q_jA = ∂₁λ is 0), so M̃∂₁V = dH_jV.
    {#A.11.36-1} K_{x̄}F at a bond at distance r from x̄ is a sum of F over ≤ C(d)r² plaquettes within r of x̄, so M̃ has kernel ≤ C(d)e^{−δ_redabs(p − p′)/2}, and it commutes with the translations and the reflections of the scale-j lattice. So Δ_j = ∂₁*σ̃∂₁ with {#D.σ̃} σ̃ := M̃*M̃, whose kernel is ≤ C(d)e^{−δ_redabs(p − p′)/4}, and ⟨F, σ̃F⟩ ≥ γ₀‖F‖² for closed F by PRT1 (1.65) and (1.67).

    {#A.11.37} (ii) Interior regularity. If Δ_ju = 0 on the bonds of Q_r(x), then abs(∂₁u(x))² ≤ C(d)r^{−d}‖∂₁u‖²_{Q_r(x)} + C(d)e^{−δ_redr/C(d)}‖∂₁u‖². Let u′ be the axial potential of ∂₁u in Q_r(x) from one of its faces, so ‖u′‖_{Q_r(x)} ≤ C(d)r‖∂₁u‖_{Q_r(x)}, μ the minimiser of ‖u′ − ∂μ‖_{Q_r(x)} vanishing off Q_r(x), and {#D.ũ} ũ := u′ − ∂μ, so ∂*ũ = 0 at the sites of Q_r(x) and ‖ũ‖ ≤ ‖u′‖. For a cutoff η in Q_{r/2}(x), ηũ has compact support, and on Z^d ‖∇(ηũ)‖² = ‖∂(ηũ)‖² + ‖∂*(ηũ)‖² (in Fourier Σ_{μν}∂_μv_ν\overline{∂_νv_μ} = abs(∂*v)², the differences commuting). So ‖D_μũ‖_{Q_{r/4}(x)} ≤ C(d)‖∂₁u‖_{Q_r(x)}.
    {#A.11.37-1} The differences D_μ commute with Δ_j, and D_μũ is a representative of D_μu, so the Caccioppoli bound of #0.1.21, whose proof uses only the identity ⟨η²w, Δ_jw⟩ = ⟨ηw, Δ_jηw⟩ + ½Σw(b)Δ_j(b, b′)w(b′)(η(b) − η(b′))² of a symmetric kernel and the decay of the kernel, gives ‖∂₁D_μu‖²_{Q_{r/8}(x)} ≤ C(d)r^{−2}‖∂₁u‖²_{Q_r(x)}. The representatives are joined outside Q_r(x) to the axial one, whose values grow at most linearly, so the tails are ≤ C(d)e^{−δ_redr/C(d)}‖∂₁u‖². Iterating d times and using the discrete Sobolev bound on Q_{r/C(d)}(x) gives the claim.

    {#A.11.38} (iii) The wall. Let z lie in the plane, u vanish on H₋, and Δ_ju = 0 on the bonds of H₊ ∩ Q_R(z). Then E_u(Q_r(z)) ≤ C(d)(r/R)^dE_u(Q_R(z)) + C(d)e^{−δ_redR/C(d)}E_u for 1 ≤ r ≤ R/C(d), with {#D.E_u(Q)} E_u(Q) := ‖∂₁u‖²_Q and E_u the total.
    {#A.11.38-1} (A) The steps of (ii) run with the tangential differences D_τ, which commute with Δ_j and keep u = 0 on H₋. For the gauge, R is the reflection in the plane and {#D.ū} ū := u − R*u, which is odd, with ‖∂₁ū‖² = 2‖∂₁u‖² on R-symmetric cubes, and ∂₁ū vanishes on the plaquettes of the plane. The axial potential ū′ of ∂₁ū on the symmetric cube with zero normal components and zero tangential components on the plane is unique, so it is odd, −R*ū′ being another one, and ‖ū′‖ ≤ C(d)R‖∂₁ū‖ by Cauchy–Schwarz along the normal lines.
    {#A.11.38-2} Then ū − ū′ = ∂g with g odd after adding a constant. The Coulomb μ of ū′ on the symmetric cube, as in (ii), is odd, the problem commuting with R; with ũ := ū′ − ∂μ, g = μ = 0 on the plane and ‖ũ‖ ≤ ‖ū′‖. With {#D.λ.2} λ := g + μ on H₊ and 0 on H₋, u − ∂λ vanishes on H₋ and equals ũ on H₊. So ‖D^α_tanF‖²_{Q_{R/4}(z)} ≤ C(d)R^{−2abs(α)}E_u(Q_R(z)) + C(d)e^{−δ_redR/C(d)}E_u for abs(α) ≤ d + 1, {#D.F.2} F := ∂₁u.
    {#A.11.38-3} Let N₁(s)² be the sum of R^{2abs(α)−(d−1)}‖D^α_tanD_τF(·, s)‖² over the slice at depth s within R/4 of z, over τ, and over abs(α) ≤ d. By the Sobolev bound on the slices, sup_yabs(D_τF(y, s)) ≤ C(d)N₁(s) for the y within 3R/16 of z, and Σ_{s≤R/4}N₁(s)² ≤ C(d)R^{−(d+1)}E_u(Q_R(z)) + tails by (A).
    {#A.11.38-4} (B) {#D.G} G := σ̃F has ∂₁*G = 0 at the bonds of H₊ ∩ Q_R(z). At the tangential bond at (y, s), s ≥ 1, in the direction τ this reads G_{nτ}(y, s) − G_{nτ}(y, s − 1) = Σ_{τ′}(D*_{τ′}G_{τ′τ})(y, s) up to signs, the normal plaquettes being indexed by their lower depth.

    {#A.11.39} For each depth s₀ let {#D.Ñ₁(s₀)} Ñ₁(s₀) := Σ_{s′}e^{−c(d)abs(s₀ − s′)}N₁(s′). For y within R/8 of z, the right side of (B) and the tangential differences of G_{nτ}(·, s₀) are σ̃ applied to tangential differences of F, so by #A.11.38-3 and the decay of σ̃ (#A.11.36) they are ≤ C(d)Ñ₁(s₀) + tails, the plaquettes beyond R/16 of y entering through the tails.
    {#A.11.39-0.1} Choose s₀ ≤ R/16 with Ñ₁(s₀) ≤ (16/R)Σ_{s≤R/16}Ñ₁(s). Then the oscillation of G_{nτ}(·, s₀) over Q_{R/8}(z) is ≤ C(d)RÑ₁(s₀) + tails, and (B) summed between the depths s₀ and s ≤ R/8 adds ≤ C(d)Σ_{s″≤R/8}Ñ₁(s″) + tails. Both are ≤ C(d)Σ_{s′≤R/4}N₁(s′) + tails, the slices s′ > R/4 entering with weights ≤ C(d)e^{−c(d)R/8}.
    {#A.11.39-0.2} Let ḡ_τ be the mean of G_{nτ} over H₊ ∩ Q_{R/8}(z). Since Σ_{s′≤R/4}N₁(s′) ≤ (R/4)^{1/2}(Σ_{s′≤R/4}N₁(s′)²)^{1/2} ≤ C(d)R^{−d/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} + tails by #A.11.38-3, abs(G_{nτ}(y, s) − ḡ_τ) ≤ C(d)R^{−d/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} + tails for s ≤ R/8 and y within R/8 of z. Also abs(ḡ_τ) ≤ C(d)R^{−d/2}‖G‖_{Q_{R/8}(z)} ≤ C(d)R^{−d/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} + tails.
    {#A.11.39-1} F_{ττ′} = 0 on the plane and dF = 0 give abs(F_{ττ′}(y, s)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{s′<s}N₁(s′) for y within R/8 of z. On the normal line through y, G_{nτ}(y, s) = Σ_tk(s − t)F_{nτ}(y, t) + e(y, s). Here k(s) is the kernel of σ̃ from the type nτ to itself summed over the tangential translations. The tangentially constant parts from the types nτ′, τ′ ≠ τ, cancel under the reflection y_τ ↦ −y_τ. And e collects the tangential differences of F_{n·} and the components F_{ττ′}, so abs(e(y, s)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{s′}e^{−δ_redabs(s − s′)/C(d)}Σ_{s″≤s′}N₁(s″) + tails. F_{nτ}(y, t) = 0 for t < 0.
    {#A.11.39-2} The matrix k(s − t), s, t ≥ 0, is ≥ γ₀: a tangentially constant F with the components F_{nτ}(t) alone is closed, and the bound ⟨F, σ̃F⟩ ≥ γ₀‖F‖² on the closed fields holds for the symbol of the translation-invariant σ̃ on the kernel of d̂(k) at every momentum k ≠ 0, in particular at k = (0, k_n). Its entries decay exponentially, so on [0, R/8] its inverse has kernel ≤ (2/γ₀)e^{−c(d)abs(s − t)} by the conjugation argument of #A.11.29-0.2.
    {#A.11.39-3} The values F_{nτ}(y, t), t > R/8, that the truncation moves to the right side enter through k(s − t) and are ≤ C(d)t^{−d/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} for t ≤ R/4 by (ii), with tails beyond. Inverting k on [0, R/8], with G bounded by #A.11.39-0.2 and the sums Σ_{s″≤s′}N₁(s″) in e bounded as there, gives abs(F_{nτ}(y, s)) ≤ C(d)R^{−d/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} + tails for s ≤ R/8 and y within R/8 of z, and #A.11.39-1 with #A.11.38-3 gives abs(F_{ττ′}(y, s)) ≤ C(d)s^{1/2}R^{−(d+1)/2}E_u(Q_R(z))^{1/2} + tails.
    {#A.11.39-4} Summing over Q_r(z), r ≤ R/8, gives E_u(Q_r(z)) ≤ C(d)(r^dR^{−d} + r^{d+1}R^{−(d+1)})E_u(Q_R(z)) + tails ≤ C(d)(r/R)^dE_u(Q_R(z)) + tails.

    {#A.11.40} (iv) The bound. Let x lie within N_w^{1/2} of the centre of Q_{N_w} at depth s, ξ be a unit vector, and w_x the minimiser of ⟨w, Δ_jw⟩ − 2ξ·∂₁w(x) over the class of N_w. The equations of c^{N_w} and w_x, tested against each other, give ξ·∂₁c^{N_w}(x) = −⟨h, ∂₁w_x⟩, with {#D.h.2} h := σ̃∂₁V_f on the plaquettes meeting H₊, so abs(h(p)) ≤ C(d)θ_Be^{−δ_reds(p)/8}, summing the kernel of σ̃ over the plaquettes of H₋ at distance ≥ s(p), and ‖∂₁w_x‖ ≤ γ₀^{−1}.
    {#A.11.40-1} For g supported outside Q_r(x), the same identity gives ⟨g, ∂₁w_x⟩ = ξ·∂₁v_g(x), with v_g the response to g, ‖∂₁v_g‖ ≤ γ₀^{−1}‖g‖, and Δ_jv_g = 0 on the bonds of H₊ ∩ Q_{r−1}(x). For r ≤ C(d)s, (ii) at the scale min(r, s)/2 gives abs(∂₁v_g(x)) ≤ C(d)r^{−d/2}‖g‖. For r > C(d)s, the same follows from (iii) at the foot z of x with R = r/2, applied to Q_{3s/2}(z) after (ii) at the scale s/2 if s ≥ C(d), and to Q_{C(d)}(z), which contains the plaquettes at x, if s < C(d). Taking g := ∂₁w_x off Q_r(x) gives ‖∂₁w_x‖²_{H₊∖Q_r(x)} ≤ C(d)r^{−d}.
    {#A.11.40-2} For z′ in the plane with abs(z′ − z) ≤ N_w/4 and {#D.R′.3} R′ := max(abs(z′ − z), s)/2, w_x is Δ_j-harmonic on H₊ ∩ Q_{R′}(z′), and ‖∂₁w_x‖²_{Q_{R′}(z′)} ≤ C(d)R′^{−d} by the exterior bound, so (iii) gives ‖∂₁w_x‖²_{Q_{t+1}(z′)} ≤ C(d)(t + 1)^dR′^{−2d} for t + 1 ≤ R′/C(d). Summing with the weights e^{−δ_redt/8} over the depths t and over z′, the rest being bounded through ‖∂₁w_x‖ ≤ γ₀^{−1} and the exterior bound, gives Σ_pabs(h(p))abs(∂₁w_x(p)) ≤ C(d)θ_B(Σ_{z′}max(abs(z′ − z), s)^{−d} + N_w^{−1/2}) ≤ C(d)θ_B/s for s ≥ C(d), since s ≤ N_w^{1/2}.
    {#A.11.40-3} For s < C(d), the same sum with C(d) in place of s gives C(d)θ_B, the z′ with abs(z′ − z) ≤ C(d) entering through ‖∂₁w_x‖ ≤ γ₀^{−1} on their C(d) plaquettes, where abs(h) ≤ C(d)θ_B. Since F^{N_w}(x) − ∂₁c^{N_w}(x) = ∂₁V_f(x) is ≤ 4θ_B and vanishes at depth ≥ 1, the claim holds.

    {#A.11.41} {#K0.g4} (4) The patching. {#D.E.7} E := V on the data bonds and {#D.E.8} E := χ_dΣ_fχ_fE^σ_f on the free bonds, with χ_f, χ_d, and T̂_f of (b) in the units of L^j. χ_f = 0 on the free bonds of H₋(f) and on the data bonds off f's closure, and T̂_f = 0 on the data bonds of f's closure, so χ_fT̂_f vanishes on H₋(f), and ⟨σ̃∂₁E^σ_f, ∂₁(χ_dχ_fT̂_f)⟩ = 0.
    {#A.11.41-1} So {#D.ℓ_E(T).2} ℓ_E(T) := ⟨σ̃∂₁E, ∂₁T⟩ consists of the terms of (b) with σ̃ inserted, the commutators [σ̃, χ_f] and [σ̃, χ_d], whose kernels are ≤ C(d)e^{−δ_redabs(p − p′)/8}abs(p − p′)sup abs(∇χ), and the parts of σ̃ that reach from supp χ_f into H₋(f) off the layer or into the data off H₋(f).
    {#A.11.41-2} These parts lie at distance ≥ min(r, L/8)/(6√d) from the points of supp χ_f at distance r from the strata, by the property of supp χ_f in (b) with the layer for Λ₀, so they are ≤ C(d)θ_Be^{−c(d)δ_redmin(r, L)} ≤ C(d)θ_B/min(max(r, 1), L)², a source of the form of S_y and of Morrey exponent d − 2. So the bounds of (b) hold: abs(E) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B, coarse data of the residual ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)Lθ_B, and the same S_y and S(Q_r).

    {#A.11.42} {#K0.g5} (5) The weight. Let W_j be W of #0.1.18-4-1 in the units of L^j, with t the distance to the faces, edges, and vertices of Λ_{j+1} at the interface Λ_j/Λ_{j+1}, and t₃ the distance to the contacts of codimension ≥ 2, lying in ∂Λ_{j+1}, between the local components of the layer Λ_j ∖ Λ_{j+1}; the pinches of Ω_j next to Λ_{j−1}, which lie outside R_j (#A.11.48), are not counted. Both are capped as in #0.1.18-4. Let {#D.W₀} W₀ := W and {#D.W_ms} W_ms := max_jW_j.
    {#A.11.42-0.1} Each layer is ≥ RM ≥ 2L wide in its own units, so W_j = (1 + log L)^p beyond distance L of the interface Λ_j/Λ_{j+1}, and at each site at most one W_j exceeds (1 + log L)^p.
    {#A.11.42-0.2} The blocks of Λ_{j+1} are centred on the scale-(j + 1) lattice, so the coordinate planes through the centres of its blocks lie at distance ≥ L/2 − ½ from the faces of Λ_{j+1} (as in #0.1.19-1), and the blocks of the scales ≥ j + 2 lie in Ω_{j+2}, at distance ≥ RML from the interface in the units of L^j, where W_j = (1 + log L)^p.
    {#A.11.42-0.3} So the averages of W_j over the blocks of the scales ≥ j + 1 and these planes are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p as for W. On a block y of a layer Λ_i only W_{i−1} and W_i can exceed (1 + log L)^p, y being of a scale ≥ (i − 1) + 1; so the averages of W_ms over y and the coordinate planes through its centre are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p, unless y lies within L of Λ_{i+1} in the units of L^i, where y carries the scale-i data, which the chain reads in supremum only (#A.11.43).
    {#A.11.42-1} W_ms ≤ (1 + log L)^pL, t and t₃ being ≥ ρ₀. (KW) at Λ_j/Λ_{j+1} is run for V_L, with ∂₁*V_L constant on the blocks of Λ_{j+1} ((1)) and the ℓ² bounds of #A.11.48, and gives ‖V_L‖_{W_j} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^pC_H^{reg}θ_B, in the units of the layer, at the points x̄ with Q_{48L}(x̄) ⊂ R_j, which include the points within RM/16 of supp χ_j (#A.11.49).
    {#A.11.42-2} W_j(y′) ≤ (1 + abs(y − y′)/ρ₀)W_j(y), since t and t₃ are 1-Lipschitz and ≥ ρ₀ ≥ 1, so the kernels ≤ C(d)e^{−c(d)abs(y − y′)} of #A.11.45 and #A.11.47 preserve the weight up to C(d). On B, λ = g + ψ′, with g harmonic in B and equal to λ on ∂B, and {#D.ψ′} ψ′ := Σ_{y∈B}G_B(·, y)σ(y)/(2d), so that Δψ′ = −σ in B and ψ′ = 0 on ∂B (𝓛G_B(·, y) = −δ_y in B, Δ = 2d𝓛, #A.10).
    {#A.17-3} Lawler–Limic Theorem 6.3.8(a) ((6.17), p.131, for n = t/4 above the threshold of d) applied to g − λ(w), w ∈ ∂B, with ‖g − λ(w)‖_∞ ≤ osc_{∂B}λ by the maximum principle, gives abs(∇g(x)) ≤ C(d)t^{−1}osc_{∂B}λ. By Proposition 4.6.2(a) (p.97), G_B(·, y) = G(· − y) − h_y with {#D.h_y} h_y := E^·G(S_{τ_B} − y), τ_B the exit time from B. Theorem 4.3.1 (p.81), G(x) = C_dabs(x)^{2−d} + O(abs(x)^{−d}), gives abs(∇G(x − y)) ≤ C(d)max(abs(x − y), 1)^{1−d}, so Σ_{y∈B}abs(∇G(x − y)) ≤ C(d)t.
    {#A.17-4} h_y is harmonic in B, and for x′ ∈ 𝒞_{t/16}(x), h_y(x′) = Σ_{w∈∂B}H_B(x′, w)G(w − y) ≤ C(d)t^{1−d}Σ_{w∈∂B}abs(w − y)^{2−d} by Lemma 6.3.7 and Theorem 4.3.1. As ∂B has ≤ C(d)k^{d−1} sites within distance k of y, the sum is ≤ C(d)t, so h_y ≤ C(d)t^{2−d} on 𝒞_{t/16}(x), and Theorem 6.3.8(a) on 𝒞_{t/20}(x) gives abs(∇h_y(x)) ≤ C(d)t^{1−d}. Summing over the ≤ C(d)t^d sites of B, abs(∇ψ′(x)) ≤ C(d)t sup abs(σ). Hence abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ C(d)(t^{−1}osc_{∂B}λ + t sup abs(σ)), with ∂B ⊂ Q_{2t}(z) when t < L and ∂B ⊂ Q_L(x) when t = L, and t sup abs(σ) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}θ by (K1).
    {#A.17-5} If t = L, abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}θ ≤ C(d)W(x)θ. Let 4ρ₀ ≤ t < L, and r₀ that of (K5) at z. If r₀ ≥ 2t, there is an r_m ∈ [2t, 2Kt], and (K5), with a₀ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}Lθ and (r_m/r₀)^μ ≤ C(d)(t/t₃(z))^μ, gives osc_{Q_{2t}(z)}λ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}(t/t₃(z))^μLθ. As t₃ ≤ t₃(z) + t + √d ≤ 2t₃(z) and 1 − μ = κ, abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}(L/t)^κ(L/t₃)^{1−κ}θ ≤ C(d)W(x)θ. If r₀ < 2t, then t₃ ≤ t₃(z) + t + √d ≤ C(d)t, so W(x) ≥ c(d)(1 + log L)^pL/t, and abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}(L/t)θ ≤ C(d)W(x)θ.
    {#A.17-6} Let now t < 4ρ₀, so z exists and both endpoints of b lie in Q_{8ρ₀}(z). If r₀ ≥ 8ρ₀, (K5) at an r_m ∈ [8ρ₀, 8Kρ₀] gives abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ osc_{Q_{8ρ₀}(z)}λ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}(ρ₀/t₃(z))^μLθ = C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}ρ₀(L/ρ₀)^{1−μ}(L/t₃(z))^μθ, and with L/ρ₀ ≤ 4L/t, t₃ ≤ t₃(z) + 4ρ₀ + √d ≤ 2t₃(z), and ρ₀ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L), this is ≤ C(d)W(x)θ. If r₀ < 8ρ₀, then t₃ ≤ C(d)ρ₀, so W(x) ≥ c(d)(1 + log L)^pL/ρ₀ ≥ c(d)(1 + log L)^{p−1}L, and abs(∂λ(b)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ+2}Lθ ≤ C(d)W(x)θ, as p − 1 = p_θ + 2.
    {#A.17-7} On the bonds at x̄ that are neither data bonds nor mass bonds, A = v_{x̄} + w_{x̄} + ∂λ, with abs(v_{x̄}) ≤ C(d)W(x̄)θ and abs(w_{x̄}) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p_θ}θ by the bounds of #A.13 and the comparison above. Hence abs(A) ≤ C(d)W(x̄)θ = C(d)W(x̄)C_H^{reg}θ_B on the bonds at x̄.
